cases.attribution_rationale:
Premise confirmed by inspection. photo_004.jpg is a narrow galley kitchen whose right-hand and hall walls are visibly blotchy and unevenly toned, with patched/skim-coated areas, scuffing, and an unfinished jamb at the right doorway — walls that genuinely need prep and repainting. But there is no peeling, flaking, or bubbling paint film anywhere in the frame. So a real problem was billed (work warranted) under a name asserting a defect class that is not present (claim misnamed) — the appendix_misnamed premise holds.

The 2a prose contained the correct reading and only the correct reading: "Walls/paint need attention. Visible scuffs, patchy areas, and generally tired finishes suggest prep, repair, and repainting throughout." It named scuffs, patchiness, tiredness, and a repaint need. It did NOT contain "peeling", "bubbling", "flaking", or "discolored paint" — the words that define the item eventually billed. 2a therefore read the photo correctly and is not responsible.

2b faithfully restated that one prose line as two bullets — "Walls have visible scuffs and patchy areas." and "Wall finishes appear tired." — the second being 2a's own "tired finishes" wording. Vaguer, but not a distortion, and the specifics survived in the sibling bullet. 2c kept both (this issue joined exact, p2c_present true), so neither 2b nor 2c introduced or lost the correct meaning; the correctly-named reading was still on the table at 2d, and in fact the sibling issue 42b2b7251c492439 resolved to wall_scuffs_marks_or_dents.

2d is the first stage that went wrong. With 7 candidates and resolution_path "llm", it mapped "Wall finishes appear tired." onto peeling_or_discolored_paint, whose claim text is "interior paint peeling, bubbling, or visibly aged finish" — importing a paint-failure mechanism that neither the prose nor the pixels support, when a scuff/dent/tired-finish item matched what was actually observed. Everything after 2d inherits that name: 2e kept it (removed_count 0), projection produced oc1_f46cc039d3163f19, and Terra supported it by leaning on the "visibly aged finish" clause ("visibly aged, uneven areas and patchy discoloration"), which is true of the wall but is not the peeling/bubbling defect the item is named for. Disposition accepted_for_work, so this is a billed misnamed claim, not the post-Terra routing gap.

Premise holds. photo_032.jpg is a cramped half-bath (toilet, small white vanity with a hanging/misaligned door, medicine cabinet, vinyl-plank floor, doorway to carpet at right). Every intermediate rung is clean. 2b produced the matching bullet verbatim (index 15, exact join). 2c kept it (it is in p2c_surviving as issue ee846d364a0b6a80, not in p2c_dropped). 2d resolved it to baseboard_wear_scuffs via exact_kind routing — and since the human graded the resulting claim axis "exact", that catalog item is a correct fit, so 2d did not mis-resolve. 2e kept the issue (p2e_status "kept", id present in kept_issue_ids), and per the case framing 2e cost nothing here anyway. condition_projection produced oc1_b10d0b1346b9e17a, so the condition existed and reached Terra.

cases.attribution_rationale:
Premise holds. photo_014.jpg is a staged dining room whose walls are a uniform, clean pale butter-yellow. The paint film is intact: no peeling, no bubbling, no flaking at corners or baseboard, no patchy nicotine-style discoloration or aged/uneven finish. The yellow is plainly a deliberate (if dated) color choice, not deterioration. So the billed claim "interior paint peeling, bubbling, or visibly aged finish" (accepted_for_work, degradation) is unsupported, matching the adjudicated v1.1 axes (claim absent / work none).

What the 2a prose DID contain: a single mention of the walls, "yellowed wall color", placed inside the list headed "Dated finishes are the main opportunity" alongside "old light fixture, ornate mirror, ceiling treatment" — all style/vintage items, framed as things that "can be transformed relatively quickly." Read in that context it is a dated-palette observation about the wall's hue, which the photo genuinely supports. The prose also carries one hedged condition remark, "likely aging paint/trim," which 2b captured as its own bullet ("Paint and trim are likely aging.") and 2c DROPPED — it is not this condition's lineage.

What the 2a prose did NOT contain: any assertion of peeling, bubbling, flaking, damaged or visibly degraded paint. Its overall reading is "good bones, cosmetic upside," and where it does flag condition (floor wear) it says "nothing obviously alarming from the photo." So the material false claim does not already appear at 2a, which rules out pass_2a.

2b joined exactly ("Wall color is yellowed.", bullet_index 5, method exact) and preserved the color reading verbatim; 2c kept that bullet — keeping a true observation is not the error. The meaning flips at 2d: resolution chose peeling_or_discolored_paint from 6 candidates via the llm path, an item whose claim template asserts "interior paint peeling, bubbling, or visibly aged finish." That is the first stage where a true dated-color observation became a false paint-degradation defect; note its sibling from the same 2a sentence ("The light fixture is old.") correctly landed as modernization. condition_projection only instantiated the catalog item's claim text, and Terra then rubber-stamped it with its own invented detail ("visibly uneven, discolored areas"), but both are downstream of the wrong-item resolution. 2e is not available (issue is in kept_issue_ids and produced a condition regardless).

Confidence is medium, not high, for two reasons: (a) "yellowed" can be read as age-discoloration rather than hue, which would push the error up to 2a — I resolved it toward hue because of the "Dated finishes" framing and the style-item company it keeps; (b) the p2c_surviving entry already carries kind "degradation", and 2d's routing_reason is "exact_kind", so if that kind label is genuinely authored at 2c then 2c pre-committed the defect framing and would be the first responsible stage. The record's per_issue block attributes the item choice to 2d (resolution_path llm, candidate_count 6), so 2d is the best-supported call from the evidence available.

(3) Positive-use card rc_924163d5a9c3 (baseboard_wear_scuffs, redfin_11077450, three photos): Terra supported and v1.1 truth says exact/warranted, but the reviewer refuted it - 'baseboards in all three rooms are freshly painted white and intact; the marks that are visible are roller patches on the walls above'. absence_statements.success_uses: This cluster HAS reviewed controls - 12 of them - so no missing-control statement is needed. Six are positive uses: rc_025ca614449b (peeling_or_discolored_paint, redfin_81000709, adjudicated supports_claim), rc_201ccb0c2313 (baseboard_wear_scuffs, redfin_125779232, supports_claim), rc_49b3ff4a6be8 (peeling, redfin_11000447, required, supports_claim), rc_d58b1f530fd9 (peeling, redfin_11077450, supports_claim), rc_7057c3c171e5 (baseboard, redfin_10952874, required, adjudicated unclear - the reviewer notes 'Trim is missing in some photos, its not visibly scuffed', so it counts for nothing in either direction), and rc_924163d5a9c3 (baseboard, redfin_11077450, adjudicated refuted despite a frozen v1.1 truth of exact/warranted and a Terra 'supported'). The four clean positive uses are the ones that make narrowing unsafe: three of them are approved by the reviewer on exactly the broad disjunct a narrowing would remove. Per-item counts confirm the base of correct behaviour is thin but real: peeling_or_discolored_paint 3 positive uses / 2 correct rejections / 1 hallucination annotation; baseboard_wear_scuffs 3 positive uses / 3 correct rejections / 0 hallucination annotations.

alternative_stage_analysis.alters_eligibility_package_economics: No item change, so no eligibility or economics effect. For context only: both items are severity 1, tier work, scope cosmetic, route_override null, package_role package_support with repair_support_when_driven true, so the four false rejections cost package-support conditions in bathroom, bedroom and living modernization packages rather than package drivers, and the two false acceptances add unwarranted PAINT_INTERIOR support. coverage_gap.rationale: Searched all 128 items in digest/items.json before considering a gap. Every observation in this cluster has a home: tired/patched/scuffed wall surfaces -> wall_scuffs_marks_or_dents (degradation, paint_drywall, DRYWALL_PATCH, all scenes open); aged or failed paint film -> peeling_or_discolored_paint (degradation, PAINT_INTERIOR); baseboard wear -> baseboard_wear_scuffs (degradation, TRIM_REPAIR); intact-but-dated wall colour -> paint_refresh_recommended (modernization, tier optional, embed_text literally 'Interior paint looks aged, yellowed, heavily personalized, or dated'); bathroom variants -> bathroom_paint_peeling_or_worn and bathroom_paint_refresh_recommended; cracks and holes -> damaged_drywall_or_cracks. The interior painted brick surround (633bb1ea) sits inside peeling_or_discolored_paint's own subject, 'interior paint', and the style-side alternative dated_fireplace_surround also exists (modernization, optional). Nothing in this cluster is unnamed, so there is no coverage gap and no split parent is needed.

diagnosis.catalog_ownership_argument: The catalog does not own this cluster, and the evidence closes the catalog lever from both sides at once. Both atomic claims already contain the disjunct that covers the supported photos: baseboard_wear_scuffs states 'scuffs, paint loss, dents, or general wear' and peeling_or_discolored_paint states 'peeling, bubbling, or visibly aged finish'. That same broad disjunct is simultaneously (a) the clause Terra refused to test on four real conditions the humans graded exact/warranted (b10d0b13, d7af7b65, e26ef990, 633bb1ea; all four carry disposition excluded / reason_code verdict_unsupported) and (b) the clause Terra leaned on to bill two intact surfaces (in-cluster counterexample 4a9736e4, truth absent/none, plus hallucination control rc_ab90ab9da2ab, truth absent/none). One phrase cannot be widened to rescue the four false rejections and narrowed to block the two false acceptances. More decisively, the cluster's own evidence shows that wording precision is not the binding lever at all: on d7af7b65 Terra wrote 'generally intact without clear scuffs, paint loss, or dents' and never evaluated 'general wear', on 633bb1ea it wrote 'no peeling or bubbling paint is apparent' and never evaluated 'visibly aged finish', and on 4a9736e4 it asserted 'visibly uneven, discolored areas and an aged-looking finish' about a uniform clean wall. A verifier that skips disjuncts it was given and invents detail it was not given will do the same to any replacement wording, so a re-worded claim cannot be predicted to move either error class. The catalog-owned facts that do exist here are real but inconsequential in this evidence: the item name and description over-commit to mechanism ('Peeling or Discolored Paint'; 'Paint that is peeling, bubbling, cracked, or visibly aged') while Terra only ever sees the atomic claim, and both items' embed_text promises more than their claim (divergence_scan: peeling_or_discolored_paint promised_not_claimed damage_break, moisture_rot, stain_discolor; baseboard_wear_scuffs promised_not_claimed missing_incomplete, trim_casing). Neither divergence changed a billing outcome in any of these seven units, so under the 2026-09-03 catalog-first direction they get documentation, not a change.

rejected_alternative_owners.why: Rejected on the two-sided trap plus the verifier-behaviour evidence above. Broadening is blocked by 5 confirmed correct rejections and 2 hallucination controls. Neither direction is verifiable offline because Terra behaviour cannot be replayed here.

evidence_bar_claim.conflict_note: Mixed signal is real and mandatory to state: three human supports_claim and three human refuted adjudications sit inside this cluster. Supports: f46cc039 (galley-kitchen walls blotchy, patched and scuffed with no peeling film), d7af7b65 (wide painted baseboard grimy and tired with no resolvable scuffs or dents), 633bb1ea (painted brick surround thin and streaky with brick and mortar showing through, no lifting paint). Refutations: b10d0b13 and e26ef990, both role=support, where the reviewer found the named mechanism plainly visible - bare, dark, paint-absent base trim in the half-bath, and a diagonal crack with lifted paint edges and flaking beside the bedroom door casing - so the cluster claim's 'mechanism not clearly visible' premise fails on those photos; and counterexample 4a9736e4, a uniform clean butter-yellow dining room with human truth absent/none. The conflict does not cancel the bar because it splits along a line that reinforces the outcome: on b10d0b13 and e26ef990 the human truths are exact/warranted and Terra still rejected, so those photos are additional Terra false rejections of claims that already fitted, while 4a9736e4 is a Terra false acceptance on intact paint. In other words the same wording fails in both directions on the same evidence, which is precisely why no wording change is proposed. No adjudication is contested here; the divergences from frozen v1.1 truth that do exist are listed as unresolved questions.
evidence_bar_claim.correlation_note: Not required by the ladder (3 counted supports on 3 distinct properties), recorded for completeness. redfin_80990371 contributes one counted support (d7af7b65, baseboard, photo_028) and one refuted support-role unit (e26ef990, bedroom wall, photo_003) on a different photo and a different condition, so no counted support is duplicated within a property; the other two counted supports are on redfin_10806500 and redfin_80917686 and share neither property, photo nor condition with it. pass_2d_follow_ups.note:
Confusion family, stated in full: paint-film failure vs wall-surface wear: two degradation items in the same trade (paint_drywall) and tier (work) at severity 1, differing in work_item_code (PAINT_INTERIOR vs DRYWALL_PATCH) and in whether the defect is the coating or the substrate
redfin_10806500 photo_004, kitchen scene, resolution_path llm, routing_reason exact_kind. 2d mapped the observation 'Wall finishes appear tired.' to peeling_or_discolored_paint at rank 7 while wall_scuffs_marks_or_dents sat at rank 6 with kind_ok and scene_ok both true; the 2a prose named the correct reading and only the correct reading ('Visible scuffs, patchy areas, and generally tired finishes suggest prep, repair, and repainting throughout') and the sibling issue on the same photo did resolve to wall_scuffs_marks_or_dents, so the better item was reachable and demonstrably selectable in the same run. The reviewer's own lineage note agrees: 'wall_scuffs_marks_or_dents (rank 6) fits the scuffs and patched areas better than a peeling item'. Human truth is misnamed/warranted and the condition was billed (accepted_for_work), so the correction is naming and specificity only: identical kind, severity, tier, scope and package_role, no economics delta. This is the only 2d selection failure in the cluster; the counterexample 4a9736e4 is deliberately NOT filed here because no better item was reachable in its list (all six candidates were degradation items and paint_refresh_recommended was kind-gated with rank null).

proposal.economics_fit: No economics field is touched; none is natively authorable for a carryover in any case. Context only: both items are severity 1, tier work, scope cosmetic, package_role package_support with repair_support_when_driven true across bathroom/bedroom/kitchen/living, so the six human units in this cluster differ from one another in name and trade bucket, not in materiality. Dollar effects of the four Terra false rejections are context under the scope direction and are not used to justify anything.
proposal.expected_benefit: The benefit is claimed for the non-catalog actions, not for a catalog change. (1) Terra calibration - require the verifier to evaluate every disjunct of the atomic claim it is given, and to refuse to assert visual detail the image does not show. On this cluster alone that addresses four false rejections of conditions the humans graded exact/warranted (b10d0b13, d7af7b65, e26ef990, 633bb1ea) and two false acceptances on intact paint (4a9736e4 and control rc_ab90ab9da2ab), i.e. errors in both directions from one calibration lever, which is exactly what a wording lever cannot do. (2) 2c kind routing - a dated-hue observation such as 'Wall color is yellowed' must be kinded modernization so paint_refresh_recommended (tier optional) becomes reachable; today it is kinded degradation and the modernization item is gated out with rank null on every unit here, which is the mechanism of the yellow-wall hard_false_billed card. (3) One pass_2d_follow_ups entry (f46cc039). (4) Documentation of the name/description and embed-vs-claim divergences on both items, per the scope direction's harmless-naming rule.
proposal.package_route_effects: None. route_override stays null on both items (no no_action route is implicated), trade buckets stay paint_drywall and trim_doors_windows, work item codes stay PAINT_INTERIOR and TRIM_REPAIR, and package_affinity is unchanged. The non-catalog actions proposed below are all verifier- or upstream-stage actions and cannot move a route by themselves.
proposal.product_policy: Not applicable. Neither implicated item is in a product-quarantined trade; electrical is not involved, so nothing forces a product-policy outcome.
proposal.regression_risk: Zero from this finding, because there are no ops and the guarded files are untouched. The risk being deliberately avoided is stated in the negative: a broadening of either claim would be tested against five confirmed correct rejections (rc_42f54b0e00fd, rc_532fa2016ed9, rc_7380e1876137, rc_aeea1143efaf, rc_cc24e226f76c) and two hallucination controls (in-cluster 4a9736e4, card rc_ab90ab9da2ab), and a narrowing would be tested against two of the three counted supports (f46cc039, 633bb1ea) and three positive-use cards whose reviewer reasons rest on the very disjunct that would be removed (rc_025ca614449b, rc_49b3ff4a6be8, rc_d58b1f530fd9). The Terra-calibration action carries its own regression exposure that must be measured live rather than here: making the verifier enumerate disjuncts could raise acceptance on marginal surfaces, so the five correct-rejection cards plus rc_ab90ab9da2ab should be re-run as the control set for that action.
proposal.retrieval_effects: None: no embed_text, name, description, support_any, deny_any or require_any is edited, so no item's rank changes anywhere and no offline-unverifiable embedding edit is incurred. Recorded for the lead's documentation lane: both items already promise more in retrieval than their claims deliver (peeling_or_discolored_paint promised_not_claimed damage_break, moisture_rot, stain_discolor - its embed advertises 'Lower-wall moisture staining, tide marks'; baseboard_wear_scuffs promised_not_claimed missing_incomplete, trim_casing - its embed advertises 'Missing baseboards, detached trim, visible gaps at wall base'). That is the channel by which incompleteness and staining observations reach claims that cannot cover them, and it is the substance of unresolved question 1.
proposal.semantic_before_after: No change. peeling_or_discolored_paint keeps atomic_claim subject 'interior paint' / state 'peeling, bubbling, or visibly aged finish' (ontology_basis visible_deterioration) and baseboard_wear_scuffs keeps subject 'baseboards' / state 'scuffs, paint loss, dents, or general wear' (ontology_basis dent_without_functional_impact). Both remain change_type reclassified carryovers with a single successor each. Nothing in the decisions file is touched, so the migration output is byte-identical.

unresolved_questions: baseboard_wear_scuffs promises incompleteness in retrieval that its claim does not cover. Its embed_text reads 'Missing baseboards, detached trim, visible gaps at wall base, incomplete base trim installation' and divergence_scan reports promised_not_claimed [missing_incomplete, trim_casing], while the atomic claim Terra sees is only 'scuffs, paint loss, dents, or general wear'. Unit b10d0b13's 2a observation was exactly an incompleteness observation ('Baseboards, caulking, and paint lines look incomplete or rough') and Terra rejected it on wear vocabulary. This is a genuine catalog-owned surface split, but it has zero supporting adjudications today because that unit is adjudicated refuted, so it cannot ground anything. Promotion recipe: human review of two photos on distinct properties showing missing or incomplete base trim where the pipeline resolved baseboard_wear_scuffs; two supports_claim verdicts would open a properly evidenced claim-coverage question.

Truth conflict on control rc_924163d5a9c3: frozen v1.1 truth is exact/warranted and Terra said supported, but the Phase B reviewer refuted it on the photos. Until reconciled it should not be leaned on as either a success control or an over-billing control. Flagged only; the adjudication stands as recorded and is not changed here.

Whether a differently worded claim would change Terra's behaviour is untestable offline - there is no Terra replay in this evidence set - and the direct evidence here (three units where Terra skipped a disjunct it was given, two where it asserted detail the photo lacks) argues it would not. Any future wording hypothesis on these two items needs a live Terra arm before it can be evaluated.

peeling_or_discolored_paint's degradation claim ('visibly aged finish', tier work) and paint_refresh_recommended's modernization retrieval text ('Interior paint looks aged, yellowed ... or dated', tier optional) both claim the word 'aged' across the kind boundary. That overlap is what lets an intact dated colour land on a work-tier degradation claim. The lever is the 2c kind decision, not either claim, but if a future cluster establishes the overlap costs billings in both directions it may deserve its own proposal - it cannot be raised here because the only unit that exercises it is the refuted counterexample.

f46cc039's kitchen candidate list put five kitchen-object items ahead of both wall items (wall_scuffs_marks_or_dents 6, peeling_or_discolored_paint 7). Whether retrieval systematically under-ranks wall and trim items in kitchen scenes is unmeasured - this cluster has a single kitchen unit - and would need a scan across kitchen-scene units to become a finding.

cases.attribution_rationale: The photo shows a metal-panel shed whose siding and trim are visibly damaged: creased/dented panels, rust streaking down the lower front and right panels, the door-opening trim bent and deformed at the head and jamb, a detached trim board lying on the broken slab, and a rusted deteriorated panel in the window opening. The human's note that this is a shed rather than the house is a scope remark, not a denial of the damage, and the v1 verdict recorded the Terra claim as supported, so the miss premise holds. The 2a prose did NOT omit the condition -- it states it directly under "Severe deferred maintenance": "missing/removed door, damaged siding and trim, deteriorated window". What the prose did not do is characterize the damage type (it says "damaged", never "rot", "warping", "cracks" or "missing sections"), but that is a wording difference, not a loss of the observation. Every intermediate stage carried it faithfully: 2b emitted the exact bullet "The siding and trim are damaged." with an exact join; 2c kept it (the four 2c drops were trees, fencing and metal posts, none of them this); 2d resolved it to damaged_or_rotted_siding_or_trim via support_phrase_hit, which is the correct catalog item, not a misresolution; 2e kept the issue id; projection produced condition oc1_1650c027b1d144a2. diagnosis.catalog_ownership_argument: The catalog does not own this unit and there is no catalog lever to pull. The frozen v1 truth agrees (terra_claim_supported), the lineage is clean at every stage (2a prose stated 'damaged siding and trim'; 2b joined exact; 2c kept; 2d resolved rank 1 by support_phrase_hit; 2e kept; projection produced oc1_1650c027b1d144a2), and Terra then returned 'unsupported' on the rationale that the siding and trim 'do not show clear rot, warping, cracks, or missing sections' - a verdict the image contradicts. cases.attribution_rationale: Premise confirmed by looking at photo_015.jpg: a dated galley kitchen (worn oak cabinets with doors hanging open, light laminate counters, white gas range and fridge, single flush-mount fixture) whose wall and ceiling paint is visibly tired — pale blue-gray in the kitchen going to dingy beige in the adjoining hall, with scuffing and uneven, discolored patches, and a dulled ceiling. A paint refresh is real and warranted here, matching the adjudicated claim=exact / work=warranted. The 2a prose did NOT miss this: it contains a dedicated Walls/ceilings bullet stating the paint is dated (while correctly noting no major cracking is visible), so pass_2a is ruled out. Every downstream rung before Terra also handled it correctly: 2b produced bullet 11 "Wall and ceiling paint is dated." with an exact join; 2c kept it (it is in p2c_surviving, not p2c_dropped); 2d resolved it to paint_refresh_recommended via exact_kind, which is the right catalog item for dated paint — no better target exists, so the item's canned claim_text mentioning "highly personalized colors" is a framing artifact of the item, not a mis-resolution; and condition projection produced oc1_8f96473f0a4cb633, which reached Terra. The p2e_status "absent" plus tier_optional_suppressed is not the loss point, since removed_count is 0 and the issue still carries a projected_condition_id, so 2e cost nothing. Terra is therefore the first stage that went wrong: it returned "unsupported" on the ground that the paint is "neutral and not clearly dated" — a direct contradiction of both the 2a observation and what the photo shows — and that verdict, via reason_code verdict_unsupported, is what excluded the condition from billing. This is not the known post-Terra routing gap, because Terra did not support the condition and then lose it to disposition; Terra's own rejection is the cause.

diagnosis.catalog_ownership_argument: Catalog ownership was tested and rejected. Under convention 1 the surface that decides Terra's verdict is the atomic_claim alone, and that claim already reads subject 'interior paint color', state 'dated or highly personalized colors' - a disjunction whose first limb is exactly what all six 2a observations asserted ('Wall and ceiling paint is dated', 'The wall paint is beige/tan and dated', 'The paint scheme is dated', 'The paint palette is dated', 'Room has a dated paint palette and finishes', 'The beige wall paint is dated'). Terra rejected all four cases on the second limb without ever adjudicating the first: 'neutral and not clearly dated or highly personalized' (f5459a09), 'neutral and not clearly highly personalized or dated' (6ea2a14d), 'neutral beige color without a clearly highly personalized color scheme' (29c5c08e, which concedes the beige outright), 'neutral and not clearly dated or highly personalized' (8f96473f). A disjunct that is present in the claim and unread by the verifier is not a wording defect that the catalog can fix; there is no rewrite of a claim that already says 'dated' that makes 'dated' more present. divergence_scan independently reports paint_refresh_recommended with an empty promised_not_claimed and an empty claimed_not_promised list - retrieval text and claim text agree, so the retrieval-vs-claim split that drives CAP-014 and CAP-016 does not exist on this item. The one honest catalog-side observation is recorded as a contributing cause only: 'highly personalized colors' is the concrete, testable half of the disjunction while 'dated' is left unqualified, and all four rationales anchor on the concrete half. Acting on that observation - inserting convention-4 tells ('era-specific builder beige/tan, worn or yellowed finish, dated colour scheme') into the atomic_claim - is natively expressible (paint_refresh_recommended is a reclassified carryover, so /successors/0/atomic_claim is settable), but it is NOT warranted on this evidence: the item is already over-firing in the opposite direction on the very same claim (control rc_4abeff09724f, redfin_10949071 photo_006, a required positive_use where Terra said 'supported' on freshly painted current blue-grey and the Phase B reviewer adjudicated refuted), and two more controls (rc_ef3234842cb9 mid-grey, rc_c34e48007ce2 current greige) are correct rejections that any loosening of 'dated' puts at risk. Broadening a claim that is simultaneously being read too narrowly by the verifier and too loosely on clean walls would trade four recovered conditions for an unknown number of new hallucinations, which is the opposite of the scope direction's judging criterion. The lever that actually moves these four cases sits in Terra's reading of the claim, not in the catalog.

This is the proof that Terra CAN affirm the 'dated' limb without personalization when the hue is off-neutral, which localises the failure precisely to neutral-hued era palettes.

proposal.regression_risk: The dominant risk is that a tell list written loosely degenerates back into a hue test in the permissive direction and starts billing every warm-toned wall. rc_4abeff09724f proves that failure mode is already live on this item under the current wording, so the calibration must be validated against all eight controls below before it is adopted, and specifically must keep rc_ef3234842cb9 (plain mid-grey) and rc_c34e48007ce2 (current greige) rejected. A second risk is double-billing in rooms where the era tell belongs to another item - the rc_64a78239f11f rooms (tan over grooved panelling under a popcorn ceiling) are the case in point, and the reviewer could not settle them; the calibration should require a tell attributable to the PAINT (era colour, worn/yellowed/patched finish) rather than borrowing datedness from panelling, ceiling texture or cabinetry, which have their own items. Third, this cluster's own two weaker units (8f96473f, 29c5c08e) sit close to the convention-4 line, so a calibration tuned to recover them specifically would be tuned past the line; the bar survives without them and the recipe should be tuned to the two strong ones.
proposal.retrieval_effects: None. No embed_text, name, description, support_any or deny_any is touched, so no item's rank moves anywhere, and the offline-unverifiable embedding risk called out in the brief is not incurred. This matters because paint_refresh_recommended already ranks 1-3 on every issue in this cluster: there is nothing retrieval could improve.
proposal.semantic_before_after: No catalog change is proposed, so the item's semantics are unchanged: paint_refresh_recommended keeps kind modernization, ontology_basis dated_style, subject 'interior paint color', state 'dated or highly personalized colors', name 'Paint Refresh Opportunity', its description, embed_text and support_any ['repaint','paint refresh','dated paint','bold color'], and empty deny_any/null require_any. What changes is outside the catalog: Terra's reading of the existing disjunction. Today Terra collapses 'dated OR highly personalized' into a hue test on the second limb and answers 'the colour is neutral, therefore not supported' (four rationales, all four rejecting on personalization; 29c5c08e concedes 'neutral beige' and still rejects). The intended reading is that either limb suffices and that the 'dated' limb is decided on convention-4 concrete tells - an identifiable era-specific finish (builder gold-tan/beige or taupe-brown trim, popcorn ceiling, period-typical scheme) or a visibly worn, yellowed, patched paint surface - so that a neutral hue is not by itself disqualifying and, symmetrically, a clean current neutral with no tell is not billable.

unresolved_questions: Truth conflict on rc_4abeff09724f: frozen v1.1 truth says claim exact / work warranted / supported_billed and Terra said 'supported', while the Phase B reviewer adjudicated the same photo refuted ('freshly painted mid-tone blue-grey, a current neutral'). Both are pinned facts and neither is changed here. Which one governs decides whether the recommended Terra calibration should be scored as fixing an over-bill or as introducing a miss, so the reconciliation owner should rule on it before the calibration is measured.

Boundary question with CAP-001: on the two weaker units the reviewer's supporting evidence is as much deterioration as era - 8f96473f is a dull, dingy, unevenly discoloured finish and 29c5c08e carries a streaky patch-discoloured hall wall. If deterioration rather than era is the operative tell, the natural home for those observations is peeling_or_discolored_paint ('peeling, bubbling, or visibly aged finish'), which sits in CAP-001 and was kind-gated against modernization-kinded observations there. Nobody should act on this without a ruling, because the two clusters currently pull in opposite directions on the same physical surface.

Should the tell list live in Terra's prompt/rubric or in the atomic_claim? This cluster recommends the prompt, on the grounds that the claim already says 'dated' and that the control set shows two-sided error. If a later reviewer decides Terra cannot be calibrated without claim-side tells, the op is natively expressible (paint_refresh_recommended is a reclassified carryover, so /successors/0/atomic_claim with a refreshed /atomicity_rationale and /expected_effects/routing is settable), but it would need fresh human review of the three refuted/unclear controls first.

rc_64a78239f11f leaves untested the case where dated colour, grooved wood panelling and popcorn ceiling co-occur. Until that is adjudicated, the corpus has no reviewed answer to whether paint_refresh_recommended should fire alongside dated_wood_paneling and popcorn_or_acoustic_ceiling_texture in the same room or defer to them.

cases.attribution_rationale:
Premise confirmed. The photo shows a dark, high-gloss plank floor whose grain repeats photographically board-to-board (laminate/LVP rather than solid hardwood), and the foreground third shows light streaks along board edges, mismatched lighter boards toward the bottom-left, and seam lines catching light — consistent with the adjudicated v1.1 verdict (claim=exact, work=warranted, terra_claim_supported). A real, billable flooring condition went unbilled.

The 2a prose DID contain the condition, and contained it specifically: it names the flooring bullet as "heavily worn/scuffed" and as appearing "to have lifting/open seams or patched areas near the foreground" — both the material read ("dark plank") and the defect ("lifting/open seams") are present, so pass_2a is not the failure. What 2a did NOT contain was a material identification as vinyl/linoleum; it said only "dark plank flooring."

Walking the ladder: 2b produced the matching bullet ("Flooring has lifting or open seams near the foreground.") and the join is exact, so not 2b. p2c_dropped is empty and the bullet appears in p2c_surviving, so not 2c. 2d resolved it to vinyl_linoleum_torn_or_lifted; that resolution is endorsed rather than faulted by the truth basis, because the human graded the claim axis "exact" against that item's claim text ("vinyl or linoleum flooring torn, worn through, or lifting material") — so 2d is not the first wrong stage. p2e_status is "kept" and, per the corpus rule, 2e is not an available attribution anyway. The issue did become a condition (projected_condition_id oc1_476cd4f80565d162), so condition_projection is not it.

That leaves Terra, which is where it actually died: terra_verdict "unsupported", terra_rationale "The visible flooring is hard plank material, with no vinyl or linoleum tears, lifting, or open seams shown", disposition excluded with reason_code verdict_unsupported and accepted=false. Terra rejected a claim the human adjudicated as supported, and it did so on material-identity grounds — asserting the plank material is not vinyl/linoleum — which the photo does not establish (the repeating grain and gloss are at least as consistent with LVP as with hardwood) and which the human's own note flags as a catalog-vocabulary trap ("we might want to change the catalog to 'hard flooring' ... so that we dont get caught up on hardwood, LVP, linoleum"). Note also that Terra's rationale goes further and denies "lifting, or open seams" outright, contradicting the 2a observation and the foreground evidence. This is not the known post-Terra routing gap: Terra did not support this condition, it rejected it, so the ladder has a rung that fits.

cases.attribution_rationale:
Premise holds. Reading photo_004.jpg directly: the galley kitchen has dark maroon sheet/vinyl flooring in a plank pattern whose seams are plainly visible across the entire floor, with lighter worn-through streaks along the traffic path, dark gouges/marks mid-floor, and a ragged light-colored break in the material at the wall base under the sink/counter run on the right where the flooring no longer sits flush. That matches the v1.1 adjudication (claim exact, work warranted) for the claim "vinyl or linoleum flooring torn, worn through, or lifting material", so this is a genuine MISS.

The 2a prose DID contain the condition, and contained it in the right terms: it devotes a whole standout bullet to "Flooring is a major issue: worn, stained/discolored sheet flooring or old vinyl/linoleum with visible seams and damage. Plan on removal and subfloor inspection before new flooring." What the prose did NOT do is understate or generalize it -- it names the substrate (sheet flooring / vinyl-linoleum), the seam separation, and the damage, and calls for removal and subfloor inspection. So pass_2a is not the failure.

Nor is any intermediate stage. 2b emitted bullet index 5, "Sheet flooring has visible seams and damage", joined exact/matched. 2c kept it -- it appears in p2c_surviving and is absent from p2c_dropped (the seven 2c drops are all unrelated: range, open lower cabinet, storage, cords, range hood, galley layout, window/exterior access). 2d resolved it to vinyl_linoleum_torn_or_lifted, kind defect, via exact_kind, and the human graded the resulting claim wording as "exact" -- i.e. the catalog resolution was correct, not a mis-resolution. 2e kept the issue (p2e_status "kept", issue id present in kept_issue_ids), and per the case brief 2e cost nothing here anyway. condition_projection produced condition oc1_cb817305acf2e48c, so the issue did become a billable condition.

The condition therefore reached Terra fully intact, and Terra rejected it: terra_verdict "unsupported" with the rationale "The flooring is visible, but no clearly torn, worn-through, or lifting material is apparent" -- contradicted by both the 2a prose and my own reading of the photo -- yielding accepted=false, disposition excluded, reason_code verdict_unsupported. Terra is the first stage that went wrong. This is expressly NOT the known post-Terra routing gap, because Terra did not support the condition and let routing drop it; Terra itself is the rejecting stage, which the ladder does have a rung for.

cases.attribution_rationale:
Premise confirmed on inspection. Both photos show the same green marbled/veined tile floor — continuous, intact, no wear-through, no cupping, no missing tiles, and no staining distinguishable from the tile's own marbling (the "scattered dark marks" Terra cited read as veining and lighting falloff). What the floor unmistakably is, is dated mid-century green marble-look tile. Replacement is warranted, but the warranting mechanism is obsolescence/style, not surface degradation — exactly the misnamed_billed pattern (work warranted, claim misnamed).

The wrong name originates in 2a. On photo_042 the prose says "the green tile/vinyl-style floor is dated and appears worn/dirty", welding a false wear/dirt mechanism onto a correct "dated" reading; on photo_044 it says the tile "appears worn/uneven in places" while framing the fix as something that "would dramatically modernize the room". So 2a prose DID contain the correct condition (dated, needs replacement) and ALSO contained the unsupported degradation mechanism (worn/dirty, worn/uneven). It did not contain any observation that survives inspection as actual wear or staining.

Everything after 2a is faithful. 2b split 042's sentence into two separate bullets ("...is dated." and "...appears worn and dirty."), exact join at bullet_index 7 on both photos, no distortion. 2c dropped neither flooring bullet on 042 and kept the wear bullet on 044 (it dropped only "dominates the space"). 2d resolved the wear bullets to worn_or_stained_flooring by exact_kind — the correct catalog item for the text it was handed — and separately resolved the "dated" bullet to older_flooring_style, so the correctly-named issue was available and not lost. 2e kept all issues (removed_count 0, no suppression), the condition projected, and Terra supported it. No later stage introduced or re-labeled the wear meaning; it was already in the prose. Under the hallucination branch — unsupported material claim already present in the 2a prose — 2a is the first stage that went wrong.

cases.attribution_rationale:
Premise holds. Photo_005 is a dated kitchen: white raised-panel cabinets, dark speckled laminate counters, mosaic backsplash, coil range, and a beige faux-tile-pattern vinyl SHEET floor running under the range and dining table. The floor reads as intact and unbroken -- no tears, no discrete stains, no visible discoloration beyond general dinginess/scuffing near the range toe-kick -- but its pattern and material plainly date the room and it is a legitimate replacement item. That is exactly the human adjudication: work=warranted, claim=misnamed. So a real condition existed and went unbilled (disposition excluded, reason verdict_unsupported) -- a MISS.

Pass 2a is NOT at fault: the prose carries the condition with the correct meaning, in the "Flooring is ripe for replacement" bullet -- "The vinyl is worn-looking and visually dated. LVP, tile, or a continuous floor into adjoining spaces would modernize it quickly." The framing there is modernization (dated, replace to modernize), with "worn-looking" used as an appearance word, not a claim of staining or material failure. 2b rendered it faithfully as bullet 13, "Vinyl flooring is worn-looking and visually dated." (exact join), and 2c kept it -- it is present in p2c_surviving, so neither of those rungs fits.

2d is the first stage that went wrong. With 7 candidates it took resolution_path=lexical_shortcut on shortcut_reason=support_phrase_hit -- i.e. it latched onto the token "worn" -- and resolved to the degradation item vinyl_linoleum_worn_or_stained, whose claim text asserts "vinyl or linoleum flooring staining, discoloration, or wear on intact material." That is a physical-deterioration assertion the prose never made and the photo does not support, and it discards the half of the bullet that actually mattered ("visually dated"). The same photo's other dated-finish bullets resolved correctly to modernization items (outdated_kitchen_finishes, appliances_dated_or_basic), which is where a dated-flooring observation belonged. Condition projection then faithfully carried the misnamed claim forward, and Terra rejected it accurately on its own terms -- "The visible vinyl flooring appears intact without clear staining, discoloration, or wear" -- which matches what I see in the photo. Terra therefore is not the first wrong stage; it verified correctly the claim it was handed. One caveat: the record exposes catalog kind only alongside the 2d-resolved item, so if the degradation kind label were assigned upstream at 2c rather than chosen at 2d, blame would shift one rung earlier; the recorded p2d shortcut mechanism is the concrete documented cause, so 2d is the call.

diagnosis.catalog_ownership_argument: The catalog does NOT own this cluster, and the Phase A hypothesis that the material commitments are wrong is overturned by the adjudications. Take the four human units one at a time. (1) rc_d60c090abd2c, redfin_11000447 photo_004: the reviewer read maroon SHEET VINYL with a worn-through traffic lane and a ragged lifted edge at the wall base - exactly the material and mechanism vinyl_linoleum_torn_or_lifted commits to - and 2d actively overrode rank 1 (hard_flooring_broken_or_warped) to pick the vinyl item at rank 2. (2) rc_128caa6212b8, redfin_11000447 photo_003: 2d resolved to vinyl_linoleum_torn_or_lifted and the human graded the CLAIM axis 'exact' against that item's wording; Terra rejected on a material-identity ground ('the visible flooring is hard plank material') that the reviewer says the photo cannot establish. Steven's own v1.1 note on that row - 'we might want to change the catalog to "hard flooring" or something similar so that we dont get caught up on hardwood, LVP, linoleum' - is the single strongest argument for collapsing the material split, and it runs OPPOSITE to every adjudicated material finding in this cluster (on both decidable cases the material matched the item used). It cannot be acted on: unclear never becomes support, and it is one note on one row. Promotion recipe: re-review photo_003 at full resolution to settle the material, or add a second decidable vinyl-vs-laminate case where the material commitment demonstrably costs a billing; only then does a material-subject op have a counted human support behind it.

Is Terra's material-identity reasoning a systematic failure mode on printed-grain resilient flooring? Two of four human units here died on it (rc_128caa6212b8 asserts 'hard plank material' about a floor the reviewer says could be LVP; rc_d60c090abd2c denies wear-through the reviewer sees), and a third case at the same family - the redfin_125970550 lead - shows Terra happily verifying SHEET goods against a 'hard flooring' claim. This needs a Terra-lane sample, not a catalog edit; it also sits inside the already-closed downstream-miss finding (docs/RESULT_error_attribution_20260831.md).

Both vinyl split successors have zero reviewed positive uses, zero agreements and zero correct rejections. Before any op touches vinyl_linoleum_torn_or_lifted or vinyl_linoleum_worn_or_stained, the control base has to be built; today a change to either could not be regression-checked at all.

cases.attribution_rationale:
Premise holds on my own inspection. Photo_044 shows a dark-stained oak floor that, despite a glossy sheen, carries a distinct dark scuff/smear blemish in the center foreground plus fine surface scratching visible in the raking light across the left half; photo_048 shows the same flooring with clear board-to-board color variation and a dulled, worn finish along the traffic path toward the closet. That is exactly the catalog claim "hard flooring finish scratches, scuffs, or worn finish on intact flooring," and it matches the adjudicated v1.1 axes (claim=exact, work=warranted).

The 2a prose did NOT omit this. Both photos' prose name it in the first bullet: photo_044 says the hardwood floors "appear scuffed/worn in places and could benefit from refinishing or at least a deep clean and recoat," and photo_048 says they "could benefit from refinishing or at least a deep clean/polish; there may be minor wear and color variation." What 2a did not contain was any competing or hedged reading that would have weakened the condition -- it is stated plainly as wear needing refinishing, so pass_2a is not the failure.

Every intermediate rung also passed it through cleanly, so none of them can be first: 2b produced verbatim bullets ("Solid hardwood floors are scuffed and worn." and "Hardwood floors show minor wear and color variation.") and both joined with method=exact; 2c kept both as survivors rather than dropping them (2c's drops on these photos were unrelated -- registers, trim, natural light, closet doors); 2d resolved both to the correct catalog item hard_flooring_scratched_or_worn via routing_reason exact_kind, so there is no wrong-item error; 2e status is "kept" for both issues; and condition_projection succeeded, yielding condition oc1_523e4aed4e443052.

The condition therefore reached Terra fully formed, and Terra is where it died: terra_verdict "unsupported" with the rationale that the flooring "appears generally intact without clear scratches, scuffs, or worn finish," producing accepted=false and reason_code verdict_unsupported. That directly contradicts what the photos show. This is not the known post-Terra routing/disposition gap -- Terra did not support the condition and then lose it downstream; Terra itself rejected it -- so "unclear" does not apply. Terra is the first and only stage that went wrong.

cases.attribution_rationale:
Premise holds. Photo_005 is a dated kitchen: white raised-panel cabinets, dark speckled laminate counters, mosaic backsplash, coil range, and a beige faux-tile-pattern vinyl SHEET floor running under the range and dining table. The floor reads as intact and unbroken -- no tears, no discrete stains, no visible discoloration beyond general dinginess/scuffing near the range toe-kick -- but its pattern and material plainly date the room and it is a legitimate replacement item. That is exactly the human adjudication: work=warranted, claim=misnamed. So a real condition existed and went unbilled (disposition excluded, reason verdict_unsupported) -- a MISS.

Pass 2a is NOT at fault: the prose carries the condition with the correct meaning, in the "Flooring is ripe for replacement" bullet -- "The vinyl is worn-looking and visually dated. LVP, tile, or a continuous floor into adjoining spaces would modernize it quickly." The framing there is modernization (dated, replace to modernize), with "worn-looking" used as an appearance word, not a claim of staining or material failure. 2b rendered it faithfully as bullet 13, "Vinyl flooring is worn-looking and visually dated." (exact join), and 2c kept it -- it is present in p2c_surviving, so neither of those rungs fits.

2d is the first stage that went wrong. With 7 candidates it took resolution_path=lexical_shortcut on shortcut_reason=support_phrase_hit -- i.e. it latched onto the token "worn" -- and resolved to the degradation item vinyl_linoleum_worn_or_stained, whose claim text asserts "vinyl or linoleum flooring staining, discoloration, or wear on intact material." That is a physical-deterioration assertion the prose never made and the photo does not support, and it discards the half of the bullet that actually mattered ("visually dated"). The same photo's other dated-finish bullets resolved correctly to modernization items (outdated_kitchen_finishes, appliances_dated_or_basic), which is where a dated-flooring observation belonged. Condition projection then faithfully carried the misnamed claim forward, and Terra rejected it accurately on its own terms -- "The visible vinyl flooring appears intact without clear staining, discoloration, or wear" -- which matches what I see in the photo. Terra therefore is not the first wrong stage; it verified correctly the claim it was handed. One caveat: the record exposes catalog kind only alongside the 2d-resolved item, so if the degradation kind label were assigned upstream at 2c rather than chosen at 2d, blame would shift one rung earlier; the recorded p2d shortcut mechanism is the concrete documented cause, so 2d is the call.

alternative_stage_analysis.alters_eligibility_package_economics: No change is proposed, so no economics move. The economics answer this cluster owes, stated affirmatively: KEEP 'clean but' in older_flooring_style's atomic_claim. It is the only textual guard that stops a floor that is both dated and dirty from billing on both lanes, and both lanes are already simultaneously live - redfin_80925528 emitted a degradation bullet ('worn and dirty' -> worn_or_stained_flooring, accepted, and the human called it a 2a hallucination) and four modernization bullets ('the green floor is dated' -> older_flooring_style at rank 1) on the same floor. The lanes are not economically symmetric: older_flooring_style is severity 2, scope replace and package_DRIVER for bedroom_modernization and living_modernization, while worn_or_stained_flooring is severity 1, package_SUPPORT only and defaultHidden true. Removing 'clean but' would therefore not merely add a hidden second line - it could promote a whole-room modernization package that the wear item cannot trigger on its own, with zero counted human support asking for it and two hallucination controls (rc_7cceb5c878de, rc_c135e76317be) sitting on exactly that surface. One honest caveat that strengthens rather than weakens the call: six leads on floors the reviewer described as dirty, soiled or heavily worn (redfin_11000447 x2, redfin_125779232 x2, redfin_125970550, redfin_80990371) carry stored_verdict=supported on older_flooring_style anyway, so the guard is under-enforced at runtime today. Deleting the words would legitimise that leakage rather than fix it, and the enforcement gap belongs to Terra.

diagnosis.catalog_ownership_argument: Catalog ownership was tested to the point of a runnable counterfactual and REJECTED. The one candidate catalog lever with a counted human support behind it was vinyl_linoleum_worn_or_stained's support_any, because the redfin_80916010 miss is recorded as resolution_path=lexical_shortcut / shortcut_reason=support_phrase_hit. The family structure step deferred that lever because the digest never names which phrase matched. This analysis resolved it: tools/scene_classifier_passes.py::_resolve_candidate_via_lexical_shortcut tests only candidates[0]'s support_any using tools/pipeline_common.py::term_matches, and running that real matcher over the real observation ('Vinyl flooring is worn-looking and visually dated.') against the item's shipped support_any returns exactly one hit - the bare material token 'vinyl'. 'worn vinyl' and 'stained vinyl' do not match, and 'worn' is not a token of this item at all, so the case's own attribution rationale ('latched onto the token "worn"') is factually wrong about the mechanism. That answer points AWAY from the catalog rather than toward it, for three independent reasons. (1) Prevalence: bare subject nouns in support_any are the catalog's own authoring convention, not this item's error - 125 of 128 items carry at least one condition-free support token (appliance, cabinet, window, gutter, outlet, deck, front door, ...), and the sibling successor vinyl_linoleum_torn_or_lifted carries the identical five material tokens. Pruning one successor would make it inconsistent with 124 other items and would leave the same hazard everywhere else. (2) Contract: tools/catalog_embeddings.py documents and implements support_any as 'soft support / ranking hint only (not enforced as gate)', and retrieval score is pure cosine over the item's embed text, so support_any changes no rank anywhere. The author wrote a legal ranking hint; 2d's shortcut unilaterally promotes that hint into a sufficient rule for asserting the item's atomic_claim ('staining, discoloration, or wear on intact material') without ever consulting the LLM. The defect is in the consumer, not in the field. (3) divergence_scan agrees: vinyl_linoleum_worn_or_stained records promised_not_claimed = [] - its material tokens match its own subject, so there is no two-surface divergence to repair. Under convention 1 the surface that failed here is 2d-side mechanics, not claim-bearing wording. The other flooring items are equally clean on the claim surface: hard_flooring_scratched_or_worn's support_any (scratch, scuff, worn floor, dull finish, worn finish) carries no stain or style token, so the catalog did not invite the redfin_10952874 error either.

Both needed concepts exist as catalog items with the right scene groups (see coverage_gap.rationale). Nothing observed here is unnameable in catalog 3.2, so no split parent and no new successor is warranted.

The dated/worn boundary is a deliberate design, not an ambiguity: older_flooring_style is modernization with 'clean but visually outdated'; worn_or_stained_flooring and hard_flooring_scratched_or_worn are degradation with 'without structural concern' / 'on intact flooring'. The reachability scan shows the boundary is actually decided upstream by Pass 2a's word choice - 'dated' alone yields an all-modernization pool with older_flooring_style at rank 1, while adding 'worn' or 'scuffed' flips the pool to degradation and drops it entirely - and is then enforced by the exact_kind filter. Collapsing the ontology would be a very large lever aimed at an upstream cause, and it would remove the anti-double-bill guard analysed under alters_eligibility_package_economics.

evidence_bar_claim.conflict_note: Mandatory and material. The same item family produced one counted human support for 'the resolved kind is wrong' and one counted human refutation for 'the resolved kind is right, Terra was wrong'. At redfin_10952874 (rc_eef1daf73e2a) the reviewer found paint spills and splatters on otherwise intact laminate billed as a scratched or worn finish - human truth misnamed_but_warranted, attribution stage 2d. At redfin_126418713 (rc_d0197df43080) the reviewer found that hard_flooring_scratched_or_worn was exactly the right name for the faint smudge and hairline scratches visible, refuting the cluster claim - human truth exact_and_warranted, attribution stage terra. The refutation does not cancel the support because the two fail at different stages and about different behaviour: one is a selection error with the better item at rank 1, the other is a verification error on a correctly resolved item. The refutation's own property shows Terra failing in both directions on the same item - rc_d0197df43080 rejects a real condition while control rc_c135e76317be supports the same claim on newly refinished floors across three photos - so the refuting signal is evidence about Terra's consistency, not evidence that the catalog's wear wording is well calibrated. Net effect on the outcome: the mixed signal reinforces no_change, because the supporting half points at Pass 2d and the refuting half points at Terra, and neither points at an editable catalog surface.

redfin_80916010 photo_005, issue 14a0ed440898b159. Two defects in one case, both non-catalog. (a) Reachability: older_flooring_style was not in the pool and could not have been - routing_reason=exact_kind on a degradation bullet, all seven candidates degradation, older_flooring_style kind_ok=false (reachability_scan). better_rank is null for that reason, and the best in-pool alternative (worn_or_stained_flooring at rank 2) over-claims wear exactly as the selected item does, so no re-ranking rescues this. (b) Mechanism, now verified rather than assumed: 2d took resolution_path=lexical_shortcut with shortcut_reason=support_phrase_hit, and re-running the shipped matcher (tools/scene_classifier_passes.py::_resolve_candidate_via_lexical_shortcut with tools/pipeline_common.py::term_matches) over the real observation against the item's shipped support_any returns exactly one hit: the bare material token 'vinyl'. Not 'worn vinyl', not 'stained vinyl'; 'worn' is not a token of this item at all, so the case's attribution rationale is wrong about which token fired. The shortcut therefore skipped the LLM entirely and asserted 'staining, discoloration, or wear on intact material' on the strength of a material noun; Terra correctly rejected that claim and a real dated-flooring replacement went unbilled. The actionable owner is the shortcut rule - support_any is documented as a non-gating ranking hint and 125 of 128 items author bare subject nouns into it - not this item's tokens. Suggested 2d-lane fix, for the deferred Pass 2d work and explicitly NOT proposed as a catalog change: require a condition-bearing term match (or subject-plus-condition co-occurrence) before the shortcut may bypass the LLM.

So no support_any edit anywhere in this cluster could have changed a candidate rank, and the ranks that actually mattered - worn_or_stained_flooring at rank 1 on both redfin_10952874 issues, older_flooring_style absent by kind at redfin_80916010 - are untouchable from the catalog's retrieval-hint surface.
proposal.semantic_before_after: No change proposed; the catalog's semantics stay exactly as authored. Recorded for the lead, the op that was built and rejected would have been: legacy_id worn_or_stained_vinyl_linoleum, path /successors/1/support_any (index 1 is vinyl_linoleum_worn_or_stained; index 0 is vinyl_linoleum_torn_or_lifted), op set, after ['worn vinyl', 'stained vinyl', 'discolored flooring'] - dropping the five bare material tokens linoleum / vinyl / vinyl sheet / sheet flooring / resilient flooring - with the required companion sets on /atomicity_rationale and /expected_effects/routing. It is natively expressible (support_any is set directly on a split successor) and it does fix the failing case in simulation, but it is NOT proposed for the reasons in diagnosis.catalog_ownership_argument and alternative_stage_analysis.steals_neighbors_or_damages_successes. No dry run was executed and no expected_item_changes are claimed.

unresolved_questions: Whether the degradation kind on the compound bullet 'Vinyl flooring is worn-looking and visually dated.' (redfin_80916010, issue 14a0ed440898b159) was assigned at 2c or chosen at 2d. The frozen record exposes catalog kind only alongside the 2d-resolved item; routing_reason=exact_kind with all seven candidates degradation points to a real upstream kind filter, but that is inference. It decides whether the follow-up is owned by 2c or by 2d; it does not change the outcome, because neither owner is the catalog.

worn_or_stained_flooring's 'dated' / 'aged' / 'outdated' support_any tokens on a claim asserting only wear (divergence_scan promised_not_claimed=['dated']) are a genuine two-surface divergence and are natively editable via overrides on a reclassified carryover, but no counted human unit traces a failure to them. Promotion recipe: find a case where worn_or_stained_flooring is candidates[0] and the observation matches only a style token - i.e. resolution_path=lexical_shortcut with shortcut_reason=support_phrase_hit and no wear word in the bullet. No such case exists in the frozen evidence; every unit where those tokens could have mattered resolved by LLM.

Catalog-wide question raised but not answered by this cluster, for the Pass 2d lane: 2d's lexical shortcut treats any support_any hit on candidates[0] as sufficient to assert that item's atomic_claim without LLM adjudication, while catalog_embeddings documents support_any as a non-gating ranking hint and 125 of 128 items author bare subject nouns into it. That contract mismatch is a resolver-design question; a per-item catalog fix would be arbitrary and would leave the hazard on the other 124 items. Suggested shape (not proposed here): require the shortcut to match a condition-bearing term, or a subject term co-occurring with a condition term, before it may bypass the LLM.

cases.attribution_rationale:
Premise confirmed from the photo: the vanity needs real work, but the billed name is wrong. photo_008 shows a narrow green bath whose vanity has painted, dated-but-serviceable door fronts, while its base is physically compromised — a dark open gap under the countertop overhang where the base/toe-kick trim has come away, and a rough, dark, deteriorated strip down the exposed side panel edge to the floor. That is damage, not a faded finish; the billed claim_text "worn or faded finish on intact vanity" asserts an intactness the photo contradicts. Terra's own supporting rationale ("dark deterioration along its exposed side edge") describes a damage condition, not the condition it was supporting.

What the 2a prose DID contain: both halves of the truth — the general wear ("The vanity looks worn") and the actual base anomaly ("possibly not fully finished at the bottom—the toe-kick/base area is open or misaligned"). What it did NOT contain: any damage/deterioration/water-stain wording; it framed the base as incomplete installation and headlined the vanity as "worn" and "dated." Because the real problem is present in 2a prose, pass_2a is not the answer — 2a saw it.

Downstream stays faithful until naming. 2b split the compound 2a sentence into atomic bullets and emitted BOTH "The vanity cabinet surfaces appear worn" (exact join, bullet_index 4, the billed one) and "The vanity toe-kick or base area appears open or misaligned" — no bullet is missing. 2c dropped neither; both survived. So the first stage with a choice it got wrong is 2d, whose entire job is choosing the catalog name. With candidate_count 8 it took resolution_path "lexical_shortcut" with shortcut_reason "support_phrase_hit" — a keyword latch on "worn" — and landed on vanity_worn_finish. The correct name was available and demonstrably reachable in this very run: the sibling bullet from the same 2a sentence on the same photo resolved to vanity_damaged_or_water_stained. 2d bound a true-but-weak observation to an item carrying a false qualifier ("intact vanity") about an object the same photo shows is not intact. This maps onto the ladder's own rung: resolved to the wrong catalog item -> 2d.

Confidence is medium, not high, for one honest reason: judged only on its own input string ("The vanity cabinet surfaces appear worn"), 2d's pick is defensible, and an alternative reading blames 2b for fragmenting one compound vanity-condition observation into pieces, stripping the not-intact qualifier from the piece that got billed. I rejected that because 2b's split is faithful atomization — its job, done correctly, with every bullet individually true — whereas 2d is the stage that actually assigns names and had the right one among its candidates. The post-Terra routing gap does not apply: the condition reached Terra, Terra supported it, and it was billed (disposition accepted_for_work, accepted true).

cases.attribution_rationale:
Premise confirmed on the photos. Both images show one small bathroom with real, warranted work: the sheet-vinyl floor is heavily yellowed and blotched at the tub edge and around the toilet, walls are scuffed and patched with an unfinished panel by the vanity, the baseboard/trim at the lower right doorway is damaged, and the frameless mirror is desilvered. What the photos do NOT show is the billed name: the one-piece fiberglass surround and the tub base are white and intact apart from mild dinginess at the base and caulk seam, and the toilet/sink porcelain is not heavily stained. The 2a prose did NOT introduce that name. cases.attribution_rationale:
Premise confirmed on my own reading of photo_017.jpg: the shower's wet-area enclosure is genuinely damaged — the tile wall is broken open at the valve location (rough, chipped penetration, no trim/escutcheon), there is a second damaged penetration at the bare shower-arm stub, and the mud pan and curb are eroded, spalled and chipped under heavy staining. That matches the claim text "tub surround or shower pan cracked, chipped, or damaged wet-area enclosure" and matches the v1.1 adjudication (claim=exact, work=warranted). The condition was projected (oc1_c00cb1e0f1fdb9da) and then unbilled with disposition=excluded / reason_code=verdict_unsupported, so it is a miss.

Walking the ladder: 2a DID contain the condition — the prose names the enclosure twice ("a questionable curb/pan condition", "a new properly waterproofed pan and surround") and separately notes "the shower valve/trim appears incomplete or damaged". What the prose did not contain was the literal words "cracked" or "chipped"; it hedged the enclosure as "questionable" and "heavily compromised", but the condition is unmistakably present, so 2a is not the failure. 2b emitted the matching bullet and joined it exactly (bullet_index 4, method exact). 2c kept it (p2c_present true); it dropped the sibling bullet "The shower curb and pan condition is questionable.", but that drop cost nothing because the surviving bullet carried the same condition forward. 2d resolved to tub_surround_or_shower_pan_damage — the bullet is phrased about valve/trim while the item is about the enclosure, which is the one arguable hop, but the human adjudicated the resulting claim as EXACT, so by the truth basis 2d resolved correctly and is not the first wrong stage. 2e kept the issue, and per the record 2e never cost a condition here. condition_projection produced the condition and it reached Terra.

Terra is therefore the first stage that went wrong: it returned "unsupported" with the rationale that only staining was visible and "no clear crack, chip, or enclosure damage is visible", which the photo contradicts — the surround is physically broken open at two wall penetrations and the pan/curb is chipped and degraded. Terra's rejection is what caused the unbilling (reason_code verdict_unsupported), so this is a Terra verdict error, not the known post-Terra routing/disposition gap (that gap applies only when Terra supported the condition).

alternative_stage_analysis.alters_eligibility_package_economics: No change is proposed, so nothing is altered. For the record, and as context only per the priority ruling: today's misnamings had no economic effect at all because work dedup absorbed both. At redfin_125779232 the misnamed FIXTURES_UPDATE item was suppressed into the one outdated_bathroom_finishes already drove (1092-10924 unchanged); at redfin_11000447 the two vanity conditions merged into one VANITY_REPLACE item (380-4563).
