alternative_stage_analysis.existing_item_exists: Yes for every unit. rc_6285e9a79e45: vinyl_linoleum_worn_or_stained (flooring, FLOORING_REPLACE) claims the floor, bathroom_paint_peeling_or_worn (paint_drywall, PAINT_INTERIOR) and wall_scuffs_marks_or_dents claim the wall/ceiling, and outdated_bathroom_finishes claims the dated package that the reviewer's own note ('more just extremely outdated and needing of refresh') describes. rc_e9d27cf6e9aa: vanity_damaged_or_water_stained claims 'water damage or broken components' on a bathroom vanity. rc_ace7463d6837: tub_surround_or_shower_pan_damage is itself the exact item and the human truth calls it exact/warranted.
alternative_stage_analysis.retrieved_but_2d_selected_other: Yes, and this is the primary cause. In rc_6285e9a79e45 four bullets naming three different building elements all collapsed onto bath_fixtures_stained_or_worn while better items sat in the same top-8: the floor bullet had vinyl_linoleum_worn_or_stained at rank 4 (and worn_or_stained_flooring at 2, floor_dirty_or_heavily_soiled at 3), the ceiling/wall bullet had bathroom_paint_peeling_or_worn at rank 2 and wall_scuffs_marks_or_dents at rank 3. Three of the four took the lexical_shortcut path; the fourth took the llm path and still chose the same item. In rc_ace7463d6837 2d chose correctly at rank 1. In rc_e9d27cf6e9aa the better item was not in the candidate list at all.
alternative_stage_analysis.scene_or_retrieval_metadata_cause: No. Scene resolved to bathroom on all three human units and scene_ok is true for every hypothesised better item in the reachability scan, including the ones that were kind-gated. All three implicated items carry scene_groups ['bathroom'] and no require_any that could have excluded these observations. Retrieval is exonerated positively rather than by default: it placed the better items inside the frozen top-8 on the two bullets where a better item existed and was of the right kind.
alternative_stage_analysis.steals_neighbors_or_damages_successes: Every lever considered would. Narrowing bath_fixtures_stained_or_worn's support_any or embed_text puts three human-verified positive uses at risk (rc_699d79f6ee07 'discolored cultured-marble tops with worn chrome faucets, a soiled shower pan and a dingy blue toilet', rc_d5cf0019df00 'the tub floor is brown-stained... all on undamaged fixtures', rc_ff9596f21e23 'blue-green staining across its basin... a dulled, worn surface'), and because support_any also feeds ranking and the annotator index the damage cannot be measured offline. Adding deny_any for floor/wall words would fire on the legitimate 'tub floor is brown-stained' wording in rc_d5cf0019df00. Adding require_any fixture nouns would not have blocked the two bad bullets, which both contain the word 'tub' as a location. Loosening vanity_worn_finish's intactness qualifier would steal from its own sibling, which is already doing the job. This is the decisive reason the cluster stays at no_change despite a met bar.
alternative_stage_analysis.terra_adjudicated_wrong_detail: Yes, twice, in opposite directions. rc_ace7463d6837 is a pure Terra error: the human truth is exact/warranted, tub_surround_or_shower_pan_damage ranked 1 and names the visible damage precisely, yet Terra returned unsupported ('no clear crack, chip, or enclosure damage is visible') against a photo showing a tile wall broken open at the valve and a chipped, eroded pan and curb, and the condition was excluded with reason_code verdict_unsupported - a lost real condition owned entirely by Terra. In the other direction Terra's supporting rationale on rc_6285e9a79e45 ('The tub surround and tub base show visible discoloration and worn-looking seams') overstates what the reviewer found on the surround, so Terra ratified rather than caught the 2d misnaming; and on rc_e9d27cf6e9aa Terra supported a claim whose 'on intact vanity' qualifier its own rationale ('dark deterioration along its exposed side edge') contradicts.
alternative_stage_analysis.upstream_kind_wrong: Partly, on one unit, and it cost nothing. For rc_e9d27cf6e9aa the 2c kind of the billed bullet was degradation, so the reachability scan shows vanity_damaged_or_water_stained (defect) with kind_ok false and rank null - genuinely unreachable for that bullet. But 2b had split one compound 2a sentence into two bullets and the defect-phrased sibling reached the exact item on the same photo in the same run, so the correct condition was billed anyway. The frozen attribution assigns this case to stage 2d; the reachability scan shows the exact item was not in that bullet's candidate set, so on the evidence the kind partition, not 2d, is the constraint - a correction to the frozen attribution that changes the stage story but not the outcome, since the correct billing happened regardless. For rc_6285e9a79e45 and rc_ace7463d6837 the kinds (degradation, defect) match the resolved items exactly (routing_reason exact_kind on every issue).
alternative_stage_analysis.wording_creates_unsupported_commitments: Yes, one real instance, and it is confined. vanity_worn_finish's atomic_claim commits to 'worn or faded finish on intact vanity'; at redfin_11000447 photo_008 the vanity is not intact (base/toe-kick missing, raw framing exposed), so the billed claim asserted an intactness the photo contradicts. That is a genuine unsupported commitment under convention 1, but it is not a catalog defect worth repairing here: the qualifier is exactly what separates this successor from its sibling vanity_damaged_or_water_stained, which fired correctly on the same photo. bath_fixtures_stained_or_worn's 'undamaged' qualifier is the mirror-image boundary against bath_fixtures_chipped_or_damaged and behaved correctly on all three of its reviewed positive uses. Neither item shows any promised_not_claimed or claimed_not_promised divergence in the scan.

cluster.claim_under_test: The photo shows a bathroom component (tub/shower surround or seams, bath fixtures, vanity cabinet body or toe-kick) whose visible deterioration or damage differs in component or mechanism from what the resolved catalog item claims.
cluster.merge_split_rationale: Pooled on the bathroom-component boundary within one trade bucket: after the reshape every unit is a bathroom_fixtures_tile component resolved to a sibling bathroom_fixtures_tile item, held together by one commitment type (the resolved item names a different component or a different mechanism than the photo shows). The provisional cluster additionally carried rc_eccd12ababc5 (redfin_11079485, 'The shower trim is old'), a plumbing-fixture observation resolved to dated_interior_trim in trade bucket trim_doors_windows; that is wrong-subject-across-families rather than wrong-component-within-family, so it moves to CAP-021 and takes dated_interior_trim with it (CAP-008 becomes that item's sole owner, so no worklist item loses a cluster). Never multiplied units: rc_6285e9a79e45 aggregates four observations into one condition and is counted once (convention 2).
cluster.physical_subject: bathroom tub/shower surround and seams, bath fixtures (tub, shower pan, toilet), and vanity cabinet body and toe-kick

reshape.rationale: The claim is narrowed from the provisional CAP-006 claim by dropping the 'shower valve/trim' branch: rc_eccd12ababc5 leaves for CAP-021 and dated_interior_trim leaves with it. All remaining units keep their original CAP-006 review rows and their reviewer verdicts are unchanged; the narrower claim is entailed by the pinned one, so every retained adjudication still answers the claim it was reviewed against. The recomputed bar survives the narrowing (two counted human supports on two distinct properties).

cluster.visible_state_or_mechanism: discolored, stained, worn, chipped, broken or detached bathroom components resolved to a catalog item whose named component (fixtures vs floor/wall finish) or mechanism (worn finish on an intact unit vs a broken or detached component) is not the one visible

controls.exclusion_rationale: These are the seven (not eight) dated_interior_trim control cards the provisional CAP-006 carried: two hallucination cards (rc_022497229bd3, rc_a0e75a18620e), one correct rejection (rc_73d15ca14405) and four positive uses (rc_9e889631af67, rc_ceeb17f8e242, rc_d0ffde500a92, and rc_57c6faf79c7e which the reviewer adjudicated unclear). They describe bedrooms, an enclosed porch, kitchens and a powder room, not bathrooms, and they belong to dated_interior_trim, which this reshape releases to CAP-008 as sole owner; CAP-008 already carries the identical seven cards. They are excluded because their item is no longer implicated here, not because their evidence is discounted. The five retained controls all sit on items this cluster still implicates: rc_699d79f6ee07, rc_d5cf0019df00 and rc_ff9596f21e23 (positive uses of bath_fixtures_stained_or_worn), rc_c95dacf421ce (positive use of vanity_worn_finish) and rc_61b0f2981ca9 (correct rejection on vanity_worn_finish).

coverage_gap.rationale: Every subject in this cluster already has a claiming item and, in the same frozen runs, most of them actually fired. The heavily stained sheet-vinyl floor at redfin_125779232 was separately billed as vinyl_linoleum_worn_or_stained (oc1_df18cf31cc724d4c, Terra supported, accepted_for_work); the wall/ceiling damage on the same photos was billed as damaged_drywall_or_cracks (oc1_e266d6e75396d96f) and wall_scuffs_marks_or_dents (oc1_9d02cb2ce9604fd4); the dated bathroom package was billed as outdated_bathroom_finishes (oc1_0283283b405edf5c). The vanity damage at redfin_11000447 was billed on the very same photo through vanity_damaged_or_water_stained (oc1_7a9ba957963d1492, Terra supported, accepted_for_work). The broken enclosure at redfin_125970550 resolved to tub_surround_or_shower_pan_damage at rank 1 and the human truth calls that name exact. Nothing in this cluster is an uncovered concept, so no coverage gap is declared and no split parent is needed.

diagnosis.catalog_ownership_argument: The catalog does not own this cluster, and I tested that conclusion rather than assuming it. (1) The divergence scan shows NO retrieval-vs-claim divergence for two of the three implicated items (bath_fixtures_stained_or_worn and vanity_worn_finish have empty promised_not_claimed and empty claimed_not_promised) and only 'moisture_rot' for tub_surround_or_shower_pan_damage. Unlike CAP-008 and CAP-013, there is no surface here that promises one thing to retrieval and commits to another at Terra. (2) The one genuinely catalog-owned surface I found is that bath_fixtures_stained_or_worn carries the bare adjectives 'stained' and 'worn' plus the location nouns 'tub$' and 'shower' in support_any, and that its embed_text advertises 'perimeter grime at shower pan or tub edges'. Three of the four bullets in rc_6285e9a79e45 resolved by resolution_path lexical_shortcut / shortcut_reason support_phrase_hit. That looks like a catalog lever until you read the code: tools/scene_classifier_passes.py builds the shortcut only for the ALREADY top-ranked candidate (a min-score and min-margin gate at lines 1101-1109 runs before _candidate_support_terms is consulted), so support_any did not select the item, it only skipped the LLM call for an item retrieval had already put at rank 1. The fourth bullet in the same case ('The toilet seat or toilet appears worn.') took the llm path with the same top-8 and chose bath_fixtures_stained_or_worn anyway. Deleting the generic tokens would therefore have handed these bullets to the same LLM that independently picked the same item; it would not recover the case it is built on, it cannot be verified offline (support_any is also a soft ranking hint and the annotator search index, and there is no offline embedding store), and it puts three human-verified positive uses of the item at risk (rc_699d79f6ee07, rc_d5cf0019df00, rc_ff9596f21e23, all exact/warranted and all phrased in exactly those words). Rejected as not the smallest lever and not a fix. (3) The second catalog-flavoured observation is vanity_worn_finish's atomic_claim qualifier 'on intact vanity', which redfin_11000447 photo_008 falsifies (base/toe-kick missing, raw framing exposed) while Terra supported it anyway. Removing that qualifier would broaden vanity_worn_finish across the boundary the 3.x split deliberately drew against its sibling vanity_damaged_or_water_stained - and that sibling already fired correctly on the same photo, so the broadening would buy nothing and would make an over-claim easier. Rejected. (4) What remains is a 2d selection failure with the better item reachable (rc_6285e9a79e45), a kind-gate that cost nothing because the exact item fired on the sibling bullet (rc_e9d27cf6e9aa), and a plain Terra error on a correctly named item (rc_ace7463d6837). Per the 2026-09-03 scope direction, a 2d selection failure is never compensated by editing the catalog; it becomes a pass_2d_follow_ups entry with the catalog unchanged.

rejected_alternative_owners.why: Pass 2a named every component correctly and at the right strength in all three human units: at redfin_125779232 it assigned heavy staining to the floor and only hedged 'somewhat worn/discolored' for the surround; at redfin_11000447 it emitted both the general wear and the open toe-kick; at redfin_125970550 it named the damaged valve/trim and the questionable pan. No 2a error to attribute, and 2a is frozen and out of scope regardless.

All 128 items were searched. Every mis-billed subject here has a claiming item and in each case that item was actually used somewhere in the same frozen run (vinyl_linoleum_worn_or_stained, damaged_drywall_or_cracks, wall_scuffs_marks_or_dents, outdated_bathroom_finishes, vanity_damaged_or_water_stained). Coverage is present; selection is what failed.

Scene was bathroom on every unit and scene_ok is true for every hypothesised better item in the reachability scan. Retrieval put the better items inside the frozen top-8 for the two mis-selected bullets (vinyl_linoleum_worn_or_stained rank 4 on the floor bullet, bathroom_paint_peeling_or_worn rank 2 and wall_scuffs_marks_or_dents rank 3 on the wall bullet), so retrieval delivered the right candidates and 2d passed over them.

Checked directly in the frozen artifacts and the downstream behaved correctly, indeed it absorbed both misnamings. At redfin_125779232 the misnamed condition's FIXTURES_UPDATE work item (wk1_0a432a2287bfbd24) was suppressed as dedup_collision into wk1_c8ce56fe056d7138, which outdated_bathroom_finishes already drove at 1092-10924. At redfin_11000447 both vanity conditions merged into one active VANITY_REPLACE work item (wk1_1b9a56a0ba5affbe, 380-4563) with both per-condition items suppressed as dedup_collision. Dollar effects are context only, but this rules the downstream out as an owner.
All three implicated items bill (bills=true, route work, tier work) in trade bathroom_fixtures_tile, which is not the quarantined trade (electrical is). No quarantine rule applies.

Considered because vanity_worn_finish, vanity_damaged_or_water_stained and vanity_dated_style are three successors of one legacy parent split across three kinds, and a degradation-phrased bullet can never reach the defect successor. Rejected as the owner for this cluster because the split demonstrably worked on this very photo: the defect-phrased sibling bullet reached vanity_damaged_or_water_stained, Terra supported it, it was accepted for work, and it deduped with the misnamed condition into a single VANITY_REPLACE work item. The ontology cost a display name, not a condition. Recorded as an unresolved question for the program rather than a defect of this cluster.

evidence_bar_claim.conflict_note: Mandatory and supplied: this cluster has mixed human signal. Two human support units were adjudicated supports_claim and one human support unit, rc_ace7463d6837, was adjudicated refuted. The conflict is real but structured, not noise. The refutation is confined to tub_surround_or_shower_pan_damage: on redfin_125970550 photo_017 the reviewer found the resolved item names the visible damage exactly ('the tiled shower enclosure is broken open at the valve... which is exactly the cracked/chipped/damaged wet-area enclosure the resolved item claims'), so on that unit there is no component or mechanism mismatch at all - the failure is Terra's rejection of a correct claim. The two supporting units concern different items (bath_fixtures_stained_or_worn, vanity_worn_finish) and a different failure, so the refutation does not contradict them; it constrains the cluster's reach. I treat it as decisive against any proposal touching tub_surround_or_shower_pan_damage - the reviewed evidence on that item says the catalog is right and the verifier was wrong - and it reinforces the no_change outcome rather than undermining the bar. The adjudication itself is untouched: refuted stays refuted.
evidence_bar_claim.correlation_note: Not required (two distinct properties, redfin_125779232 and redfin_11000447, with no shared photo, condition or run). Recorded for completeness: the only same-property pairing anywhere in the cluster is the refuted human unit and one model lead on redfin_125970550 photo_017, and neither of those counts toward the bar, so no correlated evidence inflates the count.
evidence_bar_claim.justification: Counting only role=support units adjudicated exactly supports_claim: rc_6285e9a79e45 (runtime:canary:redfin_125779232:...:oc1_7369dbd37bee24fd, evidence_class human_review, independent true) and rc_e9d27cf6e9aa (runtime:canary:redfin_11000447:...:oc1_4f0058d96b06f3a3, evidence_class human_review, independent true). Two human units on two distinct properties gives two_independent_human. The third support unit, rc_ace7463d6837 (redfin_125970550), is human but adjudicated refuted, so it does not count toward the bar and instead supplies the cluster's one reviewed refutation with photos available. The four model_judge units (redfin_10806500, redfin_10952874, redfin_11185681, redfin_125970550/oc1_562dd1da5b0d9252) are context and count for nothing; no conclusion here rests on them. The provisional digest recomputed three human supports on three properties because it still contained rc_eccd12ababc5; after that unit moves to CAP-021 the bar is unchanged at two_independent_human. Recomputed counts for the tool to match: counted_support_units 2, human 2, leads_counted 0, distinct_properties 2, reviewed_refutations 1, mixed_signal true.

human_inputs.effect: rc_6285e9a79e45's four aggregated observations count as exactly one support unit, which is why the bar is two and not five. It also means the aggregation itself is judged as a single naming failure rather than four.
human_inputs.ruling: Judge multi-photo and multi-issue conditions at the characteristic issue level and never multiply units: several issues on one condition are one evidence unit.

human_inputs.effect: Forced the surface-by-surface test that produced the finding that no divergence exists on these items, and identified vanity_worn_finish's 'on intact vanity' as a claim-side commitment falsified by the photo - recorded, not repaired.
human_inputs.ruling: Terra sees only the atomic_claim; name/description/embed_text/support_any are what 2d and retrieval see, and it matters which surface failed.

human_inputs.effect: rc_6285e9a79e45's two mis-selected bullets become pass_2d follow-ups with the catalog untouched; this is the single largest driver of the no_change outcome.
human_inputs.ruling: For an imperfect mapping decide right-item-unavailable versus right-item-reachable-but-another-selected; the second is a pass_2d_follow_ups entry and the catalog usually stays unchanged. Never compensate for a 2d selection failure by broadening the catalog.

human_inputs.effect: Governing precedent applied here: reachable-better-item cases are 2d questions, so this cluster declares no coverage gap despite a met bar.
human_inputs.ruling: Deck weathering is real but the right existing concept was reachable, so treat it as a 2d specificity question, not missing coverage.

human_inputs.effect: Confirms the condition is a dated-package condition, which outdated_bathroom_finishes already billed on that property and which deduped with the misnamed fixtures item - the basis for calling the harm a naming-level false positive rather than a lost condition.
human_inputs.ruling: 'The wear is overstated. It is more just extremely outdated and needing of refresh.'

human_inputs.effect: Confirms the correct rejection on vanity_worn_finish was right, and is direct evidence against loosening that item's intactness qualifier.
human_inputs.ruling: 'The vanity is just opened. Its not unfinished.'

human_inputs.effect: The work-dedup findings (both misnamings absorbed at zero dollar cost) are reported as context and are not used to justify the outcome; the outcome rests on the fact that no catalog edit would remove a false billing or recover the one lost condition.
human_inputs.ruling: Judge on fewer hallucinations and fewer lost real conditions; dollar effects are context only.
human_inputs.source: Steven (fewer hallucinations, fewer lost conditions; dollars are context)

pass_2d_follow_ups.note: Observation 'The floor has discoloration and staining around the tub and vanity.' (redfin_125779232 photo_007, kind degradation, scene bathroom) resolved to bath_fixtures_stained_or_worn by lexical_shortcut/support_phrase_hit while three flooring items sat in the same frozen top-8 (worn_or_stained_flooring 2, floor_dirty_or_heavily_soiled 3, vinyl_linoleum_worn_or_stained 4, all kind_ok and scene_ok). The reviewer identifies the yellowed blotched sheet vinyl as the genuinely deteriorated component. The correct item was in fact selected for the sibling floor bullets on the same two photos and billed (oc1_df18cf31cc724d4c), so 2d had the answer and used it elsewhere in the same run. Note for the 2d owner: support_phrase_hit only fires on the already top-ranked candidate, so the fix is selection or ranking, not the support list.

Observation 'The ceiling and wall area near the tub look rough.' (redfin_125779232 photo_007) resolved to bath_fixtures_stained_or_worn by lexical_shortcut/support_phrase_hit with bathroom_paint_peeling_or_worn at rank 2 and wall_scuffs_marks_or_dents at rank 3, both kind_ok and scene_ok. The word 'tub' appears only as a location in the observation. The wall condition was independently billed on the same property via damaged_drywall_or_cracks and wall_scuffs_marks_or_dents, so again nothing was lost - the cost is one extra condition billed under the wrong subject. Same aggregation event as the entry above: four bullets naming three building elements were bound to one condition.

proposal.economics_fit: Unchanged. All three items keep bills=true, route work, tier work, trade bathroom_fixtures_tile; work_item_codes stay FIXTURES_UPDATE, VANITY_REPLACE and TUB_SHOWER_REPAIR; no economics field is authorable in any case.
proposal.expected_benefit: None claimed from the catalog, which is the point of this outcome. The benefit of the judgment is negative-space: it removes three tempting but wrong levers from the program's candidate list with a mechanical reason for each (support_any cannot select an item it did not already rank first - tools/scene_classifier_passes.py lines 1101-1109; loosening vanity_worn_finish's intactness qualifier steals from a sibling that already fired on the same photo; there is no negative control on any of these items against which a broadening could be proved safe), and it routes the two real defects to their owners: two pass_2d follow-ups and one Terra verdict error (rc_ace7463d6837), which is the only lost real condition in the cluster.
proposal.package_route_effects: None. bath_fixtures_stained_or_worn stays package_support in bathroom_repair, vanity_worn_finish and tub_surround_or_shower_pan_damage stay package_driver in bathroom_repair, and no route_override is proposed. Observed in the frozen runs and reported as context only: today's two misnamed conditions both deduped into work items that a correctly named condition already drove, so package economics were already unaffected.
proposal.product_policy: Not applicable. No implicated item sits in the product-quarantined electrical trade; all three are bathroom_fixtures_tile and all three bill under work_default.

regression_controls.note: Positive use of bath_fixtures_stained_or_worn (redfin_126224899). No change proposed, so nothing can flip; listed to record that any future narrowing of this item must keep it supported.

Positive use of bath_fixtures_stained_or_worn (redfin_11079485 photo_005). Unchanged. Doubles as the proof that the CAP-021 fixture condition was billed correctly on the same property through the right item.

Positive use of bath_fixtures_stained_or_worn (redfin_10740044). Unchanged. Its reviewer text ('staining across its basin... a dulled, worn surface') is exactly the wording a support_any narrowing would have endangered.
Positive use of vanity_worn_finish (redfin_10806500 photo_006), peeling chipped laminate on an intact cabinet body - the item working exactly as its claim says. Unchanged.

Correct rejection on vanity_worn_finish (redfin_10952874 photo_032), reviewer-refuted, i.e. the rejection was right. Unchanged, and it is the direct evidence against removing the 'on intact vanity' qualifier.

proposal.regression_risk: Zero by construction - no file changes, no item diff, no order change. The risk this outcome accepts is the opposite one: if the lead later concludes that bath_fixtures_stained_or_worn's breadth is worth attacking, that work must be done in the retrieval lane with an online harness and the three positive-use controls as its regression set, not as a decisions-file edit justified by this cluster.
proposal.retrieval_effects: None, by construction. No embed_text, name, description, support_any, deny_any or require_any is touched, so no item's rank changes anywhere. This is deliberate: bath_fixtures_stained_or_worn's rank-1 dominance across bathroom wear bullets is real but unmeasurable offline (no embedding store), and every candidate edit to its retrieval surface risked three human-verified positive uses without recovering the case that motivated it.
proposal.semantic_before_after: No catalog change is proposed, so no item's semantics change. Recorded for the reconciliation: bath_fixtures_stained_or_worn keeps atomic_claim {subject: 'bath fixtures', state: 'heavy staining or worn finish, undamaged', ontology_basis: visible_deterioration}; vanity_worn_finish keeps 'worn or faded finish on intact vanity'; tub_surround_or_shower_pan_damage keeps 'cracked, chipped, or damaged wet-area enclosure'. All three are left exactly as they are because the reviewed evidence says each names its own subject correctly and the failures happened at selection and verification.

unresolved_questions: Retrieval-lane question deferred out of the catalog: bath_fixtures_stained_or_worn is rank 1 for almost any bathroom wear bullet in the corpus - it took rank 1 on all four bullets of rc_6285e9a79e45 and on every issue of all four model leads, including bullets about ceilings, caulk, grout, shower glass and a curb. That is an embedding-rank concentration, not a claim defect, and there is no offline embedding store to test a fix against. If a future session gets an online retrieval harness, the experiment is to test whether trimming the bare adjectives 'stained'/'worn' and the location nouns 'tub$'/'shower' from support_any and the 'perimeter grime' clause from embed_text changes rank at all, with rc_699d79f6ee07, rc_d5cf0019df00 and rc_ff9596f21e23 as the regression set. Not proposable now.

Program-level ontology question (crosses into CAP-015): the vanity trio and the cabinets pair are split across kinds, so a degradation-phrased bullet can structurally never reach the defect successor. Here it cost nothing because 2b's sibling bullet carried the defect phrasing and reached the right item. Whether that redundancy is reliable, or whether it silently drops the exact item whenever 2b happens not to emit a defect-phrased sibling, is not answerable from this cluster's four counted units.

The frozen attribution for rc_e9d27cf6e9aa records stage 2d, but the reachability scan shows vanity_damaged_or_water_stained was kind-gated out of that bullet's candidate set entirely (kind_ok false, rank null). I record the discrepancy rather than resolving it; it does not change the outcome, since the exact item was billed from the sibling bullet on the same photo either way. The lead may want this reflected in the error-attribution record.

rc_6285e9a79e45 collapsed four distinct observations into a single condition. Whether 2d should ever bind more than one bullet to one condition is a pipeline-policy question outside this cluster's scope; it is the mechanism that made this misnaming possible and it will recur independent of any catalog wording.

gold.attribution_rationale: This is exactly the known ladder gap, and I am answering unclear for that reason rather than from uncertainty about the facts. Every rung is affirmatively ruled out by the record: 2a saw it ('Window and exterior door: both look older and may be drafty'); 2b produced 'The window appears older.'; 2c kept it (survivor, issue 0e028fcb40afa1e3); 2d resolved it correctly to dated_or_older_windows; a condition was projected (oc1_d3e7cd176d2f8dd6); and Terra did NOT reject it - terra_verdict is 'supported' with the rationale 'The window has an older-style frame and blinds.' The condition nonetheless ends accepted=false with disposition 'no_action' and reason_code 'route_no_action'. The loss therefore happens in post-Terra routing/disposition, which sits after every stage the ladder covers. Note the 2e temptation to be resisted: this issue is absent from p2e.kept_issue_ids and the photo carries tier_optional_suppressed=3, but the door issue in that same suppressed set was billed anyway, so 2e is not the responsible stage - the record's own rule and the local counter-example agree.

cases.attribution_rationale: Premise holds, though marginally: the photo shows plain white builder-grade horizontal mini-blinds in flat white casing on the bathroom window, which is a defensible read as a dated window treatment worth replacing, and 2a independently called it out. I do not overturn the human. Ruling out pass_2a: the 2a prose DOES contain the real condition verbatim ("Good natural light is a plus, but the blind and window trim look dated"). What the 2a prose does NOT contain anywhere is any mention of a valance, cornice, swag, or curtain — it speaks only of a blind and window trim, and the photo confirms no valance exists on that window. 2b joined the observation exactly as bullet 18 ("Window blind and trim appear dated.") and 2c kept it in p2c_surviving, so neither of those stages lost anything. 2e is not available: p2e_status is "absent" with one tier_optional_suppressed, but the issue still produced projected_condition_id oc1_bd04d765dac55f9b, so nothing was lost there. The condition did reach Terra and Terra did NOT support it (disposition excluded, reason_code verdict_unsupported), so the post-Terra routing gap does not apply. The first stage that actually went wrong is 2d: it resolved a blind-and-trim observation to dated_window_treatment_valance, an item whose defining feature is a valance that neither the prose nor the pixels contain. Terra's rejection rationale ("The windows show plain horizontal blinds, with no dated valance visible") is factually correct against the photo — Terra did not misread anything; it correctly refused a claim about a feature that is not in the room. The false framing entered at 2d, before Terra, so Terra is the second failure and not the first. Held to medium rather than higher because the item's claim text does say "or treatments", which leaves a defensible alternative reading in which the item legitimately covers blinds and Terra is responsible for fixating on the valance prong; the v1_only truth basis and the borderline "dated"-ness of plain mini-blinds also argue against more confidence.

absence_statements.correct_rejections: Three reviewed correct rejections exist, all adjudicated refuted by the Phase B reviewer in agreement with Terra. On dated_window_treatment_valance: rc_4f4b93c40ef3 (redfin_25809814 photo_023, plain white roller shade and mini-blind, no valance) and rc_ffad088fa5fe (redfin_80925528 photo_005, plain straight intact mini-blinds, no valance) - both reached Terra as blinds-only observations and both were excluded with reason_code verdict_unsupported. On dated_or_older_windows: rc_64f996e3a886 (redfin_11000447 photo_001, white vinyl replacement windows). All three have regression_controls entries.
absence_statements.counterexamples: The cluster is refutation-backed and the counterexamples are the strongest part of the record. Counting reviewed exposures of dated_window_treatment_valance: four of five are blinds-only and the reviewer refuted all four - rc_a22a241b3bf0 (a human_review support unit adjudicated refuted), rc_4f4b93c40ef3 (also the role=context model-judge unit), rc_ffad088fa5fe, and hallucination control rc_429ba6851d09. Only rc_429ba6851d09 got past Terra, and it billed. So the item's reviewed record is two billings, one of which is a hallucination. There is no reviewed case in which routing blinds to no_action would suppress a condition the reviewer judged billable - the only such case, rc_7c5b9f9bb3aa, is billable on its fabric prong, which the proposal deliberately keeps on a billing route.
absence_statements.success_uses: Controls were checked and are NOT absent for dated_window_treatment_valance: it has exactly one reviewed positive use, rc_7c5b9f9bb3aa (redfin_81000709 photo_003), adjudicated supports_claim, human truth claim 'exact' / work 'warranted' / class_v1_1 'supported_billed', disposition accepted_for_work. That single card is the entire reviewed billable population of the valance/curtain concept, and it survives on the fabric prong (a red holiday-print cloth hung as a makeshift curtain) rather than on its blinds. dated_or_older_windows has ZERO positive uses, and structurally can never have one: it carries neither cost nor work_item_code, so resolve_terminal_route returns ('no_action','no_economics_approved_gap') for every instance of it - it is a detect-only item by approved policy, not by defect. No op touches it.

alternative_stage_analysis.alters_eligibility_package_economics: No. The dry run's added_detail shows both successors at pricing_status 'inherited_from_split_parent' with the parent's economics byte-identical: cost {mode: heuristic}, work_item_code WINDOW_TREATMENT_UPDATE, estimate null, cost_model null, package_affinity null, package_role 'ignore', estimate_scope null; tier stays optional, trade_bucket stays trim_doors_windows, and repair_support_marker_routes is empty for both, so neither drives nor supports a rehab package. Nothing is repriced and no economic field is authored - which is required, since economics are never authorable. The only economic consequence is routing: resolve_terminal_route returns ('no_action','route_override_no_action') for the blinds successor, making its inherited economics inert, and ('work','work_default') for the fabric successor, identical to the parent today. route_override is legal here precisely because the successor inherits a work_item_code - the validator rejects route_override on an item with neither cost nor work_item_code as redundant.
alternative_stage_analysis.existing_item_exists: Yes. All 128 items were searched: dated_window_treatment_valance is the catalog's only window-treatment item and it already covers both blinds and valance/curtains; dated_or_older_windows covers the window unit itself. Nothing here is uncovered. There is no wear-kind window-treatment item, which is why g4's wear-classified blinds bullet found nothing.
alternative_stage_analysis.retrieved_but_2d_selected_other: No for the over-bill lane; yes but harmless for one gold unit. On rc_a22a241b3bf0 and rc_4f4b93c40ef3 the LLM took rank-1 dated_window_treatment_valance and the reviewer records that no candidate on either list fits. On g7 the bullet 'The window appears older.' resolved by lexical_shortcut to dated_or_older_windows (rank 1) with dated_window_treatment_valance at rank 2, so the shortcut pre-empted an LLM choice that could have named the valance - but Terra supported the window reading and the reviewer confirms the wood window really is old, so no harm is demonstrated on that photo. It is filed as a pass_2d_follow_up, not as grounds for a change.
alternative_stage_analysis.scene_or_retrieval_metadata_cause: Scene gating is not a cause: reachability_scan shows kind_ok and scene_ok true for both implicated items on every issue, and the item is valid in all five interior scene groups. Retrieval metadata IS a cause. support_any contains the bare token 'blinds', and two of five reviewed exposures resolved by lexical_shortcut / support_phrase_hit on it, bypassing LLM selection entirely (_resolve_candidate_via_lexical_shortcut in tools/scene_classifier_passes.py resolves the top candidate outright when any support term matches the observation). embed_text compounds it by advertising basic/worn/bent/damaged mini blinds - three concepts divergence_scan lists as promised_not_claimed.
alternative_stage_analysis.steals_neighbors_or_damages_successes: Neighbours: no. The frozen co-listed neighbours are dated_overall_decor_style, dated_or_older_windows, dated_wood_paneling, dated_interior_trim, dated_electrical_outlets_switches, ceiling_fan_blades_mismatched, mismatched_or_inconsistent_furniture_staging, outdated_bathroom_finishes, dated_lighting_fixtures, paint_refresh_recommended. Neither successor's text reaches those subjects, both keep the parent's scene_groups, and both retain the parent's glazing deny terms (broken window / fogged window / failed seal) so neither annexes glazing defects. Successes: one real exposure. rc_7c5b9f9bb3aa is the item's only human-approved billing and it is a MIXED photo (yellowed bent mini-blinds AND a red holiday-print cloth hung as a makeshift curtain). If 2d sends it to the blinds successor it is detected but routed no_action and the approved billing is lost. The blinds successor's deny_any on valance/curtain/drape terms is designed to force exactly that case to the fabric successor - deny_any is a hard guardrail matched against the observation text in CatalogEmbeddingsRetriever._passes_guardrails - but the card is a v1.1 label with no stored 2b bullet in the frozen bundle, so I cannot confirm offline that its observation names the cloth. This is the proposal's single largest risk and it is stated as such rather than assumed away.
alternative_stage_analysis.terra_adjudicated_wrong_detail: Yes on one card, and it is a symptom of the claim, not an independent Terra fault. Shown 'window treatments dated valance or treatments' against four visually equivalent blinds-only photos, Terra answered unsupported three times ('The windows show plain horizontal blinds, with no dated valance visible.') and supported once ('The window has visible horizontal blinds that appear dated.' - rc_429ba6851d09, which then billed). Both answers are defensible readings of a disjunction whose second prong any window covering satisfies.
alternative_stage_analysis.upstream_kind_wrong: Partly, on one unit, and NOT fixed here. g4's bullet 'Window blinds are worn.' was carried as a wear/degradation-family observation and its entire frozen candidate list was wear items (door_hardware_worn, wall_scuffs_marks_or_dents, vinyl_linoleum_worn_or_stained, floor_dirty_or_heavily_soiled, peeling_or_discolored_paint, baseboard_wear_scuffs); dated_window_treatment_valance had rank null because it is modernization. Both proposed successors remain modernization, so that bullet would still resolve to nothing. Under convention 5 the blinds half is not billable anyway, so this is recorded, not repaired. For all four over-bill cards the kind was modernization and correct.
alternative_stage_analysis.wording_creates_unsupported_commitments: Yes, in both directions. The Terra surface commits to a valance-or-treatment subject with an unqualified 'dated' state, which cannot separate a builder-grade blind from a vintage valance; the retrieval surface commits to plain/basic, wear, and damage states that the atomic claim never states (divergence_scan promised_not_claimed = damage_break, plain_basic, wear_scuff). That mismatch between the two surfaces is exactly the convention-1 defect.

cluster.claim_under_test: The photo shows dated, bent, partial, or damaged window blinds/treatments (not a valance, and not the window unit), and the resolved catalog item commits to a valance (dated_window_treatment_valance) or to the window itself (dated_or_older_windows).
cluster.merge_split_rationale: Kept pooled with all four reviewed units and both items; the allocated id CAP-020 is deliberately unused. The prior hypothesis that CAP-007 pools two failures is CORRECT on the facts - an over-bill lane (ordinary intact blinds recruited onto a valance-committed item) and a loss lane (real treatment-level findings landing on the window item or on nothing) - but partitioning them destroys the analysis. The two gold units at redfin_11000447 are the family's only supports_claim evidence, so every partition leaves each resulting cluster at bar `none`, and bar `none` forecloses a native_decisions_proposal. Pooled, the two lanes are the two halves of one defect and a fix needs both: the refutations plus hallucination control rc_429ba6851d09 show the item over-reaching onto blinds, g7 and positive-use control rc_7c5b9f9bb3aa show the valance/curtain concept is real and billable, and g4 shows blinds-only conditions exist with no valance at all. The claim wording is kept verbatim from the reviewed Phase B packet because all four adjudications were made against that exact string; the blinds-vs-valance framing lives in the diagnosis, not in a rewritten claim.

coverage_gap.rationale: No coverage gap is declared. Every one of the 128 items in digest/items.json was searched for blind / curtain / drape / shade / valance: dated_window_treatment_valance is the only window-treatment item and it already spans both subjects, so the blinds concept is over-covered (covered by an item that bills) rather than uncovered. The one place where nothing was reachable is g4's bullet 'Window blinds are worn.', which 2c classified into the wear family; its whole frozen candidate list was wear/degradation items and the only treatment item is modernization, so it resolved to no item. That is a kind-availability question, it is NOT fixed by this proposal (both successors stay modernization), and under Steven's convention 5 nothing billable is lost by it, so it is documentation rather than a gap to fill. The proposal does add a catalog item, but as a successor of a legitimate split of an existing conflated item - not to fill an absence.

diagnosis.catalog_ownership_argument: dated_window_treatment_valance is one item spanning two subjects whose billability Steven has ruled differently. Its Terra surface is the disjunction 'window treatments dated valance or treatments', whose second prong is satisfied by any window covering; its 2d/retrieval surface goes further and advertises 'Basic or builder-grade mini blinds ... Aged, bent, or damaged mini blinds', with support_any carrying the bare token 'blinds'. divergence_scan records exactly that gap: promised_not_claimed = [damage_break, plain_basic, wear_scuff]. Both surfaces are catalog fields, so under convention 1 this is catalog-owned, and the record shows it doing measurable damage. Five reviewed exposures of the item exist. Four are blinds-only and the Phase B reviewer refuted all four (rc_a22a241b3bf0, rc_4f4b93c40ef3, rc_ffad088fa5fe, rc_429ba6851d09). On two of them (rc_429ba6851d09, rc_ffad088fa5fe) resolution never reached the 2d LLM at all: resolution_path is lexical_shortcut with shortcut_reason support_phrase_hit, fired by the item's own support_any token 'blinds'. Terra then split on visually identical facts, returning unsupported three times ('no dated valance visible') and supported once - and that once, rc_429ba6851d09, ended accepted=true, disposition accepted_for_work, reason_code route_work. That is a billed hallucination whose entry point is a catalog keyword and whose survival is a catalog claim ambiguity. The fifth exposure, rc_7c5b9f9bb3aa, is the item's only human-approved billing and it turns on a fabric prong (a cloth hung as a makeshift curtain), which is the branch Steven left open. So the item is simultaneously over-reaching on blinds and carrying a genuine valance/curtain concept - the definition of a conflated item, and the shape a split resolves.

rejected_alternative_owners.why: On the two LLM-path over-bill cases the model picked the rank-1 candidate and no better item existed on the frozen list - the reviewer says so for both ('No candidate fits'; dated_or_older_windows at rank 5 does not fit a blinds observation). On the other two over-bill cases 2d never chose at all: a catalog support_any token short-circuited it. Broadening or re-ranking cannot fix a list on which the correct answer does not exist.

2a is frozen and, for the over-bill lane, 2a is defensibly right: it reported blinds that really are basic ('The window and blinds are dated.', 'The blinds are older.'). What makes those unbillable is convention 3 and convention 5, which are catalog-side policy, not observation errors. The one genuine 2a miss in this cluster is g7's unnamed valance and winterizing sheeting, and that half is explicitly excluded from this proposal.

This IS the true owner of the two gold units' dollar loss, and the proposal does not claim otherwise. Both gold conditions were Terra-supported and then ended accepted=false / disposition no_action / reason_code route_no_action on dated_or_older_windows, which resolve_terminal_route reports as ('no_action','no_economics_approved_gap') because the item carries neither cost nor work_item_code. Economics are never authorable in the decisions file, so no catalog change recovers those dollars. It is recorded as a non-catalog follow-up; it is not the cluster's primary cause because it does not explain the over-bill lane the ops act on.
The blinds subject is covered today - by an item that bills it. The defect is conflation, not absence, so this is a split of an existing item and not a coverage gap; see coverage_gap.rationale.

Terra's 3-1 inconsistency on identical blinds-only photos is real but derivative: every one of its rationales is a defensible reading of the string it was shown. Convention 1 assigns an unstable claim to the catalog surface that authored it.

evidence_bar_claim.conflict_note: REQUIRED and supplied: mixed_signal is true because the support units contain both human/gold supports_claim (g7, g4) and a human/gold refutation (rc_a22a241b3bf0). The two directions are not in factual conflict - they are the same object conflation seen from opposite sides. The gold pair records real treatment-level conditions that the resolved item did not name (it named the window unit, or nothing); rc_a22a241b3bf0 records ordinary intact mini-blinds pulled onto a valance-committed item that Terra then correctly refused. Both say the item boundary sits in the wrong place. Note also that rc_a22a241b3bf0's older v1 truth (v1_verdict terra_claim_supported) disagrees with the Phase B reviewer, who refuted it; Steven's convention 6 reconciliation settles it explicitly - 'rc_a22a241b3bf0 ordinary mini-blinds = not billed' - so the Phase B adjudication and the convention agree, and the stale v1 label is superseded, not overturned by me.
evidence_bar_claim.correlation_note: REQUIRED and supplied: both counted units are gold rows on the single property redfin_11000447, from one run (20260817_224602_d422d7ae), so distinct_properties = 1. They are not duplicates of one another - photo_004 is a kitchen window with a brown fabric valance plus taped winterizing sheeting, photo_005 is a bay-window bedroom with three sets of yellowed venetian blinds and explicitly no valance - so they are two different rooms, two different windows and two different treatment types, but they share one house's age and decorating habits and must not be read as two independent properties. Two counterweights are worth recording. First, the same property also supplies correct-rejection control rc_64f996e3a886 (its facade's vinyl replacement windows, Terra unsupported, reviewer refuted), so the property is not uniformly 'everything here is old'. Second, and more important, the correlated pair is NOT what the ops act on: the over-bill lane the split actually repairs is evidenced on four other and mutually distinct properties - redfin_10803207 (rc_a22a241b3bf0), redfin_25809814 (rc_4f4b93c40ef3), redfin_80925528 (rc_ffad088fa5fe) and redfin_11185681 (rc_429ba6851d09, the billed hallucination). The proposal therefore does not rest on the single-property pair alone, even though the formal bar does.
evidence_bar_claim.justification: Recounted by hand from the pinned adjudications. Three units carry role 'support'. Exactly two are adjudicated supports_claim: gold:redfin_11000447:photo_004.jpg:g7 and gold:redfin_11000447:photo_005.jpg:g4, both evidence_class gold_reference with independent true, both photos available. The third support unit (runtime:canary:redfin_10803207:...:oc1_bd04d765dac55f9b, human_review, case rc_a22a241b3bf0) is adjudicated refuted and therefore does not count. The fourth unit is role 'context' and evidence_class model_judge (the factorized lead on case rc_4f4b93c40ef3); it is excluded twice over and grounds nothing. So human = 2, leads = 0, and two or more human units gives two_independent_human. reviewed_refutations = 1 (rc_a22a241b3bf0, human, photos available), lead_refutations = 0, distinct_properties among counted units = 1. This matches digest/index.json (bar two_independent_human, human 2, lead 0, props 1, refutations 1, mixed_signal true) and the digest's evidence_bar_recomputed block exactly.

human_inputs.effect: This is the whole shape of the proposal. It rules out narrowing the item in place (that would suppress valances and curtains) and rules out simply deleting the blinds language (that would end detectability). A split with route_override no_action on the blinds successor is the only shape satisfying both halves, and route_override is authorable only on a split successor.
human_inputs.ruling: Blinds stay detectable but must be a no_action catalog condition; the ruling is about blinds only, valances and curtains remain open, and the current dated_window_treatment_valance item combines those subjects, so the blinds ruling must not be applied silently to the whole item.

human_inputs.effect: Keeps g7's unnamed valance/sheeting (a 2a miss) and g7's lexical-shortcut resolution (a 2d question) out of the ops, and keeps the post-Terra routing loss as a non-catalog follow-up rather than something the catalog is asked to repair.
human_inputs.ruling: Catalog-first; Pass 2a is frozen; Pass 2d is deferred not fixed here; never compensate for a 2d selection failure by broadening the catalog.

pass_2d_follow_ups.note: resolution_path lexical_shortcut / support_phrase_hit fired on dated_or_older_windows' bare support_any tokens 'window' and 'windows', pre-empting LLM selection while dated_window_treatment_valance sat at rank 2 and would have named the brown fabric valance the reviewer sees. Logged as a follow-up only: on THIS photo the shortcut's output was Terra-supported and correct (the wood single-hung really is old), so no harm is demonstrated inside this cluster and I am not proposing a change to that item's support_any. Worth watching because the same bare-token shortcut pattern also drove two of the over-bill cards on the other item.

proposal.economics_fit: No economic field is authored; economics are never authorable, and the dry run confirms none moved. Both successors take the split_successor_pricing policy 'inherit_parent_economics_v1' and come out with pricing_status 'inherited_from_split_parent', cost {mode: heuristic}, work_item_code WINDOW_TREATMENT_UPDATE, estimate null, cost_model null, package_affinity null, package_role 'ignore', estimate_scope null, tier optional, trade_bucket trim_doors_windows, category opportunity, display_class marketability - all inherited verbatim from dated_window_treatment_valance. The blinds successor's inherited economics are inert because route_override precedes the costing route. Retaining that work_item_code is not cosmetic: tools/catalog_validation.py rejects route_override on an item with neither cost nor work_item_code as redundant, so the inheritance is what makes the no_action override legal. Precedent is exact - landscaping_enhancement_opportunity is a split successor of landscape_improvement_needed carrying route_override no_action over an inherited LANDSCAPE_CLEANUP work code.
proposal.expected_benefit: Concrete and bounded. (1) The one reviewed billed hallucination on this item, rc_429ba6851d09 (Terra supported 'ordinary white mini-blinds, half raised and intact, with no valance'; accepted=true, disposition accepted_for_work, reason_code route_work), stops billing, because every blinds retrieval token now belongs to a no_action successor. On the reviewed record that halves this item's billings and removes the false one. (2) Convention 5 becomes true in the catalog rather than aspirational: blinds remain detectable and displayable, and are structurally unbillable. (3) Terra stops being asked an ambiguous question. The 3-1 split across visually equivalent blinds-only photos came from a disjunctive claim; each successor now commits to one object, so 'no dated valance visible' and 'blinds that appear dated' can no longer both be correct answers to the same string. (4) The fabric concept the humans actually approved (rc_7c5b9f9bb3aa's makeshift curtain, g7's brown valance) gets a claim and an embed text that name it, including improvised cloth coverings which the parent never mentioned. WHAT IT DOES NOT DO, stated plainly: neither gold unit becomes billed. Their loss is post-Terra routing onto dated_or_older_windows, an item with no economics by approved policy, and no catalog change reaches it. g4's wear-kind blinds bullet still resolves to no item. No dollars are recovered by this proposal; the benefit is one fewer false billing and a coherent boundary.
proposal.gap_description: Not the outcome - recorded because the analysis turned on it. The in-place variant of convention 5, leaving the id alone and putting route_override no_action on the existing carryover, is NOT natively expressible: carryover overrides are limited to name/description/embed_text/support_any/deny_any, and route_override sits in the inherited_fields set that only split successors may override (classify_op returns gap with 'carryover overrides are limited to wording fields; retrieval metadata, gates, and routes are not authorable here'). That is a genuine migration-system gap. It is not raised as the cluster's outcome for two reasons: the split reaches the same end natively, and the in-place version would be wrong on the merits anyway because it would route valances and curtains to no_action too, which Steven explicitly left open.

The retrieval surface advertised mini blinds while the atomic claim named a valance, so blinds-only observations were recruited onto a valance claim and Terra split on identical facts. Split by subject: blinds stay detectable but carry route_override no_action per the blinds ruling; fabric treatments keep the parent's work route.

proposal.package_route_effects: Routes, verified by running tools.renovation_architecture.catalog_projection.resolve_terminal_route on the generated items: window_blinds_dated_or_damaged -> ('no_action', 'route_override_no_action'), dated_window_valance_or_curtains -> ('work', 'work_default'), the latter identical to dated_window_treatment_valance today. Packages: package_role 'ignore' and package_affinity null are inherited by both, and the dry run reports repair_support_marker_routes empty for both, so neither successor drives a rehab package nor acts as contextual repair support under the 3.2 package_routing_decisions - the same position the parent holds. dated_or_older_windows is untouched and keeps its ('no_action','no_economics_approved_gap') route. Net billing change across the whole reviewed record: exactly one condition stops billing, rc_429ba6851d09, the reviewed hallucination.
proposal.product_policy: trade_bucket stays trim_doors_windows, which is not the quarantined trade (electrical), so no product-quarantine rule applies and nothing forces non_catalog_action. min_photo_evidence lives inside `estimate`, which is null on the parent and stays null on both successors, so no evidence-gate policy is touched. The proposal implements a stated product ruling (convention 5) rather than inventing one, and it deliberately implements only the blinds half of it, leaving valances and curtains billable exactly as Steven left them.

regression_controls.note: The hallucination, and the one control whose expectation needs care. Terra was shown a valance-or-treatment claim and answered supported on ordinary intact white mini-blinds ('The window has visible horizontal blinds that appear dated.'), and the condition BILLED (accepted=true, accepted_for_work, route_work). After the split the same observation ('The window and blinds are dated.') should resolve to window_blinds_dated_or_damaged, whose claim - basic, aged, bent, or unevenly hung blinds - those blinds arguably do satisfy, so I expect Terra to keep saying supported. That is deliberate and is what convention 5 asks for: blinds stay detectable. The harm is removed economically instead, by route_override no_action, so the card can no longer bill. I am NOT claiming this flips to rejected; claiming that would overstate the proposal.

Correct rejection on a plain white roller shade and mini-blind with no valance (Terra unsupported, reviewer refuted). Its observation 'The blinds appear dated and mismatched.' names no fabric term, so deny_any does not fire and it should reach window_blinds_dated_or_damaged. It stays unbillable either way: if Terra now supports the narrower blinds claim the route is no_action, and if Terra still refuses it is excluded as today. No path makes this card bill.

Correct rejection on plain straight intact mini-blinds, no valance. This is the second card whose resolution came from the catalog's own support_any 'blinds' via lexical_shortcut, so it is the clearest demonstration of the mechanism being moved: the identical shortcut now lands on the no_action successor. Unbillable on every path, as above.

Correct rejection on dated_or_older_windows (redfin_11000447 photo_001, white vinyl replacement windows, Terra unsupported, reviewer refuted). No op touches dated_or_older_windows - its wording, gates and scene groups are untouched and it keeps its ('no_action','no_economics_approved_gap') route - so this control is unchanged by construction. It is listed because the item is implicated in the cluster, not because the proposal puts it at risk.

proposal.regression_risk: RESOLVED AGAINST THE PROPOSAL AS DRAFTED, by the lead, from the pinned run artifact. The author ranked rc_7c5b9f9bb3aa first and marked it unproven: the item's only human-approved billing (redfin_81000709 photo_003, condition oc1_3e3158279888272c, claim exact / work warranted / supported_billed / accepted_for_work), whose 2b bullet text is absent from the evidence bundle. Their decision rule was explicit - if the bullet names a cloth or curtain the blinds successor's deny_any diverts it and the split is safe; if it names only blinds, the approved billing is lost. I read the pinned, hash-verified artifact artifacts_canary/renovation_session9_20260818/run_1/candidate/redfin_81000709/20260817_225858_d13bd83c/photo_intel_debug.json (sha256 05738c0e..., matching the bundle pin, verified true). The bullet is 'The blinds are old.' - blinds only, no fabric term - so deny_any never fires and the condition lands on the no_action blinds successor. Terra's stored rationale is 'Yellowed horizontal blinds and an improvised window covering are visible.', disposition accepted_for_work, reason_code route_work, terminal route work. CONSEQUENCE: the split as drafted removes the item's only demonstrated correct billing. That loss is intended by convention 5 if the ruling covers these blinds, and is a genuine lost condition if it does not - see unresolved_questions. Secondary risk unchanged: embed_text is the entire embedding input and there is no offline embedding store, so every post-split ranking claim is a reasoned expectation rather than a measurement.
proposal.retrieval_effects: Three mechanisms, of which two are deterministic and one is not. (1) DETERMINISTIC - the lexical shortcut. _resolve_candidate_via_lexical_shortcut resolves outright when any support_any term of the top candidate matches the observation. Today 'blinds' sits on the billing item, and that is literally how rc_429ba6851d09 (billed hallucination) and rc_ffad088fa5fe reached it. After the split every blinds token lives on the no_action successor, so the same shortcut, if it fires, lands on an item that cannot bill. (2) DETERMINISTIC - deny_any. It is a hard guardrail matched against the observation text in CatalogEmbeddingsRetriever._passes_guardrails; the blinds successor denies valance/curtain/curtains/drape/drapes/drapery, so any observation naming a fabric treatment cannot resolve to the no_action successor and is pushed to the billing one. Both successors keep the parent's glazing denies (broken window, fogged window, failed seal) so neither annexes glazing defects. (3) NOT VERIFIABLE OFFLINE - embedding rank. embed_text is the entire embedding input and there is no offline embedding store, so which successor ranks first for any given bullet, and whether the shortcut's score and margin thresholds (PASS_2D_SHORTCUT_MIN_SCORE 0.72, MIN_MARGIN 0.03) are still met once two similar items compete, can only be measured live. Note that two similar siblings can suppress the shortcut by shrinking the top-two margin, which would push these observations back to LLM selection - a neutral-to-good outcome, but an unmeasured one. Scene groups are unchanged on both successors (kitchen, bathroom, bedroom, living_areas, utility), so nothing new is reachable by scene.
proposal.semantic_before_after: BEFORE - one item, dated_window_treatment_valance. Terra sees 'window treatments dated valance or treatments': a disjunction whose subject spans hard and fabric coverings and whose state is an unqualified 'dated', so a builder-grade mini-blind and a vintage valance are indistinguishable under it. 2d and retrieval see something broader still - embed_text 'Basic or builder-grade mini blinds, horizontal blinds, older blinds, worn window coverings ... Aged, bent, or damaged mini blinds' and support_any containing the bare token 'blinds'. One route: work. AFTER - two items with disjoint subjects. window_blinds_dated_or_damaged claims 'window blinds or shades / basic, aged, bent, or unevenly hung blinds' and owns all the blinds retrieval language, but carries route_override no_action, so a blinds finding is stated and displayed and never priced. dated_window_valance_or_curtains claims 'window valance or curtains / dated, heavy, or improvised fabric window treatment' and owns only the fabric language (valance, cornice, swag, curtains, drapes, sheers, and improvised cloth coverings), keeping the parent's work route. Each successor's Terra surface and retrieval surface now describe the same object, which is what convention 1 asks for and what the parent violated in three concepts (plain_basic, wear_scuff, damage_break).

unresolved_questions: BLOCKING, and for Steven alone. Convention 5 says blinds stay detectable but must be a no_action catalog condition, and it was given against ordinary, clean, intact mini-blinds (rc_a22a241b3bf0). The item's only human-approved billing is also a blinds billing, but Terra's rationale there cites YELLOWED blinds - visible deterioration, not plain presence. Does the no_action ruling extend to visibly deteriorated blinds (yellowed, bent, unevenly hung), or only to ordinary plain ones? If it extends, this proposal is correct and the lost billing is convention 5 being applied. If it does not, the blinds successor needs a deterioration tell in its atomic_claim and must stay billable, and the proposal must be redrafted before implementation.
The 2b bullet question the author raised is now ANSWERED and needs no live run: the bullet is 'The blinds are old.' See proposal.regression_risk for the artifact provenance.

embed_text is the entire embedding input for an item and there is no offline embedding store, so the post-split ranks - which successor wins a given observation, and whether the lexical shortcut still fires on a blinds bullet at all - cannot be verified without a live retrieval run. Every retrieval claim here is reasoned, not measured.

cases.attribution_rationale:
Premise holds on my own inspection: all three photos show genuinely dated interior trim. photo_022 has heavy dark-stained casings on the cased opening and doorway plus mismatched baseboards and painted-over paneled doors; photo_028 has wide taupe-painted window casings with chipped, uneven paint and tired baseboards; photo_029 has aged painted paneled doors, jambs and casing. Trim modernization/refinishing work is warranted, matching the adjudicated v1.1 axes (claim exact, work warranted).

The 2a prose DID contain the condition on every evidence photo, so pass_2a is excluded: photo_022 lists "heavy dark wood trim, painted-over/dated doors, mismatched baseboards ... ready for modernization"; photo_028 has a whole bullet "Dated, rough window trim" describing wide painted trim with wear, uneven paint, gaps and minor damage; photo_029 has "doors and jambs look aged and may need adjustment, stripping, repainting, or replacement". What 2a did NOT contain is any statement that the trim is thin or builder-grade — it consistently describes substantial, heavy, wide, original trim.

Downstream, nothing was lost until Terra. 2b produced matching bullets and all three issues joined exactly (bullet_index 4, 9, 3, method exact). 2c kept all three (p2c_present true; the drops on these photos are unrelated bullets like windows, ceilings and the fire extinguisher). 2d resolved all three to dated_interior_trim by exact_kind — the item id matches the observation, and the adjudicated claim axis of "exact" forecloses calling this a wrong-item resolution. Condition projection succeeded: all three issues carry projected_condition_id oc1_c6c4c4017b1ed9dd, which reached Terra. 2e is not available here and in any case cost nothing (removed_count 0, condition projected despite p2e_status "absent"). Terra then returned verdict "unsupported" with reason_code verdict_unsupported, and the condition went unbilled (accepted false). Terra is therefore the first stage where a real, correctly-carried condition was destroyed.

Confidence is medium rather than high because of the misnamed-catalog tension: the billed claim_text is "interior trim plain, thin, or builder-grade trim package", and the trim in these photos is emphatically NOT thin or builder-grade, so Terra's rationale is literally accurate against the wording it was given. A reviewer could argue the real fault is upstream in the catalog item's claim text rather than in Terra's judgement. I still attribute to terra because the ladder has no rung for catalog naming, 2d chose the semantically correct item id, and the human's claim axis is "exact" — i.e. the adjudicator treated the billed claim as matching the photo, which makes Terra's rejection the error.

Its rationale describes the trim accurately as substantial painted wood, which is a correct refutation of 'plain, thin, or builder-grade' and an irrelevant one to 'dated'. Fixing the question is the lever; Terra needs no change.

coverage_gap.rationale: Coverage exists and was reached. dated_interior_trim is the catalog's interior-trim modernization concept, it appeared in the frozen candidate list on all three support issues (ranks 3, 1 and 7) and 2d resolved to it by exact_kind on all three. This matters mechanically as well as substantively: a declared coverage gap would make the structural_exception route illegal, and with no legitimate split parent (this entry is change_type reclassified with a single successor) it would force the outcome to migration_system_gap instead of a fix.

diagnosis.catalog_ownership_argument: dated_interior_trim commits to two different conditions depending on which surface you read. Terra sees only the atomic_claim: subject 'interior trim', state 'plain, thin, or builder-grade trim package', ontology_basis low_grade_material - a claim about material grade. 2d and retrieval see name 'Dated or Basic Interior Trim', description 'Plain, thin, or dated interior trim package ... Builder-grade millwork suitable for modernization', and embed_text 'Dated or builder-grade interior trim ... older painted baseboards, dated window casing ... Trim modernization opportunity' - which promise datedness. The divergence scan independently records promised_not_claimed = ['dated','door','window'] for exactly this item. That split is why the same item both rejects genuinely dated substantial trim (rc_b642fe69b86a, human truth claim exact / work warranted) and accepts clean undamaged builder trim (rc_022497229bd3 and rc_a0e75a18620e, human truth claim absent / work none, both hard_false_billed, both Terra-supported): the retrieval surface pulls the plain-trim bullet in and the claim surface then certifies it. Both error directions are produced by the item's own wording with no upstream stage at fault, so ownership is the catalog's. Steven's reconciled ruling on rc_b642fe69b86a says this directly: the heavy dated trim warrants work even though the atomic claim is limited to plain/thin/builder-grade, and the wording mismatch is catalog-owned.

rejected_alternative_owners.why: The Session-1 attribution rationale establishes that the 2a prose carried the condition on every evidence photo ('heavy dark wood trim, painted-over/dated doors, mismatched baseboards ... ready for modernization' on photo_022; a whole 'Dated, rough window trim' bullet on photo_028; 'doors and jambs look aged' on photo_029), and my own reading of photo_022 and photo_028 confirms the prose against the pixels. Nothing 2a said was wrong; what 2a never said is that the trim is thin or builder-grade, because it is not.

2d resolved all three issues to dated_interior_trim by routing_reason exact_kind, and the adjudicated claim axis is 'exact', i.e. the human treated the billed item as the right item. There is no materially more exact reachable item: the co-listed neighbours are dated_wood_paneling (wall paneling), dated_overall_decor_style (overall decor, safety_general trade, COSMETIC_MODERNIZATION), dated_or_older_windows (window units), dated_entry_or_patio_door and dated_interior_doors (door leaves, DOOR_REPLACE). None names the trim package. This cluster generates no pass_2d follow-ups.

Terra's rationale ('The visible trim is substantial painted wood trim rather than plain, thin, or builder-grade trim') is literally accurate against the claim string it was handed and accurate about the photos. Terra applied the claim correctly; the claim was wrong. The Session-1 record attributes this case to terra at medium confidence and its own rationale explains why: 'the ladder has no rung for catalog naming'. Phase C has that rung and Steven's ruling assigns it.

Retrieval behaved. dated_interior_trim appeared in the frozen top-8 on all three issues and was selected. Its scene_groups cover living_areas and bedroom, the two scenes involved, and its kind matched the 2c kind, so no scene or kind gate fired against it.

The concept exists as an item and was reached; only its Terra-facing string is wrong. Declaring a gap would also be illegal for the structural_exception route and would end in migration_system_gap rather than a fix.

evidence_bar_claim.conflict_note: There is no mixed human signal among the support units: the single support unit is adjudicated supports_claim, there are no refuted or unclear support units, so mixed_signal is false and no conflict_note is strictly required. The real tension lives in the controls and must not be hidden. Three positive_use cards carrying frozen v1.1 human truth claim exact / work warranted (rc_9e889631af67, rc_ceeb17f8e242, rc_d0ffde500a92) are described by the Phase B reviewer in almost the same words as the two hard_false_billed hallucinations (rc_022497229bd3, rc_a0e75a18620e): 'plain flat painted boards with no profile', 'narrow plain white baseboards, plain casing', 'a thin builder-grade trim, though clean and undamaged'. The visible facts do not separate the approved from the false, so any claim that requires visible datedness rejects all of them together. This proposal accepts that and argues it under convention 3 rather than pretending the hallucinations can be suppressed while the billings survive.
evidence_bar_claim.correlation_note: All support evidence is one condition on one property (redfin_80990371, condition oc1_c6c4c4017b1ed9dd, photos 022/028/029, three separate 2a observations projected onto that single condition - counted as one unit per convention 2, never multiplied). No second property corroborates the recovery direction. The suppression direction is separately evidenced by two hallucination controls on a different property (redfin_25809814) and the kill condition by a third (redfin_11185681), but those are controls, not support units, and they do not raise the bar.
evidence_bar_claim.justification: Recounted by hand from the adjudications: one unit, role support, evidence_class human_review, independent true, adjudication supports_claim -> human = 1, leads = 0, distinct properties = 1, reviewed refutations = 0, mixed_signal false. The ladder therefore yields 'none', matching the digest's recomputed bar exactly. The only remaining route is structural_exception and it is available on all three requirements: (a) at least one human/gold counted unit exists (redfin_80990371, case rc_b642fe69b86a); (b) this is not a missing-coverage cluster, so the exception is legal; (c) the demonstration is a fact readable straight off the semantic snapshot rather than off the evidence - dated_interior_trim's name, description and embed_text commit to datedness while its atomic_claim commits only to material grade, corroborated by the divergence scan's promised_not_claimed = ['dated','door','window']. The exception is what licenses a proposal on one property; it is not a claim that one property proves a broad effect, which is why confidence is medium and why the live kill-condition check on rc_73d15ca14405 is named as a gate.

proposal.economics_fit: No economic field is authorable and none is touched. The item stays severity 1, tier optional, scope replace, trade_bucket trim_doors_windows, work_item_code TRIM_REPLACE, pricing_status null, cost_model null, min_photo_evidence untouched inside estimate. The fit improves rather than degrades: TRIM_REPLACE at tier optional is a modernization spend, which is the right economics for a trim package that reads dated and the wrong economics for certifying that clean, intact, undamaged builder trim exists - which is what the item does today on three of its four positive uses. Dollar direction on this evidence is downward (six uses lost, one recovered), which the brief treats as context only. Note the recovery is one condition, not three: the three 2a observations on redfin_80990371 all projected onto the single condition oc1_c6c4c4017b1ed9dd.
proposal.expected_benefit: Two effects on billing correctness, stated with their full cost. (1) SUPPRESSION: the two required hallucination controls rc_022497229bd3 and rc_a0e75a18620e (redfin_25809814, human truth claim absent / work none, class hard_false_billed) are currently Terra-supported precisely because the claim asks about plain builder-grade material and the photos show plain builder-grade material that is clean and not dated. Under the new claim both should flip to rejected. These are not merely controls that survive a broadening - they are two false billings the current claim string actively causes, so the change removes a known hallucination mechanism rather than just failing to add one. (2) RECOVERY: the single support unit rc_b642fe69b86a (redfin_80990371, human truth claim exact / work warranted, class dirB_recovery) is a genuinely dated trim package that Terra correctly refused because the claim asked the wrong question; under the new claim it should be supported, recovering one real billable condition that three 2a observations, three exact 2b joins, 2c survival and a correct exact_kind 2d resolution had all carried intact. THE COST, stated plainly and not netted away: three positive_use cards whose frozen v1.1 human labels are claim exact / work warranted / supported_billed - rc_9e889631af67, rc_ceeb17f8e242 and rc_d0ffde500a92 - also flip to rejected, and a fourth, rc_57c6faf79c7e, flips from a supported billing on a frame containing no visible trim. The wrong name is therefore the "uneven" descriptor attached to a condition whose real mechanism is soiling plus surface aging/wear. That descriptor did not arise downstream: the 2a prose itself already reads "The hardscape is neglected, uneven-looking, and cluttered." 2a DID contain the true material (neglected, cluttered, needs rebuilding) but never described the surface as aged/worn/dirty, and it supplied unevenness that is not in the photo. Everything after 2a is faithful transport, not distortion: 2b produced the bullet "The patio hardscape appears neglected and uneven." and joined exact, 2c kept it (only chimney/clutter/planters/soil/power-line bullets were dropped), 2d resolved it to patio_or_porch_surface_wear whose claim text the human calls true, 2e kept the issue, the condition projected, and Terra supported it with a rationale ("aged, darkened, and worn") that is accurate.
