cases.attribution_rationale: Premise confirmed. Photos 017 and 028 show one raised rear wood deck reached by a long exterior wood stair: bare grey weathered decking with raised grain and worn board edges, stair treads and stringers greyed and heavily worn, a dark-stained board ceiling overhead. Real work is warranted, but the billed name ("patio or porch surface aging, surface wear, or coating breakdown") names a surface/coating mechanism on a patio-or-porch surface, while the visible mechanism is bare-wood weathering and deterioration of decking and stair treads calling for board replacement. (Photo_001 shows only marble stoops on a rowhouse front, no porch at all, so one of the three evidence legs is spurious as well.) Attribution: 2a is not responsible. Its prose contained the correctly-named problem in fuller form on both porch photos -- photo_028: "The wood porch, railings, stair stringers, and handrails show weathering and likely need repair or replacement," plus a separate rot/footing inspection note; photo_017: "Floorboards are heavily weathered and may have splitting/cupping. Expect possible board replacement and checking joists, ledger attachment, and footings." What 2a did NOT contain anywhere is the word or notion of a patio surface, a coating, or coating breakdown; nothing in any of the three proses attributes the wear to a finish failing. 2b preserved both object and mechanism verbatim in kind ("The wood front porch is weathered", "The porch floorboards are heavily weathered") -- it thinned the detail (dropping splitting/cupping and the structural-rot bullet entirely) but introduced no wrong name, and 2c kept both bullets. The mislabel is first introduced at 2d, the stage that actually chooses the name: it mapped a true generic wood-weathering bullet onto catalog item patio_or_porch_surface_wear (resolution_path llm, 7 candidates, routing_reason exact_kind), swapping wood deterioration for surface/coating wear. Condition projection and Terra then inherited that name -- Terra's own rationale echoes it ("clear weathering and surface wear") -- so neither is the first fault. Confidence is medium rather than high because the three sibling bullets on photo_028 (railings, stair stringers, handrails weathered) resolved to catalog_item_id null, which hints the catalog may lack a wood deck/stair deterioration item; if so 2d picked the closest available name rather than freely choosing a wrong one. The ladder has no catalog-gap rung, and 2d owns the naming decision, so 2d is the answer.

cases.attribution_rationale:
Premise confirmed by inspection: photo_001.jpg shows a full-width covered porch whose roof fascia/soffit line is visibly wavy rather than straight, with a dark ragged band of out-of-plane, deteriorated boards where the porch roof meets the main house above the steps. That is consistent with the adjudicated v1.1 axes (claim=exact, work=warranted), so the condition is real and the pipeline failed to bill it.

The 2a prose DID contain the condition, in plain terms: under "Roof condition" it states the shingles look aged and uneven "with visible waviness/sagging around the porch-roof connection," and separately notes the porch's "fascia, railings, steps, and porch roof appear weathered" and "may need substantial carpentry work-not just paint." What the 2a prose did NOT contain is the specific vocabulary of the catalog item ("soffit," "porch ceiling panels," "loose or missing panels") -- it described the same physical defect at the porch-roof connection in roof/framing language rather than soffit language. That wording gap did not cost anything downstream: 2b lifted the sentence verbatim as bullet index 1 (exact join), 2c kept it (p2c_present true, and the only 2c drops on this photo are four benign non-defect bullets: low house, flat yard, large porch, mature trees), 2d resolved it via the llm path to soffit_or_porch_ceiling_failed on exact_kind routing -- a resolution the human's "exact" claim axis explicitly ratifies, so 2d is not the fault -- 2e kept the issue (p2e_status kept, issue id present in kept_issue_ids), and condition_projection produced oc1_69263601050587ce.

So the condition survived intact all the way to the final verdict, and the first and only stage that went wrong is terra: it returned cannot_assess with the rationale that "the porch ceiling or soffit panels are not clearly visible enough to judge sagging, looseness, or missing panels," which set accepted=false with reason_code verdict_cannot_assess. Terra's non-assessment is what dropped a claim the human found exactly supported and warranted, on a photo where the sagging porch-roof/soffit line is in fact discernible. This is NOT the known post-Terra routing gap: that gap applies only when Terra SUPPORTED the condition and disposition still unbilled it. Here Terra did not support it -- cannot_assess is itself the terminal non-accept -- so the ladder has a rung that fits, and the "inspection" disposition is a consequence of Terra's verdict rather than an independent routing decision. The 2e note in the record (one tier_optional_suppressed count on this photo) is a red herring per the stated corpus rule and, in any case, this issue was kept and projected.

coverage_gap.rationale: I tested the structure step's coverage-gap hypothesis and it does not survive, so I am declining it on the merits rather than only because bar none forbids declaring it. The hypothesis was that a porch-roof framing sag has no exact concept because damaged_or_unsafe_deck_or_porch reads as walking surfaces and roofline_water_damage_suspected claims water staining. Convention 1 decides it: the surface that has to carry the condition through verification is the ATOMIC CLAIM, and damaged_or_unsafe_deck_or_porch's atomic_claim is subject 'deck or porch structure', state 'loose, rotted, or missing boards or railings'. The reviewer's own description of the photo is 'a band of dark, ragged, out-of-plane boards where the porch roof meets the house roof' - loose, deteriorated, out-of-plane boards on the porch structure. That claim covers what is visible. It is the item's DESCRIPTION and EMBED_TEXT that narrow the reading to walking surfaces ('boards, railings, stairs, landings, or porch surfaces', 'exterior walking surfaces'), and those are the 2d/retrieval surfaces, not the verification surface. So this is a retrieval-surface reading problem on an item whose claim was adequate, which is a 2d selection story, not absent coverage. Two supporting checks. (1) The item's divergence direction is promised_not_claimed = ['damage_break','safety'], i.e. it promises MORE on retrieval than it claims - the opposite of a claim too narrow to hold the condition. (2) I scanned all 128 items for an exterior structural-framing concept: the only framing item is rotted_subfloor_or_structural_framing, whose scene_groups are kitchen/bathroom/bedroom/living_areas/utility/other with NO 'exterior', so it can never be retrieved on an exterior scene - but it is also the wrong concept (moisture-saturated load-bearing members, severity 5, STRUCTURAL_REPAIR), and routing a distant street-view fascia wave there would be a worse billing than the one that happened. Recording the scene-group observation for the lead without declaring it a gap: scene_groups is not authorable on a carryover, so if it ever did become the right lever it would be a migration-system gap, and it is not the right lever here.

diagnosis.catalog_ownership_argument: The catalog is NOT at fault and I am not asking for a change to it. soffit_or_porch_ceiling_failed is the one item in the exterior family whose divergence scan is completely clean - promised_not_claimed [] and claimed_not_promised [] - meaning its retrieval surface and its atomic claim describe the same thing. Its atomic_claim ('soffit or porch ceiling panels' / 'sagging, loose, or missing panels') is precise, correctly split from its degradation sibling soffit_or_porch_ceiling_weathered, and it did exactly what a good claim should do: it refused to certify an object the photo does not show. Convention 1 asks which surface failed, and the answer here is neither. The residual catalog-shaped observation is an ontology one, and it is a near miss rather than a defect: three exterior items sit adjacent to a porch-roof connection (soffit_or_porch_ceiling_failed for the panels, damaged_or_unsafe_deck_or_porch for the porch structure, roofline_water_damage_suspected for the eave/fascia line but only under a moisture-evidence basis), the boundary between them is drawn on retrieval text rather than on claim text, and nothing names framing deflection as such. That is worth documenting for a future pass. It is not worth a change proposal on one unit, and at bar none it could not carry one anyway.

pass_2d_follow_ups.note:
Confusion family, stated in full: porch assembly: ceiling/soffit panels vs porch structure vs roofline eave
Issue 79ada05c9fc9051a, observation 'Waviness and sagging are visible around the porch-roof connection.', resolution path llm, routing_reason exact_kind. 2d took rank 1 - an item whose subject is the panels on the UNDERSIDE of the porch roof, which this street-view photo does not show - over rank 3, whose atomic_claim names 'deck or porch structure' with 'loose, rotted, or missing boards' and which matches the reviewer's 'dark, ragged, out-of-plane boards where the porch roof meets the house roof'. Both were kind_ok true and scene_ok true; nothing gated the better choice. Consequence was not cosmetic: the rank-1 claim was unverifiable from this viewpoint, so Terra returned cannot_assess, accepted went false with reason_code verdict_cannot_assess, and a condition the humans called exact and warranted was routed to inspection instead of billed. roofline_water_damage_suspected at rank 4 was the reviewer's other suggestion; I rank it BELOW the rank-3 item because its ontology_basis is moisture_evidence and its claim requires water staining, which the reviewer does not report - selecting it would have traded an unverifiable object for an unverifiable mechanism. Suggested probe for the 2d lane: the pull to rank 1 looks lexical, since soffit_or_porch_ceiling_failed's embed_text contains both 'sagging' and 'porch ceiling' while the better item's embed steers toward walking surfaces; test whether 2d over-weights an embed keyword match against an object the photo cannot show. NOTE that this follow-up is the whole actionable content of the cluster - do not read it as a catalog defect.

I conclude the rank-3 item's atomic_claim is adequate, so this is a 2d selection story and not missing coverage. It is also not declarable: a declared coverage gap on a non-deferred outcome requires a met bar, and with no legitimate split parent it would force migration_system_gap. Both reasons point the same way and the first is the real one.

coverage_gap.rationale: Recorded as an absent concept, deliberately NOT declared as a coverage gap. I searched all 128 items in items.json for gable / attic / vent / louver / opening / boarded / plywood: no item names a gable, attic or vent opening. It was billed under an item whose subject is wrong and whose economics are wrong, which is a precision and billing defect, not missing coverage. Two further reasons not to declare it: (a) at bar 'none' a declared coverage gap on a non-declared-deferred outcome is invalid, and with no legitimate split parent it would force migration_system_gap, which would mislocate the owner; (b) creating a gable-opening item would require an extra successor on a legitimate split entry, and boarded_up_entry_or_window is a carryover (change_type 'unchanged', single successor, no siblings) that expresses one coherent asserted-failure claim - splitting it purely to house an unrelated subject would be an illegitimate split. The absence of any legitimate split parent for a gable/attic-opening concept is recorded here for the lead.

diagnosis.catalog_ownership_argument: The catalog is NOT the owner, and that is the whole finding. Asking what went wrong operationally rather than semantically flips the answer. Operationally nothing was lost: the boarded opening is real, work is warranted (human truth 'misnamed_but_warranted', work 'warranted'), Terra supported it, and it was accepted for work. What went wrong is what it was billed AS. boarded_up_entry_or_window carries severity 4, scope 'replace', trade_bucket trim_doors_windows, tier work, bills true, work_item_code DOOR_WINDOW_REPLACE and an embed that says 'Replace and restore door or window assembly'. A nailed board panel over an attic-level gable opening was therefore priced as replacing a door or window assembly. Every lever that would correct that is unauthorable: severity, scope, trade_bucket and route_override are not settable on a carryover (the decisions entry is change_type 'unchanged' with one successor and no legitimate split parent), and cost, estimate, work_item_code, cost_model, package_affinity and package_role are never authorable on any entry by construction. Meanwhile both natively authorable moves are affirmatively wrong. Widening /successors/0/atomic_claim from subject 'entry or window opening' to any wall or gable opening is native (the lead's dry runs confirm the shape is expressible) but it would make the severity-4 DOOR_WINDOW_REPLACE billing MORE legitimate on exactly the cases where it is least appropriate, and it would open the item to interior near-misses it already retrieves: at redfin_11000447 it ranked 1 on 'The wood header or trim area at the stair opening is exposed' (2d resolved nothing) and ranked 3, 4 and 5 on three interior wiring/electrical-cutout observations that resolved to visible_electrical_risks. Adding deny_any for gable/attic via overrides is also native but would suppress a real, human-warranted condition that no item in the catalog covers. So the smallest correct lever is not a catalog change at all: record the severity/scope/work-item mismatch as an economics and work-item policy gap, record the absent gable/attic-opening concept together with the absence of a legitimate split parent to create one, carry the reviewer's own note, and change nothing in the catalog. Secondary catalog-side observations recorded but not proposed: the atomic_claim over-commits on subject (unsupported_commitment_types ['object']); the rendered claim_text is malformed - 'entry or window opening opening boarded over', with 'opening' duplicated because subject 'entry or window opening' concatenates with state 'opening boarded over'; and the divergence scan gives promised_not_claimed ['damage_break', 'door', 'sag_structural'], i.e. the retrieval surface promises damage and structural sag that the claim never asserts. A one-unit cluster at bar 'none' must not propose those edits.

rejected_alternative_owners.why: The frozen attribution assigns this case to stage 2d with high confidence, and its rationale is right that 2d is the hop where the name changed. But under the 2026-09-03 rule the operative question is 'right item unavailable' versus 'right item reachable but another selected', and this is the first case. The frozen candidate list holds eight items: boarded_up_entry_or_window (1), soffit_or_porch_ceiling_failed (2), damaged_or_unsafe_deck_or_porch (3), fence_broken_or_leaning (4), roof_shingles_missing_or_curling (5), damaged_or_rotted_siding_or_trim (6), roofline_water_damage_suspected (7), paving_heaved_or_trip_hazard (8). Every one of the other seven is a worse fit than the one chosen, and no gable/attic-opening item exists anywhere in the 128 to have been retrieved. 2d picked the best available item. There is therefore no pass_2d_follow_ups entry and pass_2d_follow_ups is empty; the divergence from the frozen attribution is flagged as an unresolved question and the attribution record is left untouched.

2a is not implicated and is frozen regardless. The 2a prose named the subject accurately and neutrally - 'The upper-gable opening is boarded' - and tied it to attic ventilation, framing and insulation, i.e. the correct domain, with no word suggesting a door, entry or window. 2b joined exact at bullet_index 13 preserving the wording verbatim, and 2c kept the bullet unchanged in p2c_surviving. Nothing upstream of 2d introduced the wrong subject.

The cluster is also at bar 'none' with a single unit on a single property and zero reviewed controls, which independently blocks native_decisions_proposal. Recorded as a contributing cause only.

But we would not want severity 4 / scope 'replace' changed on THIS item: for a genuinely boarded-up door or window those values are correct. The fields that are wrong for a gable panel are the economics fields (work_item_code, cost, estimate), which are never authorable on any entry, carryover or split, by design - they are a pricing and work-item policy surface that sits outside the migration system rather than a gap in it. proposal.economics_fit: This is the finding. The condition is genuinely billable - human truth work 'warranted', Terra supported, accepted true, disposition accepted_for_work, reason_code route_work - so billability itself is correct and is not one of the mismatched dimensions. What is wrong is everything about HOW it bills. The item carries severity 4, scope 'replace', tier 'work', trade_bucket 'trim_doors_windows' and work_item_code DOOR_WINDOW_REPLACE, with an embed_text that states the intended repair as 'Replace and restore door or window assembly'. Applied to a nailed board panel over an attic-level gable opening, that prices a small exterior trim or vent repair as a door/window assembly replacement at the second-highest severity. package_affinity, pricing_status and cost_model are all null, so nothing downstream moderates it. Not one of these fields is authorable: severity, scope, trade_bucket and route_override are non-authorable on a carryover entry, and work_item_code, cost, estimate, cost_model, package_affinity, package_role, estimate_scope and estimate_scope_reason are never authorable on any entry. That is why the correct action is a policy record rather than a catalog edit.
proposal.expected_benefit: Nothing improves in the catalog, and that is the intended result. The benefit is that a genuine, previously unrecorded billing defect is written down with its owner correctly identified, together with the proof that no catalog lever can fix it. Concretely the record hands the lead three things: (1) an economics and work-item policy gap - a non-door, non-window opening resolving to boarded_up_entry_or_window is costed as a severity-4 door/window assembly replacement, and every corrective field is unauthorable by construction; (2) the absent gable/attic-opening concept, verified against all 128 items, together with the absence of any legitimate split parent that could house it, so the design question is stated rather than silently converted into an illegitimate split; (3) the reviewer's 'generic presence' note translated into what it would actually require. It also prevents a plausible-looking harm: the one native edit this cluster invites - widening the atomic_claim - would have made the billing defect worse and admitted five known interior near-misses.
proposal.gap_description: Two gaps, both recorded as non-catalog actions. GAP 1 - economics and work-item policy. When an observation whose true subject is neither a door nor a window resolves to boarded_up_entry_or_window, it is billed at severity 4, scope 'replace', trade trim_doors_windows, work_item_code DOOR_WINDOW_REPLACE, against an intended repair of 'Replace and restore door or window assembly'. The corrective fields are unauthorable by construction: severity, scope, trade_bucket and route_override are not settable on a carryover (decisions entry legacy_id boarded_up_entry_or_window, change_type 'unchanged', one successor at index 0, no siblings), and work_item_code, cost, estimate, cost_model, package_affinity, package_role and estimate_scope are never settable on any entry. Owner: work-item and pricing policy, not the migration decisions file. GAP 2 - absent concept with no legitimate split parent. No item among the 128 expresses a gable, attic or vent opening; the nearest neighbours (exhaust_fan_missing_or_broken, soffit_or_porch_ceiling_failed, soffit_or_porch_ceiling_weathered, exposed_sheathing_or_missing_siding) are all different subjects, and the frozen candidate list offered nothing closer. A new item can exist only as an extra successor of a legitimate split entry, and boarded_up_entry_or_window is a coherent single-claim carryover that provides no legitimate split. Owner: catalog design, pending a second reviewed property. coverage_gap.rationale: Declared on BRANCH A ONLY (gold:redfin_11000447:photo_006.jpg:g5). The concept that has no catalog home is 'interior base trim missing or incompletely installed, leaving a raw wall-to-floor edge' expressed as a DEFECT-kind condition. Three independent checks establish the hole. (1) I searched all 128 items in digest/items.json for trim/baseboard/casing/millwork/missing/incomplete language: the only interior trim items are baseboard_wear_scuffs (kind degradation, atomic_claim 'baseboards: scuffs, paint loss, dents, or general wear', ontology_basis dent_without_functional_impact) and dated_interior_trim (kind modernization, 'plain, thin, or builder-grade trim package', ontology_basis low_grade_material). Neither claims missing or incomplete trim. The only item that claims missing trim at all is damaged_or_rotted_siding_or_trim, whose subject is 'exterior siding or trim'. (2) Retrieval for the branch-A bullet 'The trim is incomplete.' drew a kind-homogeneous DEFECT pool (all six frozen candidates are kind defect: unfinished_interior_wall_osb_exposed, ceiling_cracks_or_sagging, ceiling_fan_blades_damaged, visible_electrical_risks, interior_wall_stripped_to_studs, damaged_drywall_or_cracks; routing_reason exact_kind). baseboard_wear_scuffs is kind degradation and was therefore not in the pool and could not have been selected. The reachability scan reports baseboard_wear_scuffs rank null on that issue; its kind_ok=true there is a scan artifact, because the gold unit carries no recorded 2c kind (unit-level kind is null) so the gate defaults open. The scan reports kind_ok=false for baseboard_wear_scuffs on the branch-B unit, which does carry a recorded kind of defect. Confirmation that the gate is real and per-bullet: on the SAME photo the bullet 'The walls are scuffed and marked.' drew an all-degradation pool that did include baseboard_wear_scuffs at rank 3. (3) Two independent reviewers reached the same conclusion on the record: the Phase B lineage note says 'No candidate on that issue names missing/rough trim; damaged_drywall_or_cracks (rank 6) is the nearest and still wrong', and the gold attribution rationale already flags 'the fact that a sibling trim bullet resolved to null suggests catalog coverage may genuinely be thin, which would make this out_of_catalog rather than a 2d error'. Two of the three trim bullets on that photo ('The wood header or trim area at the stair opening is exposed.' and 'The ceiling edge or header area has a rough finish.') resolved to catalog_item_id null. split_parent is null because no legitimate split parent exists: a split entry exists to separate a legacy item whose ATOMIC CLAIM conflates two mechanisms with different evidence and remediation (the pattern of the damaged_soffit_or_porch_ceiling entry, which split asserted_failure from visible_deterioration). Neither candidate parent is conflated. baseboard_wear_scuffs already has a single atomic claim (wear); only its embed_text advertises 'Missing baseboards, detached trim, visible gaps at wall base, incomplete base trim installation'. unfinished_interior_wall_osb_exposed likewise has a single atomic claim; only its retrieval surface over-promises. The correct remedy for an over-broad retrieval text is to narrow the retrieval text, not to split the claim. Manufacturing a split on either item purely to mint a new successor would be a standalone 'add' wearing a split's clothes, which the authoring surface forbids. Two further blockers confirm the road is closed even if a split were manufactured: a split successor may not keep the parent's id, so baseboard_wear_scuffs would be deprecated with requires_re_resolution across the corpus while carrying five human-approved billings owned by CAP-001; and split successors inherit the parent's economics byte-identically under split_successor_pricing policy 'inherit_parent_economics_v1' while economics are never authorable here, so a missing-base-trim defect would arrive priced as a severity-1 cosmetic TRIM_REPAIR wear item with no way to correct it.

diagnosis.catalog_ownership_argument: The catalog owns this on two counts, and only the second is fixable within the authoring surface. (a) COVERAGE (branch A, the outcome-bearing count): a real, warranted, concretely repairable condition - base trim absent along an entire wall run with a raw wall-to-floor edge - has no defect-kind item in the catalog to land on. Steven's convention 3 names incompleteness explicitly as a qualifying concrete need, so this is a billable loss and not a harmless naming difference. Every stage upstream did its job: 2a captured it ('trim is minimal or incomplete'), 2b rendered it faithfully ('The trim is incomplete.'), 2c kept it and classified it as a defect (correct: missing_required_component), and 2d picked the best of six items none of which was right. When every stage behaves and the condition is still lost, the catalog is the owner. (b) WORDING (shared, both branches): unfinished_interior_wall_osb_exposed's retrieval and selection surfaces promise a generic unfinished/incomplete wall while its Terra-facing atomic_claim commits to a material (OSB/sheathing) and to an unfinished wall assembly. This is exactly the surface split named in convention 1, and the divergence scan records it as promised_not_claimed = ['missing_incomplete','trim_casing']. It is the mechanism that pulled both bullets to rank 1 and then guaranteed their rejection. I decline to propose the narrowing op for it and give the reasons under alternative_stage_analysis and unresolved_questions; that abstention is a verifiability judgment, not a finding that the divergence is acceptable.

pass_2d_follow_ups.note:
Confusion family, stated in full: finished-wall surface damage versus unfinished wall assembly (paint_drywall): patch compound, scraped paint and rough patches versus exposed OSB/sheathing or studs
redfin_10952874 photo_033, issue a33067a74cd038a2, bullet 'An area near the closet corner is unfinished and patchy.' 2c kind defect, scene bedroom, resolution_path llm, shortcut_reason null. 2d took rank 1 (the OSB item) over rank 3 damaged_drywall_or_cracks, which was kind_ok and scene_ok and whose embed_text names 'rough patches' explicitly; Terra then correctly rejected the OSB claim and the real patch-and-paint condition went unbilled. The word 'unfinished' in the bullet is doing the damage: it matches the OSB item's 'Interior wall not finished' embed_text while describing an unfinished PAINT job, not an unfinished wall assembly. Catalog unchanged for this case. Secondary cost worth recording: damaged_drywall_or_cracks is a package_driver for bedroom_repair, so the mis-selection also removed this observation from bedroom package formation, not just from the line-item list.

proposal.economics_fit: Not engaged - no op. The economics are nonetheless the wall that closes the gap road: cost, estimate, work_item_code, cost_model, package_affinity, package_role and estimate_scope are never authorable in the decisions file for either a carryover or a split successor, and split_successor_pricing policy 'inherit_parent_economics_v1' makes any successor inherit its parent's economics byte-identically. A missing-base-trim defect minted under baseboard_wear_scuffs would arrive priced as a severity-1 cosmetic wear item with no authorable path to install-and-finish economics.
proposal.expected_benefit: None claimed from this judgment, because it proposes no change. The benefit of the recorded gap, if the authoring surface is extended, is the recovery of interior base-trim incompleteness as a billable defect - currently a guaranteed loss on every property where it appears, because the bullets that describe it are routed into a claim (exposed OSB) that Terra will always and correctly reject. The measurable target is fewer lost real conditions; there is no hallucination-reduction claim, and no dollar claim is made.
proposal.gap_description: MIGRATION-SYSTEM GAP: the catalog needs a defect-kind item claiming missing or incompletely installed interior base trim, and the kind_v2_decisions authoring surface cannot create one. Three independent constraints close every road. (1) No standalone add or merge exists; a genuinely new item can only appear as an extra successor of a legitimate split entry. (2) No legitimate split parent exists. A split entry separates a legacy item whose ATOMIC CLAIM conflates two mechanisms with different evidence and remediation - the pattern of the damaged_soffit_or_porch_ceiling entry, which separated asserted_failure from visible_deterioration. Both candidate parents here have a single, already-atomic claim and merely over-broad retrieval text: baseboard_wear_scuffs claims wear only while its embed_text advertises 'Missing baseboards, detached trim, visible gaps at wall base, incomplete base trim installation', and unfinished_interior_wall_osb_exposed claims exposed OSB while its retrieval surface advertises a generic unfinished/incomplete wall. The remedy for an over-broad retrieval text is to narrow the retrieval text; manufacturing a split to mint a successor would be a standalone add wearing a split's clothes. (3) Even a manufactured split fails on its own terms: a split successor may not keep the parent's id, so baseboard_wear_scuffs would be deprecated with requires_re_resolution across the corpus while carrying five human-approved billings owned by CAP-001; and split_successor_pricing policy 'inherit_parent_economics_v1' with economics never authorable would deliver the new item priced as a severity-1 cosmetic TRIM_REPAIR wear condition, unable to bill an install. Separately, the kind gate rules out the cheap alternative of routing the concept to an existing item: 2d pools are kind-homogeneous per bullet, 'The trim is incomplete.' drew an all-defect pool, and the only interior trim items are degradation (baseboard_wear_scuffs) and modernization (dated_interior_trim), so no claim rewrite on an existing trim item can make it reachable from these bullets. What the gap needs from the migration system is either the ability to author a genuinely new item outside a split, or the ability to author economics for a new successor; either one alone would unblock this.
proposal.package_route_effects: None, since no op is proposed. Recorded as the measured cost of the status quo: the OSB item carries package_affinity null, while damaged_drywall_or_cracks is a package_driver for bedroom_repair and living_repair and baseboard_wear_scuffs is a package_support for bedroom, living, kitchen and bathroom modernization with repair_support_when_driven true. Both mis-resolutions therefore removed their observations from package formation as well as from the line items, and routed TRIM_REPAIR-class and DRYWALL_PATCH-class work onto FRAMING_DRYWALL_FINISH at severity 3.
proposal.product_policy: No product-quarantine interaction. The implicated item's trade_bucket is paint_drywall and the true homes are paint_drywall and trim_doors_windows; none is the quarantined electrical trade, so nothing here is forced to non_catalog_action on product-policy grounds. (visible_electrical_risks appears in both frozen candidate pools but is not implicated and did not take either resolution.)
proposal.regression_risk: None from this judgment. The risk this judgment AVOIDS is the substantive point: every candidate lever carried an unbounded or wrong-direction risk. Widening the OSB claim would broaden a severity-3 FRAMING_DRYWALL_FINISH defect over cosmetic patchiness and missing trim and would compensate a 2d selection failure. Widening baseboard_wear_scuffs's claim would not recover branch A (kind gate) and would push a severity-1 defaultHidden cosmetic item toward missing-component territory on another cluster's item. Narrowing the OSB item's embed_text would change its rank on every bullet in the corpus with zero reviewed uses and zero correct rejections available to detect the damage. With no reviewed control of any kind in this cluster, no proposal could have been shown safe.
proposal.retrieval_effects: None, since no op is proposed. The retrieval facts that would matter to any future op: unfinished_interior_wall_osb_exposed's embed_text is non-empty and is therefore the entire embedding input for the item, so any edit to it changes the item's rank on every bullet corpus-wide and cannot be verified offline (there is no offline embedding store). support_any is only a soft ranking hint and the annotator search index, and both resolutions in this cluster took the llm path with shortcut_reason null, so the support_any tokens 'unfinished wall' and 'exposed wall' are not the demonstrated attractor. Retrieval pools are kind-homogeneous and gated per bullet, which is why a defect-kind bullet can never reach the degradation-kind baseboard_wear_scuffs.
proposal.semantic_before_after: No change proposed; the catalog is left exactly as it is. Stated for the record so the gap is actionable if the authoring surface is extended: the shape the evidence warrants is a DEFECT-kind item with subject 'interior base trim', state 'missing or incompletely installed base trim leaving a raw wall-to-floor edge', ontology_basis missing_required_component, trade_bucket trim_doors_windows, work_item_code TRIM_REPAIR, scene_groups covering interior scenes, sitting between baseboard_wear_scuffs (degradation, cosmetic wear on installed trim) and bare_or_missing_finish_flooring (defect, missing_required_component on the floor). It must be defect-kind or it stays unreachable from the bullets that describe it. In parallel, unfinished_interior_wall_osb_exposed's retrieval surface should stop advertising a generic unfinished/incomplete wall, but that op is deliberately not proposed here (see unresolved_questions).

The cluster bar (two_independent_human) is met and the tool will recompute it, but branch B is deliberately excluded from the gap because its correct item was reachable at rank 3. If the lead requires the gap itself to carry two independent units, the fallback outcome is no_change plus the same pass_2d_follow_ups entry plus documentation of the promised_not_claimed divergence - not a native proposal, since no lever survives.

Should the OSB item's retrieval surface be narrowed anyway, as a separate coherence fix? The op would be native (name/description/embed_text/support_any via overrides on an unchanged carryover) but I decline to propose it for three reasons that a live run could resolve: both observed resolutions took the llm path with shortcut_reason null so support_any is not the demonstrated attractor; embed_text is the entire embedding input with no offline store, so the intended rank change is unverifiable before a live run; and the item has zero reviewed uses, so no control can bound the corpus-wide blast radius. PROMOTION RECIPE: run a live 2d re-resolution over the frozen bullet set with the OSB item's embed_text narrowed to OSB/sheathing/plywood language only, and check three things - (i) branch B's bullet moves to damaged_drywall_or_cracks, (ii) branch A's bullet resolves to null rather than to a new wrong item, (iii) no bullet elsewhere in the corpus that legitimately belongs to the OSB item loses it. With that run in hand this becomes a native_decisions_proposal on a met bar.

Cross-cluster: baseboard_wear_scuffs (owned by CAP-001) carries the identical promised_not_claimed pair ['missing_incomplete','trim_casing'], and the lead has a dry-run-verified native op to widen its atomic_claim to match its own embed_text. That op should be judged on CAP-001's evidence, and the lead must NOT credit it with recovering anything in CAP-013: branch A's bullet sat in a kind-homogeneous defect pool and baseboard_wear_scuffs is kind degradation, so it was unreachable regardless of what its claim says. Widening a claim does not change a kind.

damaged_drywall_or_cracks also carries promised_not_claimed ['missing_incomplete'] - its embed_text advertises 'missing sections' while its claim is 'cracks, holes, or impact damage'. coverage_gap.rationale: Searched all 128 items in items.json before considering a gap. Every mechanism named in the claim except two has a named home: staining -> peeling_or_discolored_paint (its embed_text literally reads 'Lower-wall moisture staining, tide marks, and discoloration near baseboards or base of walls'), bathroom_paint_peeling_or_worn (bathroom-scoped) and water_stain_ceiling (ceiling-scoped, require_any ['ceiling']); cracks and holes -> damaged_drywall_or_cracks; missing wall material -> interior_wall_stripped_to_studs (sev 4) and unfinished_interior_wall_osb_exposed (sev 3); unpainted patches -> damaged_drywall_or_cracks (support_any contains 'patch' and 'uneven'; embed names 'rough patches'). Two mechanisms have no named item anywhere in the catalog: graffiti (the string does not appear in any of the 128 items) and torn or water-damaged wall paneling ('wallboard' appears only inside damaged_drywall_or_cracks' embed_text, whose atomic-claim subject is 'drywall'; dated_wood_paneling is a modernization/style item, not a damage item). I still record is_missing_coverage false, for three independent reasons. (1) Operational-equivalence test: graffiti's repair is stain-block prime and repaint, which PAINT_INTERIOR under peeling_or_discolored_paint already carries at the same trade and scope; torn paneling's repair is patch/replace and finish, which DRYWALL_PATCH under damaged_drywall_or_cracks already carries. Both are naming gaps, not work-coverage gaps, and the brief forbids adding items to make output more verbose. (2) Evidence: the graffiti case rests on one model-judge lead (redfin_11077450 photo_020) and the torn-paneling case on one (redfin_125970550 photo_018); a lead can never ground a coverage declaration. (3) Expressibility: a genuinely new item exists only as an extra successor of a legitimate split entry, and neither implicated item has a defensible split parent here (wall_scuffs_marks_or_dents is a reclassified carryover with a single successor, damaged_drywall_or_cracks is unchanged), so declaring a gap would force migration_system_gap on lead-only evidence. Precedent applied: the reconciled ruling on rc_3a19f759f2d9 (deck weathering) treats 'right existing concept, reachable, wrong selection' as a 2d specificity question rather than missing coverage.

diagnosis.catalog_ownership_argument: The catalog's share of this cluster is real but secondary, and it is not large enough to act on today. What the catalog owns: wall_scuffs_marks_or_dents shows a genuine two-surface split (divergence_scan: promised_not_claimed = [damage_break, stain_discolor]). The surfaces 2d and retrieval see promise damage and staining - description 'Walls show visible scuffs, stains, dents, or minor damage indicating heavy use or deferred maintenance', embed_text 'Wall scuffs, marks, dents, or localized staining ... smudges, dents, dirty areas, or minor staining', support_any containing 'stain' and 'stained' - while the only surface Terra sees, the atomic_claim, is the narrow 'scuffs, marks, or minor dents from use'. The item's own deny_any (['mold$','mildew','water stain']) proves the catalog author already intended water staining to be out of scope, but the guardrail is lexical and every paraphrase in this cluster ('heavy staining', 'stained or discolored', 'discoloration') passed straight through it. So the catalog does help 2d read the scuffs item as the stain item. What the catalog does NOT own: the selection itself. On all 13 issues belonging to the 10 lead-supported units, peeling_or_discolored_paint sat inside the frozen top-8 (rank 1 once, rank 2 ten times, rank 5 once, rank 6 once) with kind_ok and scene_ok true, and 2d took wall_scuffs_marks_or_dents anyway; on two of those issues it took wall_scuffs from a LOWER rank than the better wall/paint item (redfin_125970550 issue b03567bd7ca1e07b, wall_scuffs rank 2 over peeling rank 1; redfin_166147710 issue 8ce15be3647f21b6, wall_scuffs rank 3 over bathroom_paint_peeling_or_worn rank 1 and bath_fixtures_stained_or_worn rank 2). That lower-rank preference is a frozen structural fact that does not depend on any lead verdict being correct, which is why pass_2d_selection is the primary cause. Under the 2026-09-03 scope direction that is a pass_2d_follow_ups entry and explicitly not a licence to broaden the catalog. The smallest catalog lever that would ever be worth trying is therefore NOT the atomic_claim but the 2d-facing description override on wall_scuffs_marks_or_dents (remove 'stains ... or minor damage'): because embed_text is non-empty it is the entire embedding input, so name and description do not move rankings, meaning a description edit changes only what the 2d selection prompt reads and leaves Terra's claim and all retrieval ranks untouched. It stays deferred because the human evidence points the other way: 6 of the 7 reviewed controls are positive uses of wall_scuffs_marks_or_dents, all human truth claim=exact/work=warranted, and two of them are exactly the stain/patch language such an edit would remove (rc_9e57092c89dd, a required control, 'tan-brown streaky stains and marks down to the baseboard'; rc_a2c0f92f2c30, 'grey smudges, dark streaks, white smears and patched areas'). Humans have therefore endorsed billing stain-like wall marks under this item at the low end, and the single gold/human unit in the cluster refutes the claim outright by showing the item used correctly when only minor marks exist.

evidence_bar_claim.justification: Recounted by hand from the 14 unit adjudications and it matches index.json (bar none, human 0, lead 10, props 0, refutations 1, mixed_signal false). Counted units are role=support with adjudication exactly supports_claim: there are 10, and every one of them has evidence_class model_judge (the factorized verifier lead). Human/gold counted units = 0, so distinct properties among counted human units = 0 and there is no ladder rung to climb: not two_independent_human, not one_human_plus_independent_corroboration, and structural_exception is not claimed (it would require at least one counted human/gold unit, which does not exist, and would in any case be the wrong instrument here). The cluster's only human/gold unit is gold:redfin_10806500:photo_005.jpg:g4, adjudicated REFUTED with photos available, which makes reviewed_refutations = 1 and makes the cluster refutation-backed - so no_change would also have been legal. I chose deferred_insufficient_evidence over that fallback because the underlying pattern is live and specific rather than closed: the 2d preference for wall_scuffs_marks_or_dents is visible in the frozen ranks independently of the lead verdicts, and a documented deferral with a concrete promotion recipe preserves it, whereas no_change would assert the question is settled on evidence that never tested it. The remaining 3 units are lead refuted (2) and lead unclear (1); refuted and unclear are facts and are never re-read as support. Per the brief a lead never satisfies the bar and never grounds a non-deferred outcome, so no proposal, no coverage-gap declaration and no non-catalog action can rest on these 10 supports.

proposal.gap_description: No coverage gap is declared. proposal.package_route_effects: None - nothing is changed. cases.attribution_rationale: Premise confirmed by direct inspection: in photo_002.jpg the right-hand sink/peninsula base cabinet run is visibly damaged -- deep black gouges and scuff scoring across the door fronts, finish worn through along edges and stiles, a chipped/chewed counter-edge, and a dark void beneath the countertop next to the sink where a drawer front or panel appears missing or detached. That is broken cabinet componentry, matching the v1.1 adjudication (claim exact, work warranted). The 2a prose DID contain the condition: it states outright that doors/drawers appear misaligned or damaged in places and that the sink-base area looks tired with possible moisture wear, so pass_2a is not at fault. What 2a did NOT do is hedge it away -- "damaged" is stated as an observation, not merely as a modernization or inspect-later note (the water-risk bullet is separate and speculative). Downstream the ladder is intact at every rung: 2b emitted bullet index 8 "Some cabinet doors and drawers appear damaged." with an exact join; 2c kept it (p2c_present true, and it is not in p2c_dropped); 2d resolved it correctly to cabinets_damaged_or_water_stained with kind defect via exact_kind routing -- the right item, so no 2d misresolution; 2e kept it (issue 7fe424e090329645 is in kept_issue_ids, removed_count 0); and condition projection produced oc1_b7dbbbb05b827f66, so projection did not lose it either. The condition therefore reached Terra whole and correctly labelled. Terra returned verdict "unsupported" with the rationale that the cabinet doors and drawers appear intact with no clear broken components or water staining visible -- a statement the photo contradicts -- and that verdict drove disposition "excluded" with reason_code verdict_unsupported and accepted=false. Terra is thus the first and only stage that went wrong. The known post-Terra routing/disposition gap does not apply here, because the exclusion was caused by Terra's own negative verdict rather than by a supported condition being dropped after Terra.

coverage_gap.rationale: Coverage is complete and was exercised. The legacy item outdated_or_damaged_cabinets was split into three successors that partition the kitchen-cabinet space by mechanism: cabinets_damaged_or_water_stained (defect: broken components or water staining), cabinets_worn_finish (degradation: worn or faded finish on intact cabinets), cabinets_dated_style (modernization: dated style or basic grade, functional). A fourth neighbour, missing_base_cabinets_exposed_subfloor, covers absent base cabinetry. On both units the correct successor for the observed mechanism existed, was scene-eligible for kitchen, and ranked 1 in the frozen candidate list (cabinets_damaged_or_water_stained rank 1 on the damage bullet; cabinets_worn_finish rank 1/1/2 on the three wear bullets). Nothing was lost for want of an item.

diagnosis.catalog_ownership_argument: The catalog does not own this cluster, and the evidence says so at every surface the catalog controls. (1) Terra is shown only the atomic_claim. Here that claim is {subject: 'cabinets', state: 'broken components or water staining', ontology_basis: asserted_failure}. In photo_002.jpg of redfin_125779232 an entire drawer front is missing beside the sink, leaving an open cavity into the cabinet box, with black gouges and worn-through finish on the neighbouring door fronts. A missing/detached drawer front IS a broken cabinet component, so the atomic_claim was satisfied on its own terms and Terra's rationale ('The cabinet doors and drawers shown appear intact, with no clear broken components or water staining visible') is contradicted by the image. No rewording of a claim that already covers the facts would have changed the verdict; the failure is the verification of a satisfied claim. The frozen attribution agrees independently: stage terra, attribution downstream, confidence high, with an explicit rung-by-rung check that 2a, 2b, 2c, 2d, 2e and projection all carried the condition intact. (2) The 2d-facing surfaces also behaved: name 'Damaged or Water-Stained Cabinets', description 'Cabinets with broken or damaged doors/drawers, water staining, or swollen panels', support_any ['cabinet','drawer','damaged','water stain','broken','swollen'] pulled the bullet 'Some cabinet doors and drawers appear damaged.' to rank 1 by support_phrase_hit with routing_reason exact_kind. diagnosis.catalog_ownership_argument: The catalog is not the thing that failed, and this cluster is the clean case for saying so. (1) The item's claim surface is precise: atomic_claim subject 'wallpaper', state 'dated or visually busy wallpaper', ontology_basis dated_style. It commits to an object, and that object commitment is exactly what the photo refutes - which is the item behaving correctly, not incoherently. (2) The item's two runtime surfaces agree: divergence_scan reports dated_wallpaper_present with promised_not_claimed [] and claimed_not_promised [], i.e. zero divergence between the retrieval text (name/description/embed_text/support_any, all of which say wallpaper and only wallpaper) and the atomic_claim Terra sees. This is the opposite of the CAP-014 / CAP-016 pattern in this family, where retrieval promises more than the claim tests. (3) The space is already partitioned three ways by subject and scene (dated_wallpaper_present / dated_bathroom_wallpaper / vintage_tile_pattern_style / outdated_bathroom_finishes), so there is no ambiguity for the ontology to resolve. (4) The false material word 'wallpaper' is not in the observation and not in Terra's rationale - it is introduced solely by the act of selecting this item. The only catalog-shaped lever available would be to widen the subject from 'wallpaper' to 'wallcovering', and that would be strictly harmful: it would manufacture overlap with dated_wood_paneling, vintage_tile_pattern_style and outdated_bathroom_finishes, and it would convert this very hallucination into a supported billing. So no false material claim reaches this chain from 2a. Filing this as out_of_scope_pass_2a would attribute the error to a sentence that is not in the case.

The claim is already at the right specificity and already names the object it means. cases.attribution_rationale:
Premise confirmed on my own reading of both photos. Photo_008 (entry close-up) shows a mismatched patched vertical strip of brick along the left door jamb with smeared, off-tone mortar, whitish staining/efflorescence on the brick faces, and a darker parged base treatment contrasting with the brick above; photo_001 (street view of #3227) shows tonal mottling across the brick field, soiling under the projecting sills and cornice, and a whitish repainted band at the first-floor base. Weathering/discoloration is modest but real, matching the adjudicated v1.1 axes (claim exact, work warranted) and the billed claim text "brickwork weathering or discoloration with intact mortar".

The 2a prose did NOT omit this. Photo_001's prose contains the condition explicitly ("Brick and masonry need close inspection: There appear to be areas of aging/discoloration and possibly prior patching"), and photo_008's prose contains it twice over ("mortar joints look weathered/uneven in places" and "the darker foundation/parged area contrasts with the brick and appears patched"). What the prose did NOT contain is any hedge that would license a later stage to distort it — no claim of a uniform facade, no assertion the brick was sound. So pass_2a is ruled out: the condition survives in both readings.

Walking the rest of the ladder, no earlier rung fails. 2b produced matching bullets on both photos ("Brick masonry shows aging and discoloration." idx 5; "The lower masonry base treatment is darker than the brick and appears patched." idx 6), both joined by exact method. 2c kept both — they appear in p2c_surviving, not p2c_dropped. 2d resolved both to brick_weathered_or_discolored via exact_kind routing, and that is the same item the human graded "exact", so the resolution is not wrong. 2e kept both issues (both issue_ids are in kept_issue_ids), and per the corpus rule 2e is not an available attribution regardless. Condition projection succeeded: both issues carry projected_condition_id oc1_261de865e0dd299d, so the condition existed and reached Terra.

Terra is therefore the first stage that went wrong. It returned verdict "unsupported" with the rationale "The visible brick facade appears generally uniform, with mortar joints intact and no clear weathering or discoloration," which drove disposition "excluded" and reason_code "verdict_unsupported". That rationale contradicts what the photos show, and it also misuses the claim's own wording: "with intact mortar" is part of the catalog claim's definition, not a fact that argues against it, so Terra cited a satisfied condition as grounds for rejection. This is not the post-Terra routing gap — Terra did not support the condition and then lose it downstream; Terra affirmatively rejected it, which is a rung the ladder covers.

cases.attribution_rationale:
Premise confirmed by direct inspection: masonry weathering/discoloration is plainly real across this property, and it is not only stone. photo_023 shows a genuine BRICK Tudor house whose tall brick chimney stack carries heavy dark vertical staining, plus a brick retaining wall and a stained/parged wall below the porch; photo_014 and photo_034 show a sandstone facade and chimney with dark staining, biological growth and worn joints; photo_035 shows discolored/moss-stained stone with patched mortar; photo_002/photo_022 show a heavily moss-stained, spalled masonry grill. The condition "brickwork weathering or discoloration" is supported, and the human adjudication (claim=exact, work=warranted) is the authority here.

The 2a prose is not the failure point: it contains the condition explicitly on four of the six photos — photo_014 "Heavy staining/weathering and potentially deteriorated mortar joints", photo_023 "The tall brick stack shows weathering", photo_034 "the chimney and some wall areas show dark staining, weathering", photo_035 "There appear to be patched/repointed areas, discoloration". What 2a did NOT contain is any claim that the mortar is intact — it repeatedly said the opposite (deteriorated/uneven mortar joints, repointing needed) — but that is a detail of the catalog item's claim wording, not an absence of the condition.

Every later stage carried it forward intact: all seven issues joined to a 2b bullet by exact match, all seven survived 2c (p2c_present true), 2d resolved each to brick_weathered_or_discolored via exact_kind, all were kept by 2e, and all seven projected to the single condition oc1_fd62a1d71743be6b, which reached Terra. Terra is the first and only stage that went wrong: it returned "unsupported" on a condition whose substance it conceded — "The visible masonry is heavily stained and weathered, but it is stone rather than brick and some joints appear deteriorated" — rejecting on the catalog item's material/mortar wording rather than on whether the weathering exists.
