So the right home exists, with the wrong claim, and the second-best home is kind-gated.
alternative_stage_analysis.retrieved_but_2d_selected_other: No, and emphatically so. 2d chose the masonry item on all seven issues, three times against a higher-ranked candidate (rank-1 exterior_siding_discoloration_fading on the two stone observations; rank-1 exterior_door_paint_failure on the parged-wall observation at photo_023). There is no materially more exact reachable item that was passed over, so there is nothing here for pass_2d_follow_ups. This is the opposite of CAP-019, where a rank-2 kind-compatible and scene-compatible item was passed over for a rank-5 one.
alternative_stage_analysis.scene_or_retrieval_metadata_cause: No. Scene is exterior on every issue; scene_ok is true for brick_weathered_or_discolored, mortar_joints_deteriorated, exterior_door_paint_failure, damaged_or_rotted_siding_or_trim and dated_exterior_finishes throughout. Retrieval delivered the masonry item at rank 1 on four issues, rank 2 on two, and rank 6 on the parged-wall issue. One documented-not-actioned observation: exterior_siding_discoloration_fading's embed_text promises 'Lower wall staining near grade, darkened exterior siding near foundation', which is why it took rank 1 on both explicit stone-wall observations - a retrieval surface reaching into masonry territory. Editing embed_text is unverifiable offline (it is the entire embedding input when set), so this is a documentation item, not a lever.
alternative_stage_analysis.steals_neighbors_or_damages_successes: Yes, demonstrably, and this is the second blocker. The candidate widening (subject 'brickwork' -> brick or stone masonry) would flip the required correct-rejection control rc_dff4c3209df1 (redfin_10740044, photo_001 and photo_009, human v1 truth terra_claim_unsupported, reviewer adjudication refuted, i.e. the reviewer AGREED the rejection was right). The reviewer rejected it SOLELY on material: 'The facade is rusticated stone block, not brick; dark staining and grime on the stone near the basement window and along the foundation base are visible, but the item's material commitment (brickwork) is not what is there.' Remove the material commitment and the remaining facts - visible staining and grime on stone - satisfy the widened claim. I opened photo_001 to see how bad that flip would be: the facade is clean, light buff rusticated limestone with continuous joints and only mild soiling under the sill and near grade. It is a different severity class from redfin_80925528's dark-streaked, moss-grown, spalled sandstone. So the flip would be a genuinely bad one: it would bill a facade that is not visibly weathered, which is exactly what convention 3 and the gold ruling on gold:redfin_10806500:photo_001.jpg:g1 (weathering not established, not billable) forbid. Any future widening must therefore carry a visible-weathering threshold, not just a wider material, and must demonstrate rc_dff4c3209df1 still rejects under it. Relaxing the intact-mortar qualifier would separately steal from mortar_joints_deteriorated, whose whole reason for existing is that boundary. The one thing at no risk is rc_35a00646adaf (positive_use on genuine yellow brick with intact mortar): widening a subject never removes brick, so it stays supported.
alternative_stage_analysis.terra_adjudicated_wrong_detail: No on the support unit, yes on the refuted one, and the pair is diagnostic. On rc_5063066c1a57 Terra's rationale ('heavily stained and weathered, but it is stone rather than brick and some joints appear deteriorated') is confirmed by the reviewer and by my own reading of photo_014, so Terra applied a mis-scoped claim correctly. On rc_5b3b3cb9e726 Terra's rationale ('generally uniform, with mortar joints intact and no clear weathering or discoloration') IS contradicted by the image per the reviewer, and it also cites the claim's own definitional qualifier ('with intact mortar') as a ground for rejection - that unit is a Terra error and the reviewer refuted the cluster claim on it accordingly. Both facts are recorded; only the first bears on the catalog.
alternative_stage_analysis.upstream_kind_wrong: No. 2c assigned degradation to observations about staining, weathering and discoloration, which is correct, and all seven issues routed with routing_reason exact_kind. The one consequence worth naming is not an error: because the observation kind is degradation, the defect-kind sibling mortar_joints_deteriorated is gated out (reachability scan: rank null and kind_ok false on all seven issues), so the part of Terra's objection that concerns deteriorated joints had no reachable item at all. That gate is the split boundary behaving as designed.
alternative_stage_analysis.wording_creates_unsupported_commitments: Yes - this is the whole finding, and there are two commitments, not one. (a) MATERIAL: the atomic_claim subject is 'brickwork' while the item's name, trade, description-adjacent embed ('Clean or seal masonry') and role as the catalog's sole masonry-degradation concept all point at masonry generally. divergence_scan records promised_not_claimed = ['masonry'] for exactly this. (b) QUALIFIER: the claim's state is 'weathering or discoloration with intact mortar'. On this property several photos show mortar that is not intact (worn joints on the sandstone bungalow; visibly patched/repointed mortar at the photo_035 stone entry), so the qualifier fails independently of the material. Terra cited both. Any repair of this claim has to decide what to do about the qualifier, and the qualifier is the split boundary against mortar_joints_deteriorated - which is why the smallest lever is not obviously sufficient and the next lever up is not obviously safe.

cluster.claim_under_test: The photo shows heavily stained, moss-covered or worn-jointed masonry that is STONE rather than brick, billed under brick_weathered_or_discolored, whose atomic_claim commits to 'brickwork ... with intact mortar'.
cluster.merge_split_rationale: SPLIT OUT of the provisional CAP-002, which pooled three physical subjects (painted siding, exterior trim/casing, and masonry) under one abstract 'exterior envelope' claim. CAP-002's recomputed two_independent_human bar was carried by exactly two units that share only the scene: this masonry material mismatch and an exterior door casing routed to a siding item. Convention 2 forbids letting a differently named subject on another constituent condition rescue the claim, so those two cannot ground one another and the split deliberately COSTS the bar. That is the point of the split, not a side effect: the bar was an artifact of pooling. CAP-018 keeps exactly the masonry question. Subject (masonry vs siding/trim), trade (masonry_exterior_structure vs exterior_siding_trim), commitment type under test (material and the intact-mortar qualifier vs a fading/chalking mechanism) and the candidate lever (the brick_weathering_or_mortar_deterioration split entry vs an exterior_door_paint_failure claim widening) all differ from CAP-019's. The refuted brick unit rc_5b3b3cb9e726 moves in with them rather than staying in a siding cluster because it is the in-cluster demonstration that this exact item works when the material really IS brick - it belongs beside the widening question it constrains. Within the surviving support unit, all seven issues across six photos are kept as ONE evidence unit per convention 2 (they are one projected condition, oc1_fd62a1d71743be6b, which Terra verified once); the true branch (the genuine brick chimney in photo_023) does not rescue the five stone issues, so the reviewer's supports_claim adjudication stands as recorded.
cluster.physical_subject: exterior masonry other than siding or trim: stone facades and stone chimneys, a stone barbecue grill, a parged/painted masonry porch wall, and one genuine brick chimney

reshape.rationale: Strictly narrower than CAP-002's claim. CAP-002 asked whether exterior siding, trim OR masonry was billed under a claim naming a mechanism (fading/chalking; rot/warping/cracks) or a material (brick) that is not visible. CAP-018 keeps only the masonry arm and only the material/qualifier commitment: stone (or parged) masonry billed under brick_weathered_or_discolored's 'brickwork ... with intact mortar'. Both units carry their original CAP-002 packet rows and their reviewer text is quoted verbatim in transfer_note. No adjudication is changed, no unit is duplicated, and CAP-002's remaining unit plus CAP-019's two units account for the other three of the five provisional units.

cluster.visible_state_or_mechanism: heavy dark staining, biological growth and moss, spalling, and visibly worn or patched/repointed joints on masonry whose material is mostly stone rather than brick

controls.exclusion_rationale: CAP-018 reads its controls from CAP-002 and keeps exactly the two that sit on the implicated item brick_weathered_or_discolored: rc_35a00646adaf (positive_use, required, adjudicated supports_claim) and rc_dff4c3209df1 (correct_rejection, required, adjudicated refuted). The three excluded cards test other items and follow those items to their clusters - rc_0b6ca8cfa337 (positive_use on exterior_siding_discoloration_fading) and rc_91bb03de4429 (correct_rejection on damaged_or_rotted_siding_or_trim, and directly on door jamb casing) are relevant to CAP-019, and rc_2990cdf4339b (positive_use on damaged_or_rotted_siding_or_trim) stays with CAP-002. No control on brick_weathered_or_discolored is dropped. MANDATORY DISCLOSURE OF COUPLING: the retained correct_rejection rc_dff4c3209df1 sits on redfin_10740044 photo_001 (and photo_009) - the SAME property and the SAME photo as CAP-019's counted support unit rc_7b23faa0bd8f. CAP-018 and CAP-019 are therefore not evidentially independent of one another on that property, and any future joint promotion of the two must say so rather than counting them as two properties' worth of evidence.

coverage_gap.rationale: I searched all 128 items in digest/items.json for stone, masonry, brick, mortar, chimney, stucco and foundation tokens. The masonry_exterior_structure trade holds exactly four items: brick_weathered_or_discolored (degradation), mortar_joints_deteriorated (defect) and the two inground pool items. Outside it, 'stone' appears only in paving_cracked_or_settled, paving_heaved_or_trip_hazard (hardscape) and dated_fireplace_surround (interior). There is no stone-masonry item, and no stone-facade concept anywhere in the catalog. Nevertheless I do NOT declare this a coverage gap, for two reasons and I want the lead to see the reasoning rather than the label. First, the catalog already claims this space on the surfaces it uses for retrieval and organisation: brick_weathered_or_discolored sits in trade masonry_exterior_structure, its embed_text closes with 'Clean or seal masonry', and it is the ONLY non-pool masonry-degradation concept in the catalog, i.e. the catalog's sole home for weathered masonry. What is narrow is one surface - the atomic_claim's subject, 'brickwork'. Under convention 1 that is a wording/specificity defect on the Terra-facing surface, not an absent concept, and calling it missing coverage would overstate the finding and reach for a bigger lever than the evidence supports. Second, the declaration would buy nothing and cost something: a declared coverage gap on a non-deferred outcome requires a met bar, this cluster's bar is none, and if a genuinely new stone item were ever wanted the legitimate split parent already exists (brick_weathering_or_mortar_deterioration, change_type split, two successors), so nothing is foreclosed by declining to declare it now. The competing reading - that stone masonry is simply uncovered - is recorded in rejected_alternative_owners and in unresolved_questions, and is a live question for whoever promotes this cluster.

diagnosis.catalog_ownership_argument: The defect is real, it is catalog-owned, and it lives on exactly one surface. Convention 1 makes the two surfaces the thing to test. (1) TERRA-FACING SURFACE. Terra sees only the atomic_claim, which is {subject: 'brickwork', state: 'weathering or discoloration with intact mortar', ontology_basis: visible_deterioration}. Terra's verdict on rc_5063066c1a57 is 'unsupported' with the rationale 'The visible masonry is heavily stained and weathered, but it is stone rather than brick and some joints appear deteriorated.' That rationale concedes the substance of the condition and rejects on the two commitments the claim adds: the material, and the intact-mortar qualifier. Terra applied the claim it was given, faithfully and accurately - the reviewer's own reading agrees that most of the masonry is stone and that several photos show mortar that is not intact. This is the signature of a claim that is mis-scoped, not of a verifier that failed. (2) RETRIEVAL/2d-FACING SURFACE. Everything the catalog shows 2d points the other way: trade_bucket masonry_exterior_structure, name 'Weathered or Discolored Brick', description 'Brickwork with weathering, staining, or discoloration; mortar intact', and an embed_text that ends 'Clean or seal masonry.' The divergence scan records exactly this as promised_not_claimed = ['masonry']. So the item advertises masonry cleaning and sealing to the stage that selects it, then binds the verifier to brickwork. Retrieval and 2d behaved accordingly: brick_weathered_or_discolored ranked 1 on four of the seven issues and 2 on two more, and on three issues 2d actively chose it over a higher-ranked non-masonry candidate (over exterior_siding_discoloration_fading at rank 1 on both explicit stone observations, and over exterior_door_paint_failure at rank 1 on the parged-wall observation). 2d moved toward the better subject every time. It had nowhere better to go, because this item is the catalog's only masonry-degradation concept. (3) SCALE OF THE MISFIT, refined. The prior hypothesis said five stone issues plus one genuine brick chimney. Counting the seven issues by photo, it is five stone (photo_002 grill, photo_014 chimney, photo_022 grill, photo_034 chimney and stone walls, photo_035 stone facade), ONE genuine brick (photo_023, 'The tall brick chimney shows weathering'), and one PARGED/painted masonry wall below the porch (photo_023, 'Exposed painted or parged masonry below the porch is stained and uneven'), whose substrate is concealed by the coating and is therefore neither brick nor stone on the face of it. That third material matters: a brick-or-stone widening would still not name it. (4) WHY THE SMALLEST LEVER IS UNDER-DETERMINED. Terra gave two grounds. A subject widening to brick-or-stone answers only the first. The second ground - 'some joints appear deteriorated' - is a failure of the claim's own 'with intact mortar' qualifier, and relaxing that qualifier collides head-on with the split that created these two successors, whose stated atomicity_rationale is that the parent 'conflated failing mortar joints ... with brick weathering/discoloration'. The sibling that names deteriorated joints, mortar_joints_deteriorated, was structurally unreachable here: rank null on all seven candidate lists and kind-gated (kind defect against a degradation observation, kind_ok false in the reachability scan). So on this unit the material widening alone might not even recover the case it was designed to recover, and the fuller fix would blur a deliberate boundary. That is a second, independent reason this cluster is not ready to author an op, over and above the bar.

rejected_alternative_owners.why: The honest competing reading, and the closest call in this judgment. It is TRUE that no stone-masonry item exists in the 128 and that nothing names a stone facade. I rejected it as the primary owner because the catalog's own organisation already puts this condition inside brick_weathered_or_discolored - masonry trade, 'Clean or seal masonry' embed, sole masonry-degradation concept - so the concept is present and one surface is narrow, which is a wording defect under convention 1. Preferring the wording reading also picks the smaller lever: widening a claim on an existing split successor rather than authoring a new successor. Recorded as a live alternative for the promoter, and note that if it is ever taken the legitimate split parent (brick_weathering_or_mortar_deterioration) is available, so the path is not blocked.

2d did not fail; it over-performed. On five of seven issues it took the rank-1 or rank-2 masonry item, and on three issues it passed OVER a higher-ranked candidate to reach the masonry item (exterior_siding_discoloration_fading at rank 1 on both stone-wall observations, exterior_door_paint_failure at rank 1 on the parged-wall observation). There is no materially more exact reachable item it declined: the only other masonry item is kind-gated. pass_2d_follow_ups is therefore empty for this cluster, and the scope direction's warning against compensating for a 2d failure by broadening the catalog does not bite here.

Terra was accurate about the photos and faithful to the claim: it conceded the weathering, then rejected on material and on deteriorated joints, both of which the reviewer independently confirms are what the images show. Contrast the unit that stayed in CAP-002 and the sibling brick unit rc_5b3b3cb9e726 in this cluster, where Terra's rationale ('generally uniform ... no clear weathering') is contradicted by the image - that IS a Terra error, and it is the reason rc_5b3b3cb9e726 is adjudicated refuted. Two different Terra behaviours on one item; only the second is a verifier fault, and it is not the one this cluster is about.

Pass 2a stated the conditions accurately and named the materials correctly - 'The stone facade has discoloration', 'The chimney and some stone wall areas have dark staining and weathering', 'The tall brick chimney shows weathering'. The frozen attribution rationale confirms 2a carried the condition on four of six photos explicitly. 2a is frozen and, on this cluster, also right; the word 'stone' survives all the way to 2d and is lost only when the claim is applied.

Not the owner. Scene is exterior, scene_ok is true for every hypothesised item on every issue, and the resolved item was in the frozen top-2 on six of seven issues. One retrieval-surface oddity is worth documenting, not acting on: exterior_siding_discoloration_fading outranked the masonry item on both explicit stone observations because its embed_text promises 'Lower wall staining near grade, darkened exterior siding near foundation', which pulls generic near-grade staining toward a siding item. That is an overlapping-ontology observation shared with CAP-019, and the lead may prefer to record it once at family level.

2c gave kind degradation, which is right for staining/weathering, and every issue routed exact_kind. The gate that kind creates - defect-kind mortar_joints_deteriorated unreachable from a degradation observation - is the split working as designed and is correct on its own terms. It is nevertheless the mechanism by which the deteriorated-joints half of this property's masonry condition has no reachable home, which is why it appears in contributing causes as an ontology observation rather than as a kind error.

Nothing downstream ran. All seven issues projected into one condition, which reached Terra; the loss is accepted=false / reason_code verdict_unsupported / disposition excluded, i.e. Terra's own negative verdict, not the known post-Terra routing gap. For context only, the item bills when supported (billability: bills true, route work, tier work, defaultHidden false).
Not applicable. Trade is masonry_exterior_structure; the electrical product quarantine does not reach this cluster and no route_override is set on the item.

evidence_bar_claim.conflict_note: MIXED SIGNAL IS TRUE and this is the substance of the cluster, not a bookkeeping note. Among the support units one human unit supports the claim (rc_5063066c1a57: the billed masonry is mostly stone, and the material commitment is not what is visible) and one human unit refutes it (rc_5b3b3cb9e726: the facade is genuine red brick with modest soiling and continuous mortar, so both the material and the mechanism the item names ARE what is visible). The two are not in conflict about the world. They are two different properties with two different materials, and together they say something sharper than either alone: brick_weathered_or_discolored is correct on brick and wrong on stone, which is precisely a subject-scope finding rather than a mechanism finding. The refuted unit is also a warning about Terra rather than about the catalog - there Terra wrongly called a soiled brick facade uniform, and cited the claim's own definitional qualifier ('with intact mortar') as a reason to reject, which no rewording of the subject would fix. The disagreement is compounded by a coupling that must be disclosed: this cluster's retained correct-rejection control rc_dff4c3209df1 sits on redfin_10740044 photo_001, the SAME property and SAME photo as CAP-019's counted support unit rc_7b23faa0bd8f, so CAP-018 and CAP-019 are not evidentially independent on that property. Net effect on this judgment: the supporting side is one property; the constraining side is one human refutation plus one human-endorsed correct rejection that the candidate lever would flip. That balance is why the outcome is a deferral with a recipe, not a proposal.
evidence_bar_claim.justification: Recounted by hand from the adjudications, not copied. Two units, both role support. rc_5063066c1a57 (redfin_80925528) is evidence_class human_review, independent true, adjudicated supports_claim - it counts, and it is the only counted unit. rc_5b3b3cb9e726 (redfin_11077450) is human_review, independent true, but adjudicated refuted - it does not count toward the bar. So counted support = 1, human = 1, leads = 0, gold = 0, distinct properties among counted human units = 1 (redfin_80925528). Ladder: not >=2 human; not 1 human plus independent corroboration, because there is no lead and no gold unit in this cluster to corroborate with; structural_exception is not claimed and would be inappropriate (no structural fact about item ids and fields explains this, and the honest position is that the evidence is thin, not that a structural exception substitutes for it). Therefore bar_met_by = none, which matches the CAP-002 arithmetic once the split is applied. Consequences I have respected: bar none forecloses native_decisions_proposal outright, so ops is empty; a non-deferred outcome would still have been legal, because reviewed_refutations = 1 (rc_5b3b3cb9e726, human, role support, adjudicated refuted, both photos available on disk) and there is also a human supports_claim support unit, so the cluster is refutation-backed and could take no_change, non_catalog_action or migration_system_gap. I chose deferral over no_change deliberately: the finding is real, catalog-owned and has a concrete promotion recipe, and closing it as no_change would discard a live catalog defect rather than park it. no_change remains the correct fallback if the convention-3 billability question below is answered against billability. I also considered and REJECTED promoting a coverage row to reach two_independent_human - see unresolved_questions; it would have been evidence laundering.

human_inputs.effect: Decisive. The 2d-facing surfaces (trade masonry_exterior_structure, embed 'Clean or seal masonry') pulled masonry observations in and 2d selected correctly; the Terra-facing atomic_claim then narrowed the subject to 'brickwork' and rejected them. Same item, one surface failed, and it is the catalog's. This is what makes primary_cause catalog_wording_or_specificity rather than terra_verification or pass_2d_selection.
human_inputs.ref: Convention 1 (brief section 2): strictest claim-bearing wording governs semantic fit; Terra sees only the atomic_claim while name/description/embed_text/support_any are what 2d and retrieval see, and it matters which surface failed.
human_inputs.ruling: Test the two surfaces separately before assigning ownership.

human_inputs.effect: Two effects. (a) rc_5063066c1a57's seven issues across six photos stay ONE unit, so the counted human total is 1, not 7, and the bar is none. (b) The single genuine brick issue (photo_023) does not rescue the five stone issues, so the reviewer's supports_claim adjudication is right on its own terms. The same convention is what forbids CAP-002's two supporting units from grounding one another, which is why this cluster exists and why the split deliberately costs the pooled bar.
human_inputs.ref: Convention 2 (brief section 2): judge disjunctions and multi-photo conditions at the characteristic issue level; a true branch does not rescue a differently named mechanism; never multiply units.
human_inputs.ruling: Several issues on one condition are one evidence unit.

human_inputs.effect: Turns the widening from a clean win into an open question. The control rc_dff4c3209df1 shows visible staining and grime on stone, but on my own reading the stone there is sound and lightly soiled. Under convention 3 that may well not be billable at all, in which case the material widening would import a non-billable presence case. This is the ruling the promotion recipe asks for.
human_inputs.ref: Convention 3 (brief section 2): plain, basic or builder-grade presence is not billable by itself; a condition needs visible datedness, deterioration or incompleteness.
human_inputs.ruling: Presence alone does not bill; visible deterioration must be established.

human_inputs.effect: The nearest precedent for question 1. The reviewer refuted that gold row with 'reads as sound, light-grey concrete with only light surface dirt ... not visibly weathered, spalled or stained'. rc_dff4c3209df1 is the same shape on stone rather than concrete, which is why I forecast flips_to_supported as a HARM rather than as a recovered miss.
human_inputs.ref: Convention 6 / reconciled conflict case: gold:redfin_10806500:photo_001.jpg:g1 - weathering not established, not billable.
human_inputs.ruling: A surface that reads as sound with only light dirt is not a weathering condition.

human_inputs.effect: Confirms this IS a catalog-first candidate (2d behaved, Terra behaved, the claim is narrow) and simultaneously forbids writing it up now. The judgment is a deferral with an executable recipe rather than a proposal at bar none.
human_inputs.ref: 2026-09-03 scope direction (brief section 3): catalog-first; never compensate for a 2d selection failure by broadening the catalog; prefer the smallest lever; a documented deferral with a concrete promotion recipe beats an under-evidenced proposal.
human_inputs.ruling: Only catalog-owned misses and consequential semantic defects are candidates, and under-evidenced proposals are worse than deferrals.

human_inputs.effect: Forecloses the proposal independently of the merits. There is no lead and no gold unit in this cluster to corroborate with, so no corroboration path exists on the frozen evidence; only a new human review can move the bar.
human_inputs.ref: Evidence-bar mechanics (brief section 4) and the validator table: native_decisions_proposal requires a met bar; a lead never satisfies the bar; a met bar needs >=2 human or 1 human plus independent corroboration.
human_inputs.ruling: One human unit on one property cannot ground a catalog change.

proposal.economics_fit: Not applicable - no change. Context: brick_weathered_or_discolored is severity 1, tier work, scope repair, work_item_code MASONRY_REPAIR, package_affinity exterior -> exterior_repair as package_support, pricing_status inherited_from_split_parent, bills true on route work. Cleaning or sealing stone is the same trade and roughly the same work as cleaning or sealing brick, so a subject widening would not strain the pricing; the cost of the widening is billing MORE conditions, not mispricing the ones it bills.
proposal.expected_benefit: None claimed today - that is the honest position at bar none. The benefit of THIS judgment is that it isolates a real, catalog-owned defect from the pooled CAP-002 claim that was hiding it, names the exact surface at fault (the atomic_claim subject on split successor index 1), proves that no other stage owns it, and hands forward a recipe that a future session can execute in four steps. The benefit a future proposal would claim, if the recipe is satisfied: stone and parged masonry weathering, currently the catalog's only home for which is an item that rejects it at Terra on material, would become billable through the concept that already advertises 'Clean or seal masonry'.

A future subject widening would not touch package_affinity, package_role or route_override (none is set, and route_override's only legal value is no_action anyway), so package membership and routing would be unchanged in kind - only the number of exterior_repair support conditions would grow.

regression_controls.note: FORECAST UNDER THE CANDIDATE WIDENING THAT IS NOT BEING PROPOSED. ops is empty, so nothing changes today and this card is in fact untouched. The forecast is the point of the entry: this required correct_rejection on brick_weathered_or_discolored (redfin_10740044, photo_001 and photo_009; human v1 truth terra_claim_unsupported; reviewer adjudication refuted, i.e. the rejection was right) was rejected SOLELY on material - 'The facade is rusticated stone block, not brick; dark staining and grime on the stone ... are visible, but the item's material commitment (brickwork) is not what is there.' Required positive_use on brick_weathered_or_discolored (redfin_126224899 photo_010; Terra supported; human truth exact/warranted; reviewer adjudication supports_claim: 'The yellow brick wall is heavily soiled and darkened across its lower courses beside the door while the mortar joints remain intact'). proposal.regression_risk: The risk of the change NOT made, stated so it is not lost. (1) rc_dff4c3209df1 flips: a required correct rejection the reviewer endorsed, rejected solely on material, would become supported under a bare subject widening - and the photo shows sound, lightly soiled limestone, so the flip would create a billing on a facade that is not visibly weathered. (2) Zero hallucination controls exist on this item, so no proposal here can DEMONSTRATE that a broadening does not make a false observation easier to bill; the safety case would be vacuous. (3) Relaxing the 'with intact mortar' qualifier, which is what Terra's second ground would actually require, blurs the deliberate split against mortar_joints_deteriorated and would let degradation-kind masonry observations absorb joint failures that the defect successor exists to carry. (4) The one thing NOT at risk: rc_35a00646adaf, the brick-on-brick positive use, survives any subject widening untouched.
proposal.retrieval_effects: None, since nothing changes. For the promoter: a claim-only widening would leave retrieval untouched, because embed_text, support_any, deny_any and require_any are unchanged and embed_text is the entire embedding input when set - so ranks would not move anywhere and the change would be verifiable offline. Demoting it to context would have quietly suppressed the strongest evidence against the widening this cluster is about. Case rc_5b3b3cb9e726; human_review; independent true; property redfin_11077450; both photos present on disk.

unresolved_questions: BILLABILITY, and this is the question the promotion turns on. Is staining, grime or biological growth on stone masonry near grade billable at all under convention 3 (plain/basic presence is not billable by itself; a condition needs visible datedness, deterioration or incompleteness)? The reconciled gold ruling on gold:redfin_10806500:photo_001.jpg:g1 says the analogous hardscape case is NOT billable - the reviewer refuted it with 'reads as sound, light-grey concrete with only light surface dirt on the treads; it is not visibly weathered, spalled or stained', i.e. weathering was not established. rc_dff4c3209df1 is the same shape one material over. If Steven rules that ordinary soiling on sound stone is not billable, then the correct outcome for CAP-018 is no_change plus documentation, because the widening would recover the redfin_80925528 case only by also billing the redfin_10740044 case. If he rules that heavy staining, moss and worn joints ARE billable but ordinary soiling is not, then the lever is not a bare subject widening but a subject widening carrying a visible-weathering threshold, and rc_dff4c3209df1 must be shown to still reject under it.

SUFFICIENCY OF THE SMALLEST LEVER. Terra rejected rc_5063066c1a57 on TWO grounds, material and 'some joints appear deteriorated'. Widening the subject to brick-or-stone answers only the first, and the reviewer confirms several photos show mortar that is not intact, so the widened claim might still fail on this very unit. Relaxing the 'with intact mortar' qualifier would answer the second but collides with the split's own atomicity_rationale (the parent 'conflated failing mortar joints ... with brick weathering/discoloration') and would steal from mortar_joints_deteriorated, which is itself unreachable from degradation-kind observations (rank null, kind_ok false on all seven issues). Someone has to decide whether a stone-masonry weathering condition with worn joints belongs to the degradation successor, to the defect successor, or to neither, before an op is written.

PARGED AND PAINTED MASONRY IS A THIRD MATERIAL. Counting the support unit's seven issues by photo gives five stone, one genuine brick (photo_023 chimney) and one parged/painted masonry wall below the porch (photo_023, 'Exposed painted or parged masonry below the porch is stained and uneven'), whose substrate is concealed. A brick-or-stone widening still would not name that one. If the intent is 'the catalog's masonry-weathering concept', the subject should probably read as masonry generally rather than as an enumeration of two materials - which is a slightly larger wording change and needs the same evidence.

A PROMOTION I CONSIDERED AND REJECTED. The nearest thing to a second independent stone unit in the frozen record is the coverage row gold:redfin_11000447:photo_001.jpg:g6 ('Cornice and upper trim show weathering and paint wear', adjudicated supports_claim, covering_item null). I did not promote it, and the lead should know why: nothing there was billed under brick_weathered_or_discolored, the subject is cornice and upper trim rather than a masonry field, and the reviewer's own text says the decisive fact cannot be established - 'how much of that is paint wear versus soiled stone facing cannot be separated'. Promoting it would have manufactured a two_independent_human bar out of a row that does not test this claim. The other stone/masonry coverage rows are equally unusable here (photo_007 g6 is peeling paint on interior basement masonry; photo_008 g8 and g10 are a stone-PATTERN resilient floor).

PROMOTION RECIPE, stated so it can be executed. (1) One further independent human-reviewed unit on a DIFFERENT property where stone or parged masonry weathering was lost at Terra specifically to the brickwork commitment - that takes the bar to two_independent_human on two properties, and the correlation_note would then not be needed. (2) Steven's ruling on question 1 above. (3) A decision on question 2 (the intact-mortar qualifier). (4) A demonstrated expected_after for rc_dff4c3209df1 under the exact proposed wording; if it still says flips_to_supported, the proposal should not be written. Expressibility is already settled and is not part of the recipe: the lead's dry run confirms that setting /successors/1/atomic_claim and /successors/1/name on the brick_weathering_or_mortar_deterioration split entry (index 1 is brick_weathered_or_discolored; index 0 is mortar_joints_deteriorated), together with /atomicity_rationale and /expected_effects/routing, classifies native and runs clean. Expressibility is not warrant.

MY OWN PHOTO READING vs THE REVIEWER: no disagreement to record. I opened two photos and both readings match the frozen verdicts (see photos_opened). Nothing in this judgment changes, or asks to change, any adjudication.

cases.attribution_rationale:
Premise confirmed by my own inspection. Both photos show the same older house clad in white painted wood siding whose finish is plainly tired: in photo_006 (flat overcast light) the paint reads dingy with a gray cast and streaking across the second story below the roofline, soiling on the wall under the porch roof, and a duller, grayer tone on the lower-level wall than the upper; photo_019 (harsh summer sun, more flattering) still shows mottled gray, uneven tone on the shaded elevation and along the lower courses. That matches the adjudicated v1.1 axes (claim exact, work warranted) for the claim "exterior siding finish fading, chalking, or uneven discoloration."

The 2a prose did NOT miss this. photo_006's prose states the painted wood siding "has visible wear, uneven boards/patching, and tired trim details" and calls for "prep, repairs, and repainting at minimum"; photo_019's prose states the painted wood siding, trim and fascia "look weathered in places" and again expects "prep/repair and repainting at minimum." What the 2a prose did not do is use the narrower vocabulary of fading/chalking/discoloration — it described the same finish failure as wear/weathering. That distinction is the only thing that could have pushed the fault earlier to 2d (a wrong-item resolution from "weathered" to "discoloration_fading"), but the human adjudicated the resulting claim text as EXACT, which means the catalog item 2d chose was the right one for what the photos show. So 2d is not the first failure either.

Everything downstream of 2a ran clean: all three issues joined to 2b bullets by exact match (indices 4, 6, 7), all three survived 2c, all three resolved to exterior_siding_discoloration_fading via exact_kind, all three carry p2e_status "kept", and all three projected to condition oc1_b2e96c2b1020d48b, which reached Terra. Terra then returned verdict "unsupported" with the rationale that the visible white siding "does not show clear fading, chalking, or uneven discoloration," and that verdict alone produced reason_code verdict_unsupported and the unbilled outcome. Terra is therefore the first stage that went wrong: it rejected a condition that the pipeline had correctly observed, structured, filtered, resolved and projected, and that the photos support. This is not the known post-Terra routing gap, because Terra did not support the condition and lose it to disposition — Terra itself is the rejecting stage.

cases.attribution_rationale:
Premise confirmed on inspection: photo_001.jpg shows a stone rowhouse front where the white-painted door surround/casing and transom frame are visibly rough and unevenly finished -- paint slopped onto the adjacent stone along the right jamb, patchy/scuffed coverage down the jamb and door bottom, and a dirty streak at the sill. That is a real, visible exterior finish defect, matching the adjudicated truth (claim=exact, work=warranted).

The 2a prose DID contain the condition: it explicitly reports that "the white-painted trim against the stone looks unfinished in spots" and calls for "Cleaner trim detailing, repaired lintel/sill areas." What 2a did NOT contain was any claim of siding fading/chalking (correctly, since the facade is solid stone and there is no siding) -- but the condition itself was captured, so 2a is not the failure. 2b lifted it verbatim as bullet index 6 ("White-painted trim appears unfinished in spots.") with an exact join, so 2b is clean. 2c kept the bullet (it survives in p2c_surviving as issue 299f90fb6266878f), so 2c is clean. 2d resolved it to exterior_siding_discoloration_fading; that mapping is the one point of tension I noticed (a stone house has no siding), but the v1.1 truth basis grades the resulting claim axis as "exact" and the v1 verdict as terra_claim_supported, which validates the claim text as it stood after 2d -- so 2d is not adjudicated as a mis-resolution. 2e kept the issue (299f90fb6266878f is in kept_issue_ids; the 2 suppressions here hit other issues and cost nothing), and projection produced condition oc1_30375086ad2fd9f6, so the condition did reach Terra (this is not the post-Terra routing gap).

Terra is therefore the first stage that went wrong: it returned "unsupported" with the rationale "No exterior siding with fading, chalking, or uneven discoloration is visible in the cited view," which produced accepted=false / reason_code verdict_unsupported / disposition excluded. A correct, human-supported claim reached Terra intact and Terra rejected it -- that rejection, not any earlier stage, is what lost the bill. Confidence is medium rather than high only because the siding-vs-trim vocabulary mismatch from 2d is a plausible competing story; the adjudicated claim axis is what rules it out.

coverage_gap.rationale: Documented as a hypothesis, deliberately NOT declared. The honest finding is that no item in the 128 claims exterior trim/casing paint on the Terra surface: I searched every item for casing / jamb / surround / lintel / sill / 'door frame' / trim and the exterior hits are damaged_or_rotted_siding_or_trim (kind defect, so kind-gated against this degradation observation and absent from the frozen list at rank null), exterior_siding_discoloration_fading (claims 'exterior siding finish'), exterior_door_paint_failure (claims 'exterior door paint'), dated_exterior_finishes (kind modernization, also kind-gated, rank null) and baseboard_wear_scuffs (an interior concept that nonetheless carries scene_group 'exterior' and ranked 3 on this very issue). I also read all 63 gold coverage rows for a casing/surround/exterior-trim finding: the four trim-ish rows (redfin_11000447 photos 002/003/007, redfin_10806500 photo_006) are interior baseboards, window sashes and a bathroom window, so no coverage row promotes into this cluster. Three reasons this stays undeclared. (1) A kind-compatible, scene-compatible item WAS reachable at rank 2 whose description and embed_text already advertise 'trim' and 'door frame'; a reachable near-exact item is a specificity question, not missing coverage. (2) The smallest conceivable lever is a claim widening on that existing item, not a new item - and 'missing coverage' would misdescribe it. (3) The bar recomputes to none, and the validator requires a met bar for a declared coverage gap on a non-deferred outcome; declaring one here would force migration_system_gap or a deferral on evidence that does not support either. There is in any case no legitimate split parent for a new exterior-trim-paint successor: exterior_door_paint_failure's decisions entry is change_type 'reclassified' with a single successor that keeps the parent id, and exterior_siding_discoloration_fading is the same shape.

diagnosis.catalog_ownership_argument: The catalog does not own the loss, and it does own two wording defects that this evidence cannot warrant fixing. Ownership of the loss: for issue 299f90fb6266878f ('White-painted trim appears unfinished in spots.') the frozen candidate list is soffit_or_porch_ceiling_weathered#1, exterior_door_paint_failure#2, baseboard_wear_scuffs#3, shed_exterior_paint_failure#4, exterior_siding_discoloration_fading#5, fence_weathered#6, brick_weathered_or_discolored#7. The reachability scan records exterior_door_paint_failure at rank 2 with kind_ok true and scene_ok true, and 2d (resolution_path 'llm', routing_reason 'exact_kind') selected rank 5 - a siding-field item, on a solid limestone rowhouse with no siding anywhere. Terra then said, correctly, that no siding fading was visible, and the condition was excluded (accepted false, reason_code verdict_unsupported) even though the frozen human truth grades it exact/warranted. The scope direction is explicit that 'right item reachable but another was selected' is a pass_2d_follow_ups entry with the catalog unchanged, and that a 2d selection failure must never be compensated by broadening the catalog. What the catalog does own, and what this outcome records rather than acts on: (a) exterior_siding_discoloration_fading's retrieval surface over-promises - its description opens 'Exterior siding OR TRIM shows fading, chalking, staining, or uneven discoloration' while its atomic_claim binds Terra to subject 'exterior siding finish' (divergence promised_not_claimed = ['trim_casing','wear_scuff']); under convention 1 the surface that failed is the retrieval surface, since that description is what 2d reads and it is a standing invitation to route trim here; (b) exterior_door_paint_failure's atomic_claim under-covers its own retrieval surface - description 'worn, chipped, or peeling around edges, panels, OR TRIM' and embed_text 'Moisture-damaged, swollen, or rotting wood at bottom of exterior door or DOOR FRAME. Deteriorated door sill or threshold.' against an atomic_claim of subject 'exterior door paint' (divergence promised_not_claimed = ['trim_casing','moisture_rot','damage_break']). Both are real, both are catalog-owned, and neither can be acted on at bar none - which is why this is a non_catalog_action that records them, not a proposal.

rejected_alternative_owners.why: Terra behaved correctly. Its rationale, 'No exterior siding with fading, chalking, or uneven discoloration is visible in the cited view', is literally true of a limestone rowhouse and the reviewer says so ('literally true and misses the trim condition'). Terra sees only the atomic_claim; given 'exterior siding finish - fading, chalking, or uneven discoloration' there was no reading available to it that would have reached the casing. The frozen attribution does record stage 'terra' at medium confidence, but its own rationale names the competing story ('the siding-vs-trim vocabulary mismatch from 2d is a plausible competing story') and rules it out on one premise: 'the v1.1 truth basis grades the resulting claim axis as exact ... so 2d is not adjudicated as a mis-resolution.' Steven's convention-6 reconciliation ruling removes exactly that premise - rc_7b23faa0bd8f is the door casing/surround or jamb trim, not siding, and must never be relabelled as siding. Attribution is not an adjudication and is not frozen against reasoning, so naming 2d here changes no fact and contradicts no verdict.

2a captured the condition accurately. The prose reports that 'the white-painted trim against the stone looks unfinished in spots' and asks for 'Cleaner trim detailing, repaired lintel/sill areas'; 2b lifted it verbatim as bullet index 6 with an exact join; 2c kept it (issue 299f90fb6266878f survives); 2e kept it. The reviewer confirms 'The Pass 2a observation ... matches the image.' There is no 2a error to be out of scope for, and no Pass 2a hallucination card exists on either implicated item.

A kind-compatible, scene-compatible item was on the frozen list at rank 2 with a description and embed_text that already name trim and door frame. Calling this missing coverage would let a 2d selection failure be re-described as a catalog hole, which is exactly the substitution the scope direction forbids. The residual truth - that no atomic_claim in the catalog names exterior casing paint - is recorded in coverage_gap as an undeclared hypothesis with a promotion recipe.

Nothing gated the better item. exterior_door_paint_failure carries scene_groups ['exterior','other'], kind degradation matching the case kind, require_any null and deny_any ['shed'] - no guardrail touches a stone rowhouse door surround - and the scan confirms kind_ok true, scene_ok true, rank 2. The retrieval layer delivered the right candidate; selection discarded it.

2c assigned degradation and that is right: the visible state is finish deterioration on intact trim, not an asserted failure. The two items that would have been nearer in subject on the defect side (damaged_or_rotted_siding_or_trim, whose embed even advertises 'door frame rot') and on the modernization side (dated_exterior_finishes) are correctly kind-gated at rank null. Re-kinding to reach them would be a much larger and worse lever than anything considered here.

unresolved_questions: The choice between this non_catalog_action and deferred_insufficient_evidence is the one soft call in the file, and the lead should know exactly what it costs. Both outcomes change no bytes; they differ only in whether the exterior_door_paint_failure claim widening stays formally alive. I close rather than defer because the widening is affirmatively counter-indicated, not merely under-evidenced: the scope direction forbids compensating for a 2d selection failure by broadening the catalog, and rc_91bb03de4429 is a concrete human-endorsed correct rejection ('small paint chips at its base' on a door jamb casing) that the widening would plausibly flip. If Steven reads the widening as still worth keeping open, the alternative is deferred_insufficient_evidence with deferral_reason 'insufficient_evidence' and the promotion recipe in the next question; nothing else in this file changes.

Promotion recipe if the widening is to be revisited. Three things are needed together, and any one of them alone is insufficient. (1) At least one further independent human unit, on a different property, where an exterior door casing or surround finish observation was lost because no atomic_claim named casing - which would take the bar to two_independent_human. (2) A reviewed control family for exterior_door_paint_failure, which today has 1 label and 0 attribution cases; at minimum one reviewed success and one reviewed rejection, so a regression check on that item is not vacuous. (3) A ruling on rc_91bb03de4429: is grime plus small paint chips at the base of an intact door jamb casing billable? Under convention 3 (plain or basic presence is not billable by itself) the answer is plausibly no even after a widening, in which case the control holds and the widening is safe; if the answer is yes, the widening buys one recovered miss at the price of one control the humans called a correct rejection, and it should not be made.

Steven's ruling owed on the general shape: should exterior painted TRIM - casing, surround, jamb, fascia edges, lintel and sill detailing - be a claimable subject at all, and if so on which item? Today three items advertise door frame, casing or trim on their retrieval surfaces and none claims it on the atomic_claim: exterior_door_paint_failure (promised_not_claimed ['trim_casing','moisture_rot','damage_break']), exterior_siding_discoloration_fading (['trim_casing','wear_scuff']) and damaged_or_rotted_siding_or_trim (['door']). That is one overlapping-ontology finding, and the lead may prefer to record it once at family level rather than repeat it in CAP-002 and CAP-019. The three candidate answers are materially different: widen exterior_door_paint_failure's claim (smallest, but risks the casing control), tighten exterior_siding_discoloration_fading's description to stop advertising trim (removes the pull but is a retrieval edit whose rank effects cannot be verified offline), or accept that exterior trim paint is deliberately not a separate concept and fix only the 2d selection.

A 2d-owned question this cluster cannot answer: why did 2d reject rank 1 AND rank 2 and land on rank 5 on both properties? On redfin_10740044 rank 1 was soffit_or_porch_ceiling_weathered (no soffit in the crop) and rank 2 exterior_door_paint_failure; on redfin_166147710 rank 1 WAS exterior_door_paint_failure. A selector that skips its own top candidates to reach a rank-5 siding item on a trim observation looks like a systematic pull toward the broadest exterior finish concept, which would be worth measuring across the corpus rather than inferring from two cases.

Recorded disagreement with a frozen record, changing nothing: the frozen attribution for rc_7b23faa0bd8f is stage 'terra' at medium confidence, and it exonerates 2d on the premise that 'the v1.1 truth basis grades the resulting claim axis as exact'. Steven's convention-6 ruling (the subject is door casing/surround or jamb trim, not siding, do not relabel) is inconsistent with that premise. I treat the adjudication as fact and the attribution as reasoning, and name 2d as primary cause. The lead may wish to flag the v1.1 claim=exact axis on this case as superseded by the reconciliation ruling, since other analyses may still be leaning on it.

cases.attribution_rationale:
Lane premise holds: the shower hardware is small and softly resolved in frame (showerhead at the top of the surround, a plain round escutcheon, a chrome tub spout), so a human could reasonably fail to reach a verdict on whether it is genuinely "dated" versus merely old-looking. But the record still permits clean attribution, because the error is a referent substitution visible independent of that judgment call.

What 2a DID contain: the real observation. The prose lists "old shower trim" explicitly, under the heading "Fixtures appear dated and in poor condition," grouped with the stained toilet, stained vanity and worn tub — i.e. plumbing fixture trim (valve handle, escutcheon, showerhead, spout). What 2a did NOT contain: any observation about interior millwork — no baseboard, casing, crown or "trim package" language anywhere in the prose, and the photo shows no such evidence either (the only millwork in frame is ordinary white door casing at far left, which is not thin or notably builder-grade).

2a is therefore not at fault. 2b is not at fault: the join is exact, "The shower trim is old." 2c is not at fault: the bullet survived (only the layout-clearance and inconsistent-finishes bullets were dropped). The first stage that went wrong is 2d, which resolved this plumbing-fixture observation to catalog item dated_interior_trim, whose claim text is "interior trim plain, thin, or builder-grade trim package" — millwork, a different thing that happens to share the word "trim." The claim Terra was handed was thus about something the photo never showed. Terra is not the first failure: it rejected correctly, and its own rationale names the mismatch ("The visible shower hardware does not clearly show a dated or builder-grade interior trim package"). Condition projection is not at fault either — the issue did become condition oc1_81d91b622cb7287d. The post-Terra routing gap does not apply here because Terra did not support the condition. Note also that p2e_status "absent" on this issue is not evidence against 2e, per the corpus rule.

Net effect: a real dated-fixture condition observed correctly at 2a went unbilled because 2d mapped it onto the wrong catalog item.

Confidence is medium rather than higher for two reasons: the truth basis is a single uncontested v1 verdict of terra_evidence_inconclusive, and the record does not list 2d's 8 candidates. Because routing_reason is "exact_kind" and the bullet's kind is "modernization," I cannot rule out that the catalog offers no modernization-kind item for dated plumbing/shower trim (the sibling degradation bullets on this same photo all landed on bath_fixtures_stained_or_worn). If so this is a catalog-coverage gap expressed through 2d rather than a pure resolution mistake — but 2d remains the first stage where the meaning changed.

absence_statements.correct_rejections: There are ZERO correct-rejection controls in this cluster. outdated_bathroom_finishes has none anywhere in the frozen evidence (see above). The one correct_rejection card in the CAP-006 control set, rc_73d15ca14405 (dated_interior_trim on redfin_11185681, Terra unsupported, v1 truth terra_claim_unsupported, reviewer adjudicated refuted), sits on the item this cluster deliberately does not implicate and is excluded to CAP-008, where it functions as that cluster's kill condition. Because no op is proposed, no regression_controls entries are owed and none are supplied; the mechanical requirement for a regression_controls entry per hallucination and correct-rejection control binds only native_decisions_proposal, and this outcome is non_catalog_action with empty ops. Worth stating plainly: the strongest 'rejection' evidence in this cluster is not a control at all but the case itself - Terra's rejection of dated_interior_trim on this photo was correct, and I confirmed it against the image.
absence_statements.counterexamples: There are ZERO counterexample-role units in this cluster; the single unit is role support. Nor did I find a counterexample I chose not to file: I checked every other CAP-006 unit for a case in which a plumbing-fixture observation resolved correctly (or a millwork observation resolved to a bathroom item, the mirror error) and there is none - the other units are all within-family bathroom_fixtures_tile confusions, which is precisely the reason for the split. The nearest thing to a counterexample is the borrowed control rc_d5cf0019df00, and it points the same way rather than against: on the same image, the sibling degradation bullets resolved to the right bathroom item and billed. So the cross-family substitution documented here is, on the reviewed evidence, a single observed occurrence and not a demonstrated pattern - which is exactly the weight a single pass_2d_follow_ups entry carries, and no more.
absence_statements.success_uses: THIS CLUSTER HAS NO REVIEWED CONTROLS ON ITS IMPLICATED ITEM, and I state that explicitly as required. outdated_bathroom_finishes has ZERO reviewed success uses, zero agreements, zero correct rejections and zero hallucination annotations: I walked the entire frozen artifact (digest/full_artifact.json) for any control card, positive use or attribution case carrying item_id 'outdated_bathroom_finishes' and found none, and the item appears in no cluster's per_item_counts because no cluster in CAP-001..CAP-017 implicated it. Consequently there is no reviewed record anywhere of this item billing correctly, of it being correctly rejected, or of it hallucinating, and no proposal touching it could be checked against a success family - which is an independent reason, on top of the bar, why no op is proposed here. The cluster is not entirely control-free: it borrows one reviewed control from CAP-006, rc_d5cf0019df00, but that card is a positive use of a DIFFERENT item (bath_fixtures_stained_or_worn), so it evidences that item's success, not this one's. Its value here is factual, not regressive: it proves the physical condition on this photo was captured and billed elsewhere. The seven reviewed dated_interior_trim controls that would otherwise be the relevant success family for the item 2d actually chose are excluded to CAP-008 and are not this cluster's to reason from.

alternative_stage_analysis.alters_eligibility_package_economics: Yes, and this is why the mismatch is consequential rather than equivalent, even though no change is proposed. The two items sit on opposite sides of every economic axis: dated_interior_trim is severity 1, tier optional, trade trim_doors_windows, work_item_code TRIM_REPLACE, and package_support for bathroom_modernization; outdated_bathroom_finishes is severity 3, tier work, trade bathroom_fixtures_tile, work_item_code FIXTURES_UPDATE, cost_model room_allowance, and the package_DRIVER for bathroom_modernization. Both bill by tier default (billability.json: route work for both), but a driver and a support are not interchangeable - a lost driver can leave a package unformed. What actually billed on this photo, bath_fixtures_stained_or_worn, is package_support for bathroom_repair, a different package, so this property's bathroom_modernization driver may have gone unformed on this image. I could not verify the property's realised package set from the digest and I record that as an unresolved question rather than a claim; either way, dollar effects are context only under the scope direction and none of this changes the outcome.
alternative_stage_analysis.existing_item_exists: Yes, and it was rank 1. outdated_bathroom_finishes (kind modernization, ontology_basis dated_style, atomic_claim subject 'bathroom finishes' / state 'dated tile, vanity, or fixtures', description 'Older tile, vanity, or fixtures where an update would improve appeal', embed_text explicitly including 'dated faucet or hardware', scene_groups ['bathroom'], trade bathroom_fixtures_tile, severity 3, tier work, scope replace, work_item_code FIXTURES_UPDATE, package_driver for bathroom_modernization) is the exact item for a dated-shower-trim observation and headed the frozen candidate list. A second exact concept, plumbing_fixture_stained_or_corroded (degradation, 'plumbing fixture staining, corrosion, or buildup without leak', trade plumbing, tier work, scope repair, PLUMBING_REPAIR), also exists for the corrosion reading. No item needs to be created and none needs its claim widened.
alternative_stage_analysis.retrieved_but_2d_selected_other: YES - this is the finding. outdated_bathroom_finishes was retrieved at rank 1 with kind_ok true and scene_ok true, and 2d selected dated_interior_trim at rank 3 via the llm path. One pass_2d_follow_ups entry is filed. Under the 2026-09-03 scope direction and Steven's rc_3a19f759f2d9 precedent this is a 2d specificity question, the catalog stays unchanged, and no broadening or guardrail may be introduced to compensate for it.
alternative_stage_analysis.scene_or_retrieval_metadata_cause: Partly, as a contributing factor, and it is worth recording precisely. scene_ok is true for every hypothesised item on this issue, so scene metadata did not gate anything out. What retrieval metadata did do is let an out-of-family item in: dated_interior_trim carries the bare token 'trim' in support_any alongside baseboard/casing/millwork tokens, and lists 'bathroom' among its five scene_groups, so a millwork item is eligible in bathroom scenes on a head-word that in the plumbing trades names valve hardware. That is a genuine ontological ambiguity between two catalog families. It is nevertheless NOT the cause of the loss, because the item it admitted ranked third, below the correct answer, and because the resolution path was llm rather than lexical_shortcut, so the support_any token did not decide the outcome by itself. Recorded as a contributing cause and flagged to the lead for CAP-008 (which owns dated_interior_trim); no edit is proposed from here.
alternative_stage_analysis.steals_neighbors_or_damages_successes: Not applicable in the forward direction, because no op is proposed and nothing changes. Recorded for the counterfactual that was considered and rejected: adding a deny_any guardrail on dated_interior_trim for shower/valve/escutcheon/spout tokens, or dropping 'bathroom' from its scene_groups, would each have blast radius well beyond this unit. deny_any is a hard guardrail evaluated everywhere; dropping the bathroom scene would suppress dated_interior_trim on the three reviewed bathroom-adjacent trim billings in the CAP-008 control family (including rc_d0ffde500a92, a powder-room baseboard the humans approved), i.e. it would damage reviewed successes to fix one selection error. Additionally scene_groups is NOT natively authorable on a reclassified carryover (it would be a migration-system gap), so that lever is unavailable as well as unjustified.
alternative_stage_analysis.terra_adjudicated_wrong_detail: No. Terra returned 'unsupported' on the claim it was given and its rationale ('The visible shower hardware does not clearly show a dated or builder-grade interior trim package') correctly identifies the substitution. I opened photo_005.jpg to test the one reading that would have overturned this - that a genuine builder-grade trim package is visible and Terra simply missed it - and it does not hold: the only millwork in frame is a single door casing at far left with a moulded, stepped profile, i.e. neither plain nor thin, and no baseboard is visible at all. alternative_stage_analysis.upstream_kind_wrong: No. 2c classified 'The shower trim is old.' as modernization, which matches the observation's plain meaning and matches the resolved item's kind (routing_reason exact_kind). The split therefore both isolates a distinct mechanism and removes a double-implication; it costs CAP-006 nothing, because that cluster's two_independent_human bar is carried by redfin_125779232 and redfin_11000447, neither of which moves.

coverage_gap.rationale: Not a coverage gap, and the evidence closes this off three independent ways. (a) The exact concept exists and was reachable: outdated_bathroom_finishes (kind modernization, ontology_basis dated_style, claim 'bathroom finishes dated tile, vanity, or fixtures', scene_groups ['bathroom'], trade bathroom_fixtures_tile, severity 3, tier work, FIXTURES_UPDATE) explicitly names fixtures, was candidate rank 1 on this issue, and the reachability scan records kind_ok true and scene_ok true for it. (b) A second, degradation-side exact concept also exists in the catalog - plumbing_fixture_stained_or_corroded (claim 'plumbing fixture staining, corrosion, or buildup without leak', scene_groups include bathroom, trade plumbing) - and was unavailable on THIS bullet only because the 2c kind was modernization and the item is degradation (kind_ok false). That is a kind gate on one bullet, not an absent concept, and it is the correct gate: 'The shower trim is old' is a datedness observation, and the corrosion aspect of the same hardware was carried by that photo's sibling degradation bullets. (c) Those sibling bullets billed: control rc_d5cf0019df00 is the same photo, resolved to bath_fixtures_stained_or_worn, Terra supported, human truth exact/warranted, reviewer supports_claim, describing 'the spout and escutcheon are tarnished with rust drips beneath'. diagnosis.catalog_ownership_argument: The catalog does NOT own this failure, and the argument is a reachability argument rather than a wording argument. On issue 7569c5ab9b09e455 the frozen candidate list was outdated_bathroom_finishes (1), dated_overall_decor_style (2), dated_interior_trim (3), dated_bathroom_flooring_style (4), dated_electrical_outlets_switches (5), dated_bathroom_vanity_light (6), dated_window_treatment_valance (7), exhaust_fan_dated (8). The item the reviewer says was correct was ranked FIRST, was kind-compatible (modernization/modernization) and scene-compatible (bathroom), and 2d nevertheless selected rank 3 through the llm path (routing_reason exact_kind, resolution_path llm, no lexical shortcut fired). Retrieval did its job; selection did not. The 2026-09-03 scope direction is explicit that this is the 'right item reachable but another was selected' case, which is a pass_2d_follow_ups entry with the catalog left alone, and Steven's reconciled ruling on rc_3a19f759f2d9 (deck weathering: the right concept was reachable, therefore a 2d specificity question, not missing coverage) is the governing precedent for exactly this shape. The contributing ontological fact is real but is not the owner: dated_interior_trim carries the bare token 'trim' in support_any and lists 'bathroom' among its scene_groups, so an item about millwork is eligible in bathroom scenes on a head-word that in the trades also names valve hardware ('shower valve trim'). That cross-family homograph is what put a millwork item into a plumbing candidate list at all. But it only reached rank 3, below the right answer, so it cost nothing on its own - the loss happened at the selection step that had the right answer in front of it. Narrowing that item's retrieval surface would also be a change to CAP-008's item made on this cluster's single unit, which is precisely the 'compensate for a 2d selection failure by editing the catalog' move the brief forbids. Finally, the catalog surface that Terra saw behaved correctly: Terra was handed dated_interior_trim's atomic_claim and rejected it with an accurate rationale ('The visible shower hardware does not clearly show a dated or builder-grade interior trim package'). No catalog field misled any stage.

evidence_bar_claim.correlation_note: Not required at this bar (correlation notes are mandated for a two_independent_human bar on fewer than two distinct properties, and this bar is 'none'), but recorded because the single-property concentration is material to how much weight the cluster can bear. That concentration is fine for what this cluster actually concludes - a single-case 2d selection error, filed as a single follow-up - and would be disqualifying for any generalisation about the catalog, which is a further reason no op is proposed.
evidence_bar_claim.justification: Recounted by hand. The cluster has exactly one unit: runtime:canary:redfin_11079485:20260817_224118_67317092:oc1_81d91b622cb7287d, role support, evidence_class human_review, independent true, adjudication supports_claim, photos status 'available' (photo_005.jpg, exists true). Counted support units = 1; human = 1; leads = 0; distinct properties among counted human units = 1 (redfin_11079485). The ladder needs >=2 human for two_independent_human - not met with one. It needs 1 human PLUS independent corroboration for one_human_plus_independent_corroboration - there is no corroborating unit of any kind in this cluster, model_judge or otherwise, so that rung is not met either. structural_exception is technically available in the sense that the preconditions exist (>=1 counted human unit, and this is not a missing-coverage cluster), but I do NOT claim it and it would be wrong to: the only field divergence I could point at belongs to dated_interior_trim, which is CAP-008's item and is not implicated here, and the failure on this case is not a claim-vs-retrieval divergence at all - the item whose claim Terra tested behaved correctly by rejecting. Manufacturing a structural exception to license an op would be exactly the under-evidenced proposal the brief warns against. Bar is therefore 'none', which matches what the tool must recompute from a single supports_claim human unit. Bar 'none' closes native_decisions_proposal permanently for this cluster, so ops are empty. A non-deferred outcome is nevertheless legal: the cluster is refutation-backed via the SECOND disjunct (>=1 human/gold supports_claim support unit - that is this unit), which admits exactly {no_change, non_catalog_action, migration_system_gap}, and the separate requirement that any non-deferred outcome rest on >=1 reviewed human/gold unit is satisfied by the same reviewed unit with photos available. non_catalog_action is chosen from that set. I did not choose deferred_insufficient_evidence, because the evidence is not thin - it is decisive, and it decides against a catalog change; deferring would leave a 2d follow-up unfiled and would misdescribe a settled question as an open one. I did not choose migration_system_gap, because nothing here is blocked by the authoring surface: the change I decline to make is one I decline on the merits, not one I am unable to express. Hand recount, stated numerically so it can be compared to the tool: counted_support_units 1, human 1, gold 0, leads_counted 0, distinct_properties_among_counted_human 1, reviewed_refutations 0, mixed_signal false, refutation_backed true via the second disjunct.

pass_2d_follow_ups.case_ref: rc_eccd12ababc5 / issue 7569c5ab9b09e455 (redfin_11079485, run 20260817_224118_67317092, photo_005.jpg, 2a/2b observation 'The shower trim is old.', 2c kind modernization, scene bathroom, routing_reason exact_kind, resolution_path llm)
pass_2d_follow_ups.note:
Confusion family, stated in full: cross-trade head-word homograph: 'trim' as plumbing valve trim (escutcheon, handle, tub spout, shower arm; trade plumbing / bathroom_fixtures_tile) versus 'trim' as interior millwork (baseboard, door and window casing, crown; trade trim_doors_windows). The selector took the millwork sense inside a bathroom scene whose candidate list was otherwise entirely bathroom-modernization items.
The selector passed over the rank-1 candidate, which was kind_ok true and scene_ok true, for the rank-3 candidate, on an issue where the rank-1 item's own embed_text names 'dated faucet or hardware'. Terra then correctly rejected the substituted claim and the condition was excluded (reason_code verdict_unsupported), so a real dated-fixtures observation went unbilled. Consequence is not cosmetic: outdated_bathroom_finishes is severity 3, tier work, and the package_DRIVER for bathroom_modernization, whereas dated_interior_trim is severity 1, tier optional and only package_support. Diagnostic value for a 2d prompt or selection fix: the useful signal is the mismatch between the observation's subject trade and the selected item's trade_bucket when a same-kind, same-scene candidate of the observation's own trade is ranked above it. The catalog is deliberately unchanged; do not implement this as a catalog guardrail. Frozen attribution independently agrees (stage 2d, downstream, medium confidence).

proposal.economics_fit: Not applicable: no ops, and economics fields (cost, estimate, work_item_code, cost_model, package_affinity, package_role, estimate_scope) are never natively authorable on any surface in any case. Recorded as context: outdated_bathroom_finishes carries work_item_code FIXTURES_UPDATE with cost_model room_allowance and pricing_status null; dated_interior_trim carries TRIM_REPLACE with cost_model null.
proposal.expected_benefit: No catalog benefit is claimed, because no catalog change is made - and that is the affirmative finding, not an absence of one. The benefit delivered is threefold and entirely non-catalog. (1) A precisely specified pass_2d_follow_ups entry with the diagnostic signal a selection fix could use (observation-trade versus selected-item trade_bucket, with a same-kind same-scene candidate of the observation's own trade ranked above). (2) A documented refusal: two plausible catalog levers on dated_interior_trim are shown to be either forbidden (compensating for a 2d selection failure), damaging to reviewed successes, or not natively authorable, so the next analyst need not re-litigate them. (3) The split itself, which gives CAP-008 sole ownership of dated_interior_trim and leaves CAP-006 a homogeneous within-family cluster, with no worklist item losing an owner.
proposal.package_route_effects: None, because nothing changes. The package facts are nevertheless the reason this mismatch is classified consequential and are recorded here for the 2d follow-up's priority: outdated_bathroom_finishes is package_driver for bathroom_modernization in the bathroom scene; dated_interior_trim is package_support for the same package; bath_fixtures_stained_or_worn, the item that did bill on this photo, is package_support for the different package bathroom_repair. Neither item carries a route_override, and billability.json gives route 'work' for both by work_default, though tier differs (work vs optional). Whether this property's bathroom_modernization package actually went unformed is recorded as an unresolved question.
proposal.product_policy: Not applicable: no ops and no policy trigger. The trades in play are plumbing, bathroom_fixtures_tile and trim_doors_windows; none is the product-quarantined electrical trade, so nothing forces the outcome on policy grounds. No item here carries a min_photo_evidence or route_override concern, so no policy gap is being masked either.
proposal.regression_risk: Zero regression risk by construction: no file changes, no ops, no dry run needed, the guarded catalog artifacts are untouched and every reviewed billing and rejection in the family behaves exactly as it does today. The residual risk is the opposite one and worth naming: leaving the catalog alone leaves the cross-family 'trim' homograph in place, so a future bathroom photo whose plumbing-trim observation is classified modernization can be mis-selected the same way. That risk is accepted deliberately - it is a selection risk owned by 2d, the correct item ranks first when it occurs, and the reviewed evidence shows the condition's degradation reading still bills through bath_fixtures_stained_or_worn. It is carried in the follow-up entry and in the CAP-008 note rather than mitigated by a catalog edit at bar none.
proposal.retrieval_effects: None: nothing is edited, so no embed_text, support_any, deny_any, name or description changes and no item's rank moves anywhere. This is load-bearing rather than incidental. The correct item already ranks first on this issue, so any retrieval edit could only move a ranking that is already right, and embed_text edits in particular cannot be verified offline (embed_text is the entire embedding input when set and there is no offline embedding store). Leaving retrieval untouched also protects the seven reviewed dated_interior_trim billings and rejections in the CAP-008 family, which a 'trim'-token or bathroom-scene narrowing would have disturbed.
proposal.semantic_before_after: Not applicable: no ops, outcome non_catalog_action, so every item keeps its current semantics verbatim and no dry run was run. Recorded so the lead can see exactly what is being left alone. outdated_bathroom_finishes stays kind modernization / ontology_basis dated_style with atomic_claim subject 'bathroom finishes', state 'dated tile, vanity, or fixtures', severity 3, tier work, scope replace, scene_groups ['bathroom']. dated_interior_trim (not implicated here; CAP-008's item) stays kind modernization / ontology_basis low_grade_material with atomic_claim subject 'interior trim', state 'plain, thin, or builder-grade trim package', severity 1, tier optional, scene_groups ['kitchen','bathroom','bedroom','living_areas','utility']. plumbing_fixture_stained_or_corroded stays kind degradation / ontology_basis surface_rust with atomic_claim subject 'plumbing fixture', state 'staining, corrosion, or buildup without leak'.

unresolved_questions: Did this 2d substitution cost redfin_11079485 a bathroom_modernization package? outdated_bathroom_finishes is the package_DRIVER for bathroom_modernization while dated_interior_trim is only package_support for it, and what actually billed on this photo (bath_fixtures_stained_or_worn) is package_support for the different package bathroom_repair. Cross-cluster note for the lead, raised rather than acted on: dated_interior_trim carries the bare token 'trim' in support_any and lists 'bathroom' in its scene_groups, so a trim_doors_windows millwork item is retrievable in bathroom scenes on a head-word that in the plumbing trades names valve hardware ('shower valve trim'). judgment.note: Steven's ruling, carried verbatim in substance: the long concrete entry stair shows algae-like greenish/grey staining on the treads (visible in the photo, especially along the tread noses and the low side wall), but weathering in the catalog sense - spalling, erosion, coating breakdown - is NOT established. judgment.note: The downspout concept is covered by clogged_or_damaged_gutters on the SUBJECT surface (subject 'gutters and downspouts', work_item_code GUTTER_REPAIR, remedy = extend/redirect the discharge) and its description explicitly promises 'dumping water near foundation'. A corrugated extension that is intact, connected and simply terminates at grade beside the basement window is none of those three, so Terra would very likely reject it.
